docs.title: cache_file
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: cache_file = "llm_cache_v2.json"

Description: The default filename for the v2 JSON disk cache. This path stores SHA-256 hashed keys mapping to string responses, ensuring prompts are scoped to the exact provider, model, and thinking budget that generated them.

docs.title: LEGACY_CACHE_FILE
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: LEGACY_CACHE_FILE = "llm_cache.json"

Description: The filename for pre-v2 cache files. Legacy cache files keyed directly on raw prompt text are no longer read by the v2 runtime to prevent prompt leakage and scoping collisions.

docs.title: load_cache()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def load_cache():

Description: Loads and initializes the in-memory cache dictionary singleton _cache from the filesystem (llm_cache_v2.json). If the cache file does not exist, an empty dictionary is assigned. If reading fails due to OS permissions or JSON decode corruption, a warning is emitted via utils.output and an empty cache is returned to allow execution to proceed. Subsequent invocations return the in-memory singleton directly to eliminate disk I/O overhead.

Parameters:

  • None.

Returns:

  • dict: In-memory dictionary containing key-value cache mappings where keys are SHA-256 hashes and values are response strings.

Raises:

  • No exceptions are raised directly; filesystem errors and JSON decoding errors are intercepted and logged.

Example:

cache = load_cache()
if key in cache:
    cached_response = cache[key]
    emit("CACHE_HIT", chars=f"{len(cached_response):,}")
    record_estimate(step, prompt_tokens, cache_hit=True)

The singleton loader is invoked at the start of cache validation cycles. It prevents reparsing large multi-megabyte cache files during high-frequency graph iterations, returning the active reference immediately when _cache is populated.

docs.title: save_cache()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def save_cache(cache):

Description: Persists the in-memory cache dictionary to disk using an atomic file replacement strategy. The cache object is first serialized to a temporary file (llm_cache_v2.json.tmp). Once written and flushed, os.replace atomically swaps the temporary file into the destination path (llm_cache_v2.json). This ensures that process interruptions or unexpected termination will not result in a truncated or corrupted cache file.

Parameters:

  • cache (dict): The full cache dictionary mapping hash strings to response strings.

Returns:

  • None

Raises:

  • No exceptions are raised directly; OSError and TypeError events encountered during writing or renaming are caught and reported via warning logs.

Example:

# Write to a temp file and atomically replace, so an interrupted run never leaves a truncated cache.
tmp_path = f"{cache_file}.tmp"
try:
    with open(tmp_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(cache, f)
    os.replace(tmp_path, cache_file)
except (OSError, TypeError) as e:
    from utils.output import emit, emit_raw

    emit("WARN_CACHE_SAVE_FAIL")
    emit_raw("WARNING", f"Cache save error: {e}", dest="LOG")

The function updates the global _cache reference, then serializes the dictionary to UTF-8 encoded JSON. The use of os.replace guarantees an atomic rename across POSIX and Windows filesystems, protecting pipeline progress against system crashes or forced exits.

docs.title: notice_legacy_cache()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def notice_legacy_cache() -> None:

Description: Inspects the filesystem for the presence of the pre-v2 prompt cache (llm_cache.json). If found, it calculates the file size in megabytes and emits an advisory notification (CACHE_LEGACY_FOUND) prompting the user or cleanup routines to reclaim disk space, as pre-v2 cache entries are intentionally ignored by the current execution engine.

Parameters:

  • None.

Returns:

  • None

Raises:

  • No exceptions are raised; missing file errors (OSError) silently terminate the routine.

Example:

def notice_legacy_cache() -> None:
    """Point out a leftover pre-v2 cache file: it is never read, so it only takes disk space."""
    try:
        size = os.path.getsize(LEGACY_CACHE_FILE)
    except OSError:
        return
    from utils.output import emit

    emit("CACHE_LEGACY_FOUND", file=LEGACY_CACHE_FILE, size=f"{size / 1_048_576:,.1f}", current=cache_file)

The routine provides disk hygiene feedback during startup preflight checks. By querying file metadata via os.path.getsize, it avoids parsing legacy formats while calculating storage reclamation figures.

docs.title: call_llm()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def call_llm(prompt: str, use_cache: bool = True, thinking_level: str | None = None, step: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: The primary orchestration function for submitting prompts to LLMs. It handles configuration lookup, token estimation, cache verification, refusal deduplication, usage accounting, and provider dispatch. Execution follows five distinct operational phases.

docs.title: Phase 1: Setup and Token Estimation
docs.text:
step = step or "other"
provider, model, _, _ = resolve_llm_settings()
prompt_tokens = count_tokens(prompt)  # memoized: the node already counted this prompt

emit_raw("DEBUG", f"{'=' * 80}", dest="LOG")
emit_raw(
    "DEBUG",
    f"LLM CALL START | provider={provider} | model={model} | thinking={thinking_level} | cache={'enabled' if use_cache else 'disabled'} | prompt_tokens={prompt_tokens:,}",
    dest="LOG",
)
emit_raw("DEBUG", f"PROMPT:\n{prompt}", dest="LOG")

The execution step defaults to "other" if unspecified, tying accounting metrics to the pipeline phase. Active provider configurations and target models are resolved via resolve_llm_settings(), followed by memoized prompt token counting through count_tokens(). Detailed debug traces are flushed to disk logs.

docs.title: Phase 2: Cache Evaluation
docs.text:
# Check cache if enabled
key = _cache_key(prompt, provider, model, thinking_level)
if use_cache:
    cache = load_cache()
    if key in cache:
        cached_response = cache[key]
        emit("CACHE_HIT", chars=f"{len(cached_response):,}")
        record_estimate(step, prompt_tokens, cache_hit=True)
        emit("LLM_CALL_CACHED", step=step, estimate=f"{prompt_tokens:,}")
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"RESPONSE (cached):\n{cached_response}", dest="LOG")
        emit_raw("DEBUG", "LLM CALL END | result=cache_hit", dest="LOG")
        return cached_response
    emit("CACHE_MISS")

If caching is enabled, the function computes a scoped SHA-256 digest using _cache_key(). If found in _cache, the response is immediately emitted as a cache hit, prompt token estimates are logged to the billing ledger with cache_hit=True, and the stored response text is returned without making network calls.

docs.title: Phase 3: Refusal Deduplication Check
docs.text:
# A request the provider already declined this run is declined again: do not re-send it on
# node retries (rate limits, billed partial output). The node retry still sees the error.
refusal_key = request_key(provider, model, thinking_level, prompt)
refused = previous_refusal(refusal_key)
if refused is not None:
    emit_raw("DEBUG", "LLM CALL END | result=refused_before (not re-sent)", dest="LOG")
    raise refused

Before dispatching an external network call, the function calculates a refusal key and checks previous_refusal(). If an identical request encountered a non-retryable refusal earlier in the pipeline execution (such as content filtering or policy violations), the recorded exception is re-raised immediately to prevent burning API quota.

docs.title: Phase 4: Provider Dispatch and Ledger Tracking
docs.text:
# Make the actual LLM call
start_time = time.time()
emit_raw("DEBUG", f"API CALL | sending request to {provider}...", dest="LOG")

# Usage of this call = ledger delta for the provider: it includes every billed request the call
# made (Anthropic truncation retry, resend after fallbacks were disabled), even when it raises.
before = usage_snapshot(provider)
returned = False
try:
    with usage_step(step):
        if provider == "GEMINI":
            response_text = _call_llm_gemini(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)
        elif provider == "ANTHROPIC":
            response_text = _call_llm_anthropic(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)
        elif provider == "OPENROUTER":
            response_text = _call_llm_openrouter(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)
        else:  # generic method using a URL that is OpenAI compatible API (Ollama, ...)
            response_text = _call_llm_provider(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)
    returned = True
except LLMRefusalError as e:
    if not e.retryable:
        remember_refusal(refusal_key, e)
    raise
finally:
    call_usage = usage_delta(before, usage_snapshot(provider))
    measured = call_usage["calls"] - call_usage["unmeasured_calls"]
    if measured:
        record_estimate(step, prompt_tokens * measured)
        _emit_call_usage(step, prompt_tokens, call_usage, measured)
    elif returned:  # answered, but the provider reported no usage
        emit("LLM_CALL_USAGE_MISSING", step=step, estimate=f"{prompt_tokens:,}")

The function captures a ledger snapshot before routing the prompt to the provider-specific adapter. Execution is wrapped within the usage_step(step) context manager to ensure token attribution. If the call fails with a non-retryable LLMRefusalError, it is recorded in the refusal ledger. Regardless of success or failure, the finally block computes ledger deltas to account for all billed calls, including provider-level internal retries.

docs.title: Phase 5: Response Finalization and Cache Persistence
docs.text:
elapsed = time.time() - start_time
emit_raw("DEBUG", f"API CALL COMPLETE | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s | response_chars={len(response_text):,}", dest="LOG")
emit_raw("DEBUG", f"RESPONSE:\n{response_text}", dest="LOG")

# Update cache if enabled. Empty and truncated responses (llm_common.TruncatedResponse)
# are never cached — they would be replayed on every later run.
if use_cache and response_text and not getattr(response_text, "truncated", False):
    cache = load_cache()
    cache[key] = response_text
    save_cache(cache)
    emit_raw("DEBUG", "CACHE WRITE | saved response to cache", dest="LOG")

emit_raw("DEBUG", f"LLM CALL END | result=success | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s", dest="LOG")
return response_text

The completed response text is logged with latency metrics. Truncated responses (TruncatedResponse) and empty replies are explicitly excluded from persistence to avoid polluting the cache with broken or partial generation states. Valid outputs are written to the in-memory cache and persisted via save_cache().

Parameters:

  • prompt (str): The complete prompt text to submit to the model.
  • use_cache (bool, optional): Whether to check and populate the on-disk cache. Defaults to True.
  • thinking_level (str | None, optional): Desired reasoning effort (e.g., "low", "medium", "high"). Clamped or translated according to provider capabilities. Defaults to None.
  • step (str | None, optional): Identifier for the pipeline node or execution stage for usage logging and cost attribution. Defaults to None (assigned to "other").

Returns:

  • str: The generated text response returned by the model.

Raises:

  • LLMRefusalError: Raised when the provider refuses the prompt due to policy, safety, or non-retryable constraints.
  • ValueError: Raised if required provider configurations are missing or invalid JSON is returned.
  • RuntimeError: Raised when API responses omit required response objects.
  • ImportError: Raised if provider SDK dependencies are not installed.
  • Exception: Raised on network failures, timeouts, or HTTP status errors.

Example:

test_prompt = "Hello, how are you?"

emit("SELFTEST_LLM_CALL")
response1 = call_llm(test_prompt, use_cache=False)
emit("SELFTEST_LLM_RESPONSE", response=response1)

docs.title: _cache_key()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _cache_key(prompt: str, provider: str, model: str, thinking_level: str | None) -> str:

Description: Constructs an immutable SHA-256 hexadecimal hash string uniquely identifying a generation request. The hash input scopes the raw prompt string by prepending the provider name, model identifier, and normalized thinking level, formatted as "{provider}|{model}|{thinking_level}\n{prompt}". This ensures identical prompts submitted to different models or reasoning budgets do not collide in the cache.

Parameters:

  • prompt (str): The raw prompt string.
  • provider (str): The active LLM provider (e.g., "GEMINI", "ANTHROPIC").
  • model (str): The specific model name string.
  • thinking_level (str | None): The reasoning level string or None (normalized to "default").

Returns:

  • str: A 64-character hexadecimal SHA-256 hash string.

Raises:

  • Does not raise exceptions.

Example:

def _cache_key(prompt: str, provider: str, model: str, thinking_level: str | None) -> str:
    scope = f"{provider}|{model}|{(thinking_level or 'default').lower()}\n"
    return hashlib.sha256((scope + prompt).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

The function normalizes the input casing of the thinking level and combines it with provider and model namespaces. UTF-8 encoding ensures deterministic hash calculation across different runtime platforms.

docs.title: _call_llm_provider()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _call_llm_provider(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Dispatches chat completion requests to generic OpenAI-compatible REST endpoints, specifically tailored for Ollama and local runtime servers. It queries environment variables for connection endpoints, constructs JSON payloads with appropriate sampling and reasoning parameters, validates responses, tracks token counts, and checks for finish truncation.

docs.title: Phase 1: Environment Resolution and Endpoint Assembly
docs.text:
# Read the provider from environment variable
provider = get_llm_provider()
if not provider:
    raise ValueError("LLM_PROVIDER environment variable is required")

# Construct the names of the other environment variables
model_var = f"{provider}_MODEL"
base_url_var = f"{provider}_BASE_URL"
api_key_var = f"{provider}_API_KEY"

# Read the provider-specific variables
model = os.environ.get(model_var)
base_url = os.environ.get(base_url_var)
api_key = os.environ.get(api_key_var, "")  # API key is optional, default to empty string

# Validate required variables
if not model:
    raise ValueError(f"{model_var} environment variable is required")
if not base_url:
    raise ValueError(f"{base_url_var} environment variable is required")

# Append the endpoint to the base URL
url = f"{base_url.rstrip('/')}/v1/chat/completions"

The function identifies the provider via get_llm_provider() and constructs dynamic environment variable lookup names. It validates that both the model and base URL are present, raising a ValueError if either is missing, before constructing the standard /v1/chat/completions target URL.

docs.title: Phase 2: Payload Assembly and Reasoning Calibration
docs.text:
# Configure headers and payload based on provider
headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
}
if api_key:  # Only add Authorization header if API key is provided
    headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {api_key}"

payload = {
    "model": model,
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
    "temperature": 0.7,
}

if provider == "OLLAMA" and thinking_level:
    # Ollama reasoning models accept low/medium/high; xhigh/max clamp to high.
    # Some Ollama SDKs / API versions look for `think`, others look for standard `reasoning_effort`
    effort = _clamp_level(thinking_level.lower(), ["low", "medium", "high"]) or "medium"
    payload["think"] = effort
    payload["reasoning_effort"] = effort
    payload["temperature"] = 1.0

if rejects_sampling_params(model):
    # Claude Opus 4.7+ / Opus 5.x / Sonnet 5 / Fable reject sampling parameters (400).
    payload.pop("temperature", None)

Headers are populated with bearer token authorization if an API key exists. For Ollama reasoning deployments, the function clamps the requested thinking level to allowed tiers (low, medium, high) and sets both think and reasoning_effort fields while resetting temperature to 1.0. If rejects_sampling_params() returns true for modern reasoning architectures, sampling parameters like temperature are removed to avoid HTTP 400 rejection.

docs.title: Phase 3: Network Execution, Error Checking, and Response Extraction
docs.text:
try:
    response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload, timeout=(10, 300))
    response.raise_for_status()  # HTTP status first: an HTML 502 page must not look like a JSON bug
    try:
        response_json = response.json()
    except (ValueError, requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError):
        from utils.output import emit

        emit(
            "WARN_INVALID_JSON",
            status_code=response.status_code,
            preview=response.text[:200].strip(),
        )
        raise ValueError(f"Provider returned invalid JSON. Status Code: {response.status_code}") from None

    # Defensive check: API may return 200 with error/rate-limit payload missing 'choices'
    if "choices" not in response_json or not response_json["choices"]:
        error_detail = response_json.get("error", response_json)
        from utils.output import emit

        emit("WARN_API_NO_CHOICES", detail=str(error_detail))
        raise RuntimeError(f"API response missing 'choices' key. Response: {error_detail}")

    usage = response_json.get("usage") or {}
    from utils.llm_common import record_usage
    from utils.token_utils import count_tokens_raw, observe_prompt_tokens

    prompt_tokens = usage.get("prompt_tokens") or 0
    record_usage(
        provider,
        model,
        input_tokens=prompt_tokens,
        output_tokens=usage.get("completion_tokens") or 0,
        thinking_tokens=(usage.get("completion_tokens_details") or {}).get("reasoning_tokens") or 0,
        cache_read=(usage.get("prompt_tokens_details") or {}).get("cached_tokens") or 0,
        cost=None,
        measured=bool(usage),
    )
    if usage:
        observe_prompt_tokens(provider, model, count_tokens_raw(prompt), prompt_tokens)
    choice = response_json["choices"][0]
    text = (choice.get("message") or {}).get("content") or ""
    if choice.get("finish_reason") == "length":
        from utils.llm_common import TruncatedResponse

        return TruncatedResponse(text)
    if not text:
        from utils.output import emit

        emit("LLM_EMPTY_REPLY", provider=provider, reason=choice.get("finish_reason") or "n/a")
    return text
except requests.exceptions.HTTPError as e:
    error_message = f"HTTP error occurred: {e}"
    try:
        error_details = response.json().get("error", "No additional details")
        error_message += f" (Details: {error_details})"
    except Exception:
        pass
    raise Exception(error_message) from e
except requests.exceptions.ConnectionError as e:
    raise Exception(f"Failed to connect to {provider} API. Check your network connection.") from e
except requests.exceptions.Timeout as e:
    raise Exception(f"Request to {provider} API timed out.") from e
except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
    raise Exception(f"An error occurred while making the request to {provider}: {e}") from e
except ValueError as e:
    raise Exception(f"Failed to parse response as JSON from {provider}. The server might have returned an invalid response.") from e

The request is submitted via requests.post with a connection timeout of 10 seconds and read timeout of 300 seconds. HTTP errors are caught and unpacked for structured error details. Token metrics from the API payload (including prompt, completion, and reasoning tokens) are logged via record_usage(). If the generation was terminated prematurely due to token budget exhaustion (finish_reason == "length"), the output is wrapped in a TruncatedResponse instance.

Parameters:

  • prompt (str): The prompt payload to send to the completion endpoint.
  • thinking_level (str | None, optional): Reasoning configuration effort to inject into the payload. Defaults to None.

Returns:

  • str: The decoded completion message content, or a TruncatedResponse string wrapper if truncated.

Raises:

  • ValueError: If required environment variables are unset or response JSON is invalid.
  • RuntimeError: If the returned JSON object lacks the 'choices' array.
  • Exception: If HTTP, connection, timeout, or parsing errors occur.

docs.title: _emit_call_usage()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _emit_call_usage(step: str, estimate: int, usage: dict, measured: int) -> None:

Description: Formats and logs a consolidated console line summarizing token consumption, cost, and deviation for an LLM call. It compares billed input tokens against initial heuristic estimates to surface token calculation drift across execution nodes.

Parameters:

  • step (str): The execution step name or node identifier.
  • estimate (int): The estimated input token count.
  • usage (dict): The token usage ledger dictionary containing input, output, thinking, and cache statistics.
  • measured (int): Count of actual measured API requests associated with this call.

Returns:

  • None

Raises:

  • Does not raise exceptions.

Example:

def _emit_call_usage(step: str, estimate: int, usage: dict, measured: int) -> None:
    """One console line per LLM call: billed input vs the estimate, output (thinking), cached, cost.
    `measured` = requests with provider-reported usage (the deviation is per measured request)."""
    from utils.output import emit, get
    from utils.token_utils import format_cost

    per_request = usage["input"] / measured
    deviation = f"{(per_request - estimate) / estimate:+.0%}" if estimate else get("CFG_VALUE_UNKNOWN")
    emit(
        "LLM_CALL_USAGE",
        step=step,
        input=f"{usage['input']:,}",
        estimate=f"{estimate:,}",
        deviation=deviation,
        requests=get("LLM_CALL_REQUESTS", count=measured) if measured > 1 else "",
        output=f"{usage['output']:,}",
        thinking=f"{usage['thinking']:,}",
        cached=f"{usage['cache_read']:,}",
        cost=format_cost(usage),
    )

The helper derives the average input tokens per request, computes the percentage deviation relative to the pre-call estimate, and outputs the structured LLM_CALL_USAGE notification.

docs.title: Cache Storage Format
docs.text:
The persistent JSON cache stored in llm_cache_v2.json and mirrored in the _cache singleton maps SHA-256 hash keys to completion responses.

Field / Key Type Description key (hashlib.sha256) str 64-character hexadecimal SHA-256 digest of {provider}\|{model}\|{thinking_level}\n{prompt} value str Full response string returned by the provider for the specified prompt

Example structure:

{
  "a3c1e847d0d0f2b3e8c9...": "# Overview\nThis module manages orchestration...",
  "b84f932e19a405cde210...": "def example_function():\n    return True\n"
}

docs.title: Usage Ledger Delta Dictionary
docs.text:
The usage dictionary returned by usage_delta() and processed by _emit_call_usage() tracks token volumes and financial cost across calls.

Field Type Description input int Total billed prompt/input tokens across the call output int Total completion/output tokens generated thinking int Total reasoning or thought tokens generated by reasoning models cache_read int Prompt tokens served from provider-side prompt caching calls int Total number of API requests initiated during this call unmeasured_calls int Number of requests that did not report usage statistics cost float \| None Financial cost incurred in USD (or None if unknown/unpriced)

docs.title: OpenAI-Compatible Chat Payload
docs.text:
Schema generated by _call_llm_provider() when dispatching requests to generic endpoints:

Property Type Description model str Provider model name (from <PROVIDER>_MODEL) messages list[dict] Array containing user message objects: [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}] temperature float Sampling temperature (set to 0.7 by default, 1.0 for Ollama reasoning, omitted for newer Claude models) think str Reasoning budget level (low, medium, high) sent to Ollama endpoints reasoning_effort str Standard reasoning effort level sent to compatible endpoints

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
call_llm.py standardizes error conditions across disparate HTTP and SDK client libraries:

  • Refusal Caching (LLMRefusalError): When an upstream provider raises an LLMRefusalError, the module checks e.retryable. If False, the refusal is recorded in memory via remember_refusal(). If the pipeline subsequently attempts to invoke call_llm() with an identical request key, the refusal is re-raised immediately without initiating network requests.
  • Corrupted or Truncated Responses (TruncatedResponse): Responses terminating due to length exhaustion (finish_reason == "length") are wrapped as TruncatedResponse instances. The caching logic explicitly validates getattr(response_text, "truncated", False) and skips writing them to disk to avoid caching partial generation outputs.
  • Network & HTTP Failures: Generic provider requests in _call_llm_provider() validate HTTP response codes prior to JSON decoding via response.raise_for_status(). HTML error pages (such as HTTP 502 Bad Gateway) are caught cleanly without raising misleading JSON decode errors. In addition, requests.exceptions.ConnectionError and requests.exceptions.Timeout are wrapped in user-friendly Exception messages specifying the target provider name.
  • Cache Corruption Safeguards: load_cache() intercepts json.JSONDecodeError and OSError if cache files are manually altered or corrupted, resetting the cache in memory to an empty dictionary and logging a warning. Atomic file replacement in save_cache() using temporary files (.tmp) and os.replace prevents partial file writes if execution terminates mid-dump.

docs.title: chapter_check.py
docs.text: Source: utils/chapter_check.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
utils/chapter_check.py provides deterministic quality assurance and linting for generated Markdown chapters. Operating without Large Language Model (LLM) calls, it inspects written documentation pages strictly through regular expressions, AST/token analysis, and pipeline-accurate rendering tests. The module functions as a verification gate at the end of the documentation build pipeline, outputting a consolidated diagnostic report to chapter_check.json and emitting structured telemetry via utils.output.emit.

The verification architecture operates across three distinct evaluation layers. First, structural checks analyze CommonMark syntax compliance across every page, identifying unclosed code fences, broken internal hyperlinks, and syntactic defects in Mermaid diagram blocks that would cause client-side rendering crashes. Second, markup fidelity checks evaluate site renderer compatibility by injecting non-rendering Unicode Private Use Area (PUA) markers into Markdown construct boundaries, rendering the marked text through the MkDocs renderer, and comparing the resulting HTML tag hierarchies against CommonMark baseline expectations. Third, factual conformance checks validate the content of API reference pages against verified source facts, detecting omitted symbols, mutated signatures, nonexistent type names in headings, and broken or superfluous cross-references.

flowchart TD subgraph Ingestion["Input Ingestion"] initNode["run_chapter_check()"] --> loadFacts["Extract Facts & Source Maps"] loadFacts --> parseInput["parse_page()"] end subgraph Verification["Validation Pipeline"] valStart["check_chapter()"] --> checkLinks["broken_links()"] valStart --> checkMermaid["diagram_problems()"] valStart --> checkMarkup["markup_problems()"] valStart --> checkFacts["Fact Conformance Checks"] checkMarkup --> injectMarks["_rendered_marks()"] injectMarks --> parseHTML["_MarkContexts (HTMLParser)"] parseHTML --> evalVerdicts["_mark_ok() & Classify"] checkFacts --> symCheck["missing_symbols()"] checkFacts --> sigCheck["signature_issues()"] checkFacts --> typeCheck["unknown_type_names()"] checkFacts --> seeAlso["see_also_issues()"] end subgraph Reporting["Diagnostics & Persistence"] repStart["Aggregate Findings"] --> writeJson["chapter_check.json"] repStart --> emitWarnings["emit(CHAPTER_CHECK_*)"] end parseInput --> valStart checkLinks --> repStart checkMermaid --> repStart evalVerdicts --> repStart symCheck --> repStart sigCheck --> repStart typeCheck --> repStart seeAlso --> repStart classDef entryNode stroke:#d33,stroke-width:3px,fill:#fff5f5; class initNode,valStart,repStart entryNode Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom

docs.title: parse_page()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def parse_page(markdown: str) -> dict:

Description: Parses raw Markdown text into structured components without executing external rendering engines. It reads the source line-by-line following GitHub CommonMark conventions to identify code fences, separating fenced blocks from prose and cataloging all headings along with their nesting levels. Any code block opener that remains unclosed at the end of the document is reclassified as prose, and its line number is tracked in the unclosed list.

Parameters:

  • markdown (str): The raw Markdown text content of a documentation chapter.

Returns:

  • dict: A dictionary containing parsed page structures:
    • "prose": List of (line_number, text) tuples for lines outside code blocks.
    • "blocks": List of dictionary records for closed code blocks (lang, start, end, text).
    • "headings": List of (line_number, level, text) tuples for Markdown headings.
    • "unclosed": List of 1-based line numbers for unclosed opening code fences.

Example:

lines = markdown.split("\n")
prose, blocks, headings, unclosed = [], [], [], []
number = 0
while number < len(lines):
    line = lines[number]
    opener = _FENCE_RE.match(line)
    if opener and opener.group(2)[0] == "`" and "`" in line[opener.end(2) :]:  # ```mermaid``` in prose: inline code
        opener = None
    if opener:
        indent, fence = len(opener.group(1)), opener.group(2)
        for end in range(number + 1, len(lines)):
            closer = _FENCE_RE.match(lines[end])
            if (
                closer
                and closer.group(2)[0] == fence[0]
                and len(closer.group(2)) >= len(fence)
                and not lines[end][closer.end(2) :].strip()
                and len(closer.group(1)) <= indent + 3
            ):
                blocks.append({"lang": opener.group(3).lower(), "start": number + 1, "end": end + 1, "text": "\n".join(lines[number + 1 : end])})
                number = end + 1
                break
        else:
            unclosed.append(number + 1)
            prose.append((number + 1, line))
            number += 1
        continue
    prose.append((number + 1, line))
    heading = _HEADING_RE.match(line)
    if heading:
        headings.append((number + 1, len(heading.group(1)), heading.group(2)))
    number += 1

The parsing loop uses _FENCE_RE to distinguish valid code fence delimiters (triple backticks or tildes). It explicitly guards against inline code spans such as ```mermaid``` appearing in prose. When a fence opener is encountered, the inner loop searches ahead for a matching closer with identical or greater delimiter length and an indentation within 3 spaces of the opener; if found, the intermediate text is recorded as a code block. If the inner search reaches the end of the file without finding a matching delimiter, the opening line is appended to unclosed and treated as prose.

docs.title: resolve_link()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def resolve_link(page: str, target: str) -> str | None:

Description: Resolves a relative Markdown link target against the site-relative path of the source page, returning a normalized POSIX path. Protocol links (https:, mailto:), root-relative links starting with /, and in-page anchor links starting with # are ignored, returning None. URL query strings and fragment identifiers are stripped, and percent-encoded escapes are decoded.

Parameters:

  • page (str): The site-relative file path of the page containing the link (e.g., "api/index.md").
  • target (str): The raw hyperlink target attribute extracted from the Markdown link.

Returns:

  • str | None: The normalized site-relative path to the target file, or None if the target is external or an anchor.

Example:

if re.match(r"^[a-zA-Z][\w+.-]*:", target) or target.startswith(("#", "/")):
    return None
path = unquote(target.split("#", 1)[0].split("?", 1)[0])
return posixpath.normpath(posixpath.join(posixpath.dirname(page), path)) if path else None

The function first checks the target against a URI scheme regex and leading # or / prefixes, immediately returning None for external or non-relative references. For candidate relative paths, query strings and anchors are discarded using string splits, and urllib.parse.unquote resolves any URL-encoded characters. The resulting path is joined with the source page's directory name using posixpath.join and normalized with posixpath.normpath.

docs.title: broken_links()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def broken_links(page: str, parsed: dict, exists) -> list[dict]:

Description: Identifies all relative hyperlinks and image references in a page's prose whose targets cannot be resolved to an existing file in the generated site. Targets are resolved via resolve_link, and their presence is checked using the caller-supplied exists predicate.

Parameters:

  • page (str): The site-relative path of the current documentation page.
  • parsed (dict): The parsed page dictionary produced by parse_page.
  • exists (Callable[[str], bool]): A predicate function returning True if a site-relative path exists.

Returns:

  • list[dict]: A list of problem records, each containing "line" (int) and "target" (str).

Example:

problems = []
for number, target in _links(parsed["prose"]):
    resolved = resolve_link(page, target)
    if resolved is not None and not exists(resolved):
        problems.append({"line": number, "target": target})
return problems

This function calls _links across all prose lines to collect link targets while omitting code spans and HTML comments. Each target is resolved against the current page path via resolve_link. If the target resolves to a site-relative path and exists(resolved) returns False, a diagnostic entry is appended with the target text and line number.

docs.title: mermaid_problems()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def mermaid_problems(source: str) -> list[dict]:

Description: Evaluates the syntax of a Mermaid diagram block to detect conditions that cause client-side rendering crashes. It validates frontmatter headers, checks diagram type declarations against supported Mermaid diagram types, and applies conservative syntax rules to flowcharts and graph diagrams to catch invalid arrow operators, unescaped brackets in labels, and unbalanced delimiters.

Parameters:

  • source (str): The raw text content of the Mermaid diagram block.

Returns:

  • list[dict]: A list of dictionaries with "line" (int, 1-based offset within the block) and "problem" (str), where problem is one of "type", "arrow", "quotes", "brackets", or "label".

docs.title: Phase 1: Header and Diagram Type Validation
docs.text:
lines = source.split("\n")
body = [(number, line) for number, line in enumerate(lines, start=1) if line.strip() and not line.strip().startswith("%%")]
if body and body[0][1].strip() == "---":  # frontmatter (title / config) before the diagram type
    closing = next((i for i, (_n, line) in enumerate(body[1:], start=1) if line.strip() == "---"), None)
    body = body[closing + 1 :] if closing is not None else []
if not body:
    return []
first = body[0][1].strip().split()[0].rstrip(":")
if first not in _MERMAID_TYPES:
    return [{"line": body[0][0], "problem": "type"}]
if not first.startswith(("flowchart", "graph")):
    return []

The function filters out empty lines and comments (%%), then checks for YAML-style frontmatter demarcated by triple dashes (---). The first active line after frontmatter is inspected to verify that its leading token belongs to _MERMAID_TYPES. If the type is unrecognized, a "type" error is reported immediately; if the diagram type is valid but not a flowchart or graph, detailed syntax scanning is skipped.

docs.title: Phase 2: Flowchart and Graph Syntax Scanning
docs.text:
markdown_strings = '"`' in source  # "`multi-line markdown labels`" span lines: quote and bracket counts do not apply
problems = []
for number, line in body[1:]:
    if line.count('"') % 2 and not markdown_strings:
        problems.append({"line": number, "problem": "quotes"})
        continue
    code = re.sub(r'"[^"]*"', '""', line)
    code = re.sub(r"\|[^|]*\|", "||", code)  # edge labels: A -->|label| B
    code = re.sub(r"\w>[^\]]*\]", "x", code)  # the asymmetric shape: id>label]
    unlabelled = re.sub(r"\[[^\]]*\]|\([^)]*\)|\{[^}]*\}", "", code)  # `>>` inside a label is text
    if re.search(r"(?<![-=.])>>", unlabelled):
        problems.append({"line": number, "problem": "arrow"})
    elif re.search(r"\w\[(?![(\[/\\])[^\]\"]*[(\[{]", code):  # A[run(x)] — not the shapes A[(db)], A[[sub]], A[/p/]
        problems.append({"line": number, "problem": "label"})
    elif not markdown_strings and any(code.count(o) != code.count(c) for o, c in ("[]", "()", "{}")):
        problems.append({"line": number, "problem": "brackets"})
return problems

For flowchart diagrams, lines are evaluated sequentially unless Markdown strings (indicated by " + `) are present. The scanner identifies odd quotation mark counts as "quotes", sanitizes label text and edge labels using regular expressions, and checks for unsupported code operators such as raw >> arrows. It also detects nested parentheses or brackets inside standard square brackets that violate Mermaid label syntax unless enclosed in quotation marks.

docs.title: diagram_problems()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def diagram_problems(parsed: dict) -> list[dict]:

Description: Identifies syntax problems across all Mermaid code blocks in a parsed page. It maps the relative block-level error offsets returned by mermaid_problems to absolute line numbers in the documentation file.

Parameters:

  • parsed (dict): The parsed page dictionary produced by parse_page.

Returns:

  • list[dict]: A list of problem records with "diagram" (int, 1-based index of the diagram), "line" (int, 1-based page line number), and "problem" (str).

Example:

diagrams = [block for block in parsed["blocks"] if block["lang"] == "mermaid"]
return [
    {"diagram": number, "line": block["start"] + problem["line"], "problem": problem["problem"]}
    for number, block in enumerate(diagrams, start=1)
    for problem in mermaid_problems(block["text"])
]

This function filters parsed["blocks"] for blocks whose language tag is "mermaid". For each diagram block, it runs mermaid_problems(block["text"]) and offsets the reported line number by block["start"], producing page-accurate diagnostics.

docs.title: markup_verdicts()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def markup_verdicts(markdown: str, parsed: dict, render) -> tuple[list[tuple[str, tuple, bool | None]], int]:

Description: Compares the CommonMark reading of a document against the output of the site's renderer. It injects tracking markers into intended block elements, renders the document to HTML, and determines whether each element rendered in its intended structural context. This function provides strict verification for markup repair routines such as utils.mkdocs.repair_markup.

Parameters:

  • markdown (str): The raw Markdown text of the page.
  • parsed (dict): The parsed page dictionary produced by parse_page.
  • render (Callable[[str], str]): A rendering function mapping Markdown text to HTML.

Returns:

  • tuple[list[tuple[str, tuple, bool | None]], int]: A tuple consisting of:
    • List of verdicts as (kind, reading, ok), where kind is the element type, reading is a normalized tuple of expected properties, and ok is True, False, or None (if the marker was swallowed by raw HTML).
    • int: Total number of rendered code blocks.

Example:

_lines, marks, found, code_blocks = _rendered_marks(markdown, parsed, render)
verdicts = []
for number, (_index, kind, expect) in enumerate(marks):
    reading = tuple(sorted((key, value) for key, value in expect.items() if key not in ("opener", "cut")))
    where = found.get(number)
    verdicts.append((kind, reading, None if where is None else _mark_ok(kind, expect, where)))
return verdicts, code_blocks

The function calls _rendered_marks to generate intended element markers and collect their rendered HTML positions from _MarkContexts. Each mark expectation is converted into an order-independent tuple of properties, omitting line-specific keys (opener, cut). The mark's rendered context is evaluated using _mark_ok, yielding an exact verdict for every structural element.

docs.title: markup_problems()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def markup_problems(markdown: str, parsed: dict, render) -> dict:

Description: Identifies structural Markdown defects where the site renderer parses content differently than intended under CommonMark rules. It evaluates list items rendered as plain text, flattened nested lists, merged adjacent lists of different types, split lists caused by indented content, tables parsed as raw text, and unclosed or swallowed code blocks.

Parameters:

  • markdown (str): The raw Markdown text of the page.
  • parsed (dict): The parsed page structure from parse_page.
  • render (Callable[[str], str]): The Markdown-to-HTML rendering function.

Returns:

  • dict: A dictionary mapping each markup error category from _MARKUP_KINDS to a list of finding records:
    • "lists_as_text": [{"line": int, "items": int}]
    • "lists_flattened": [{"line": int, "items": int}]
    • "lists_merged": [{"line": int, "items": int}]
    • "lists_split": [{"line": int}]
    • "tables_as_text": [{"line": int}]
    • "code_blocks_not_rendered": [{"line": int, "opener": str}]

docs.title: Phase 1: Mark Placement and Code Block Ownership Mapping
docs.text:
lines, marks, found, _code_blocks = _rendered_marks(markdown, parsed, render)
owners = {}  # rendered code block -> [(mark, opener)] of the fenced blocks whose first code line it shows
for number, (_index, kind, expect) in enumerate(marks):
    if kind == "code" and found.get(number) and found[number]["code"]:
        owners.setdefault(found[number]["code"], []).append((number, expect["opener"]))
problems = {kind: [] for kind in _MARKUP_KINDS}
blamed = set()  # fenced blocks already reported

def blame(opener: int) -> None:
    if opener not in blamed:
        blamed.add(opener)
        problems["code_blocks_not_rendered"].append({"line": opener, "opener": lines[opener - 1].strip()[:80]})

_rendered_marks places invisible Unicode markers at every structural construct and executes the site renderer. The resulting found contexts are inspected to establish code block ownership: for each "code" mark that landed inside a rendered code element (<pre> or Mermaid div), the mark and its opening line are indexed by rendered block ID. The blame helper records code fence failures and prevents redundant reporting of cascaded unclosed blocks.

docs.title: Phase 2: Structural Verification and Element Classification
docs.text:
split_since_item, run, item_listed, last_block = False, None, True, None  # run: list items being folded
for number, (index, kind, expect) in enumerate(marks):
    where = found.get(number)
    if where is None:  # the mark vanished (raw HTML, a comment): nothing to compare
        continue
    if kind != "code" and where["code"]:
        opened = [opener for mark, opener in owners.get(where["code"], []) if mark < number]
        if opened:
            blame(opened[-1])
        run = None
        continue
    problem = None
    if kind == "after":
        continue
    if kind == "item":
        if not where["li"] or where["marker"]:
            problem = "lists_as_text"
        elif where["depth"] < expect["depth"]:
            problem = "lists_flattened"
        elif where["list"] != ("ol" if expect["numbered"] else "ul"):
            problem = "lists_merged"
        elif ("start" in expect or expect.get("continues")) and where["number"] == 1 and not split_since_item:
            problem = "lists_split"
        split_since_item, item_listed = False, where["li"] and not where["marker"]
    elif kind == "content":  # outside the list, or in a shallower item than its own
        problem = "lists_split" if item_listed and (not where["li"] or where["depth"] < expect["depth"]) else None
    elif kind == "table":
        if not where["th"]:
            problem = "tables_as_text"
        elif expect["item"] and item_listed and (not where["li"] or where["depth"] < expect["depth"]):
            problem = "lists_split"
    else:
        knock_on, last_block = last_block in blamed, expect["opener"]
        if not where["code"]:
            if not knock_on:  # else its opening fence was taken as the closer of the block before, reported
                blame(expect["opener"])
            run = None
            continue
        if expect["item"] and item_listed and (not where["li"] or where["depth"] < expect["depth"]):
            problem = "lists_split"

The loop iterates through every placed marker. If a non-code construct was swallowed into a rendered code block (where["code"]), the preceding fence opener is blamed for leaving its block unclosed. List items (kind == "item") are checked to confirm they generated an <li> tag without visible marker characters, achieved the expected nesting depth, matched the ordered/unordered list type, and maintained numbering continuity. Tables and item continuation paragraphs ("content") are checked to verify they were not broken out into sibling blocks or rendered as plain text.

docs.title: Phase 3: Consecutive Error Aggregation
docs.text:
if problem is None:
        run = None
        continue
    if problem == "lists_split" and kind != "item":
        split_since_item = True
    if problem in _LIST_RUNS and run and run[0] == problem:
        between = [line.strip() for line in lines[run[2] + 1 : index]]
        if all(between) or not any(between):  # the same list, tight or loose
            run[1]["items"] += 1
            run = (problem, run[1], index)
            continue
    finding = {"line": expect["opener"] if kind == "code" else index + 1}
    if problem in _LIST_RUNS:
        finding["items"] = 1
        run = (problem, finding, index)
    else:
        run = None
    problems[problem].append(finding)
return problems

For recurring list errors (lists_as_text, lists_flattened, lists_merged), adjacent items belonging to the same list run are collapsed into a single diagnostic finding. The items count on the initial finding is incremented rather than emitting individual findings for every line in the list. Non-list problems or discontinuous list items trigger new finding records in the output dictionary.

docs.title: missing_symbols()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def missing_symbols(parsed: dict, symbols: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:

Description: Cross-references verified symbols extracted from the source code against the text of the documentation page. Any symbol whose terminal identifier never appears in the prose or non-Mermaid code blocks of the page is reported as missing.

Parameters:

  • parsed (dict): The parsed page dictionary from parse_page.
  • symbols (list[dict]): A list of verified symbol records from facts.py.

Returns:

  • list[dict]: A list of missing symbol dictionaries containing "name", "kind", "parent", and "line".

Example:

text = _page_text(parsed)
words = set(re.findall(r"\w+", text)) | {word.lstrip("$") for word in re.findall(r"\$\w+", text)}
words |= set(re.findall(r"[A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*", text))  # an identifier glued to CJK prose: 调用run_flow函数
missing = []
for symbol in symbols:
    name = str(symbol.get("name", "")).split(".")[-1].lstrip("$")
    if name and not (name in words or _names_in(text, name)):
        missing.append({k: symbol.get(k) for k in ("name", "kind", "parent", "line")})
return missing

The function extracts all non-diagram text using _page_text and extracts word sets using regex patterns that account for standard identifiers, PHP-style leading $, and Latin identifiers embedded within CJK prose. For each verified symbol, the terminal name component is evaluated against the extracted words and tested via utils.facts._names_in. Unmatched symbols are returned in the result list.

docs.title: signature_issues()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def signature_issues(parsed: dict, source: str, symbols: list[dict]) -> tuple[list[dict], list[dict]]:

Description: Compares declared code signatures documented in a chapter against verified symbols and the raw source code. Signatures that appear verbatim in the source are accepted immediately. Otherwise, documented parameter lists are compared against verified AST signatures: signatures that only append non-source annotations (such as synthetic type hints) are flagged as embellished, while signatures that add, omit, rename, or reorder parameters are flagged as mismatches.

Parameters:

  • parsed (dict): The parsed page dictionary from parse_page.
  • source (str): The raw text content of the underlying source code file.
  • symbols (list[dict]): Verified symbol definitions extracted from the source file.

Returns:

  • tuple[list[dict], list[dict]]: A tuple of two lists: (mismatches, embellished).
    • mismatches: [{"line": int, "signature": str, "source": str}]
    • embellished: [{"line": int, "signature": str}]

Example:

flat_source = _collapse(source)
by_name = {}
for symbol in symbols:
    by_name.setdefault(str(symbol.get("name", "")).split(".")[-1], []).append(_head(str(symbol.get("signature", ""))))
mismatches, embellished = [], []
for number, text in _signatures(parsed):
    if _collapse(text).rstrip(":{; ") in flat_source:
        continue
    name = _declared_name(text)
    candidates = by_name.get(name[0]) if name else None
    if not candidates:
        continue
    verdicts = [_compare(_head(text), candidate) for candidate in candidates]
    if "same" in verdicts:
        continue
    if "embellished" in verdicts:
        embellished.append({"line": number, "signature": text})
    else:
        mismatches.append({"line": number, "signature": text, "source": _collapse(candidates[0])[:200]})
return mismatches, embellished

The function indexes verified symbol signatures by terminal identifier name and normalizes the source code using _collapse. For each signature extracted via _signatures, if its collapsed text is not present verbatim in flat_source, it is compared against candidate signatures for that symbol using _compare. Depending on the comparison verdict, the signature is accepted, marked as embellished, or marked as a mismatch.

docs.title: unknown_type_names()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def unknown_type_names(parsed: dict, known_words: set) -> list[dict]:

Description: Detects invented type names inside code spans in Markdown headings (e.g., ###FactClaim``). Any PascalCase identifier appearing in an inline code span inside a heading that does not exist anywhere across the crawled codebase is reported as an unknown type.

Parameters:

  • parsed (dict): The parsed page structure from parse_page.
  • known_words (set): A set of all identifier tokens found across all crawled repository files.

Returns:

  • list[dict]: A list of problem records with "line" (int) and "name" (str).

Example:

if not known_words:
    return []
found = []
for number, _level, text in parsed["headings"]:
    spans = " ".join(match.group(2) for match in _CODE_SPAN_RE.finditer(text))
    names = sorted(set(re.findall(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*", spans)))  # ASCII: a name glued to CJK text still counts
    found.extend({"line": number, "name": word} for word in names if _TYPE_NAME_RE.match(word) and word not in known_words)
return found

The function extracts inline code spans from heading text using _CODE_SPAN_RE. Word tokens are matched against _TYPE_NAME_RE, which selects CamelCase or PascalCase type names containing both uppercase and lowercase characters. Any token matching this pattern that is absent from known_words is recorded as an invented type name.

docs.title: see_also_issues()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def see_also_issues(page: str, parsed: dict, module: str, module_by_page: dict, facts: dict) -> tuple[list, list]:

Description: Validates the cross-references in the "See Also" section of an API reference page. It compares linked documentation targets against the module's verified dependency graph (depends_on and used_by), identifying links to unrelated modules as well as missing links to known upstream dependencies.

Parameters:

  • page (str): The site-relative path of the documentation page.
  • parsed (dict): The parsed page dictionary from parse_page.
  • module (str): The original module path corresponding to this page.
  • module_by_page (dict): Mapping of site-relative page paths to module paths.
  • facts (dict): The verified facts record for this module from facts.py.

Returns:

  • tuple[list, list]: A tuple of two lists: (unrelated, missing).
    • unrelated: [{"line": int, "module": str}]
    • missing: [{"module": str}]

Example:

depends = {edge["module"] for edge in facts.get("depends_on", [])} & set(module_by_page.values())  # only documented ones can be linked
related = depends | set(facts.get("used_by", []))
linked = {}
pages = set(module_by_page)
section = _see_also_section(parsed, pages, page)
for number, target in _links(section):
    resolved = resolve_link(page, target)
    target_module = module_by_page.get(resolved) if resolved else None
    if target_module and target_module != module:
        linked.setdefault(target_module, number)
unrelated = [{"line": number, "module": target} for target, number in sorted(linked.items(), key=lambda item: item[1]) if target not in related]
missing = [{"module": target} for target in sorted(depends - set(linked))]
return unrelated, missing

The function filters verified dependencies down to modules that have generated pages (module_by_page.values()). It extracts all links from the "See Also" section using _see_also_section and resolves each target to a module. Modules linked in the section that do not appear in depends_on or used_by are reported as unrelated, while required dependencies that were not linked are reported as missing.

docs.title: check_chapter()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def check_chapter( page: str, markdown: str, exists, module: str = "", facts: dict | None = None, source: str = "", known_words=None, module_by_page=None, render=None, ) -> dict:

Description: Executes all checks against a single written chapter and compiles the results into a unified report dictionary. It runs link verification, diagram syntax checks, and unclosed code fence checks on all pages. When a rendering function is supplied, markup fidelity checks are executed. When verified facts are available, it also executes symbol, signature, type name, and dependency checks.

Parameters:

  • page (str): The site-relative filename of the page.
  • markdown (str): The raw Markdown text of the chapter.
  • exists (Callable[[str], bool]): Predicate testing whether a site path exists.
  • module (str, optional): The original source module path. Defaults to "".
  • facts (dict | None, optional): Verified facts record from facts.py. Defaults to None.
  • source (str, optional): The raw source code of the module. Defaults to "".
  • known_words (set | None, optional): Set of repository-wide identifier tokens. Defaults to None.
  • module_by_page (dict | None, optional): Mapping of page paths to module paths. Defaults to None.
  • render (Callable[[str], str] | None, optional): Markdown rendering function. Defaults to None.

Returns:

  • dict: Complete diagnostic report for the page containing all issue categories.

Example:

parsed = parse_page(markdown)
report = {
    "page": page,
    "module": module,
    "broken_links": broken_links(page, parsed, exists),
    "diagram_problems": diagram_problems(parsed),
    "unclosed_fences": [{"line": line} for line in parsed["unclosed"]],
}
if render:
    report |= markup_problems(markdown, parsed, render)
if facts and facts.get("claims") is not None:
    symbols = facts.get("symbols", [])
    mismatches, embellished = signature_issues(parsed, source, symbols)
    unrelated, missing = see_also_issues(page, parsed, module, module_by_page or {}, facts)
    report |= {
        "missing_symbols": missing_symbols(parsed, symbols),
        "signature_mismatches": mismatches,
        "signatures_embellished": embellished,
        "unknown_type_names": unknown_type_names(parsed, known_words or set()),
        "see_also_unrelated": unrelated,
        "see_also_missing_dependencies": missing,
    }
return report

The function first parses the document into structured components via parse_page. Base checks populate broken_links, diagram_problems, and unclosed_fences. If render is supplied, markup_problems is executed and merged into the report. If facts contains valid claims, symbol coverage, signature fidelity, unknown type names, and See Also consistency are evaluated and added to the report.

docs.title: run_chapter_check()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def run_chapter_check(output_path: str, site_dir: str, chapter_files: list, prep_res: dict, standalone: bool = False, render=None) -> dict:

Description: Coordinates chapter verification across all generated files in the documentation suite. It writes the consolidated diagnostic summary to chapter_check.json in output_path, logs structured warnings via utils.output.emit, and returns the final report dictionary.

Parameters:

  • output_path (str): Base output directory where chapter_check.json is written.
  • site_dir (str): Root directory containing the generated documentation files.
  • chapter_files (list[dict]): List of generated chapter file dicts (filename, content, original_path).
  • prep_res (dict): Pipeline preparation results containing module_facts, sources, and known_words.
  • standalone (bool, optional): Whether output is standalone Markdown rather than MkDocs. Defaults to False.
  • render (Callable[[str], str] | None, optional): Markdown renderer for MkDocs pipelines. Defaults to None.

Returns:

  • dict: Aggregated diagnostics summary dictionary with pages, totals, and reports.

docs.title: Phase 1: Context Resolution and Existence Checker Setup
docs.text:
module_facts = prep_res.get("module_facts") or {}
sources = prep_res.get("sources") or {}
known_words = prep_res.get("known_words") or set()
pages = {cf["filename"] for cf in chapter_files}
module_by_page = {cf["filename"]: cf.get("original_path") for cf in chapter_files if cf.get("original_path")}
generated = {"index.md", "full_content.md", "facts.json"}

def exists(path):
    if path in pages or path in generated:
        return True
    if standalone and path.endswith(".md"):
        return False
    return os.path.exists(os.path.join(site_dir, *path.split("/")))

The function extracts facts, source content, and known identifiers from prep_res and builds lookup maps for chapter files. An exists callback is defined to resolve relative file targets against in-memory chapter names, standard generated files, and the filesystem under site_dir. In standalone mode, references to non-current .md files are rejected to avoid linking to stale files from earlier runs.

docs.title: Phase 2: Page Iteration and Event Emission
docs.text:
reports = []
for cf in chapter_files:
    module = cf.get("original_path") or ""
    report = check_chapter(
        cf["filename"], cf["content"], exists, module, module_facts.get(module), sources.get(module, ""), known_words, module_by_page, render
    )
    reports.append(report)
    for problem in report["broken_links"]:
        emit("CHAPTER_CHECK_BROKEN_LINK", page=cf["filename"], line=problem["line"], target=problem["target"])
    grouped = {}
    for problem in report["diagram_problems"]:
        grouped.setdefault((problem["diagram"], problem["problem"]), []).append(str(problem["line"]))
    for (diagram, problem), lines in grouped.items():  # one warning per diagram and kind, its lines listed
        emit(_DIAGRAM_KEYS[problem], page=cf["filename"], line=", ".join(lines), diagram=diagram)
    for kind in _MARKUP_KINDS:  # one warning per page and kind, its lines listed
        if report.get(kind):
            emit(_MARKUP_KEYS[kind], page=cf["filename"], count=len(report[kind]), lines=_line_list(report[kind]))
    for kind in _FACT_KINDS:
        for item in report.get(kind, []):
            emit("CHAPTER_CHECK_DETAIL", page=cf["filename"], kind=kind, detail=json.dumps(item, ensure_ascii=False))

Each chapter file is processed through check_chapter. Diagnostic events are emitted via emit for broken links, diagram failures (grouped by diagram index and error type), and markup issues across all recognized categories. Verified fact mismatches are emitted individually as serialized JSON strings for downstream debugging.

docs.title: Phase 3: Aggregation, Serialization, and Summary Telemetry
docs.text:
totals = {kind: sum(len(report.get(kind, [])) for report in reports) for kind in _COUNTED}
totals["diagrams_failing"] = sum(len({problem["diagram"] for problem in report["diagram_problems"]}) for report in reports)
document = {"pages": len(reports), "totals": totals, "reports": reports}
report_path = os.path.join(output_path, REPORT_FILENAME)
with open(report_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    json.dump(document, f, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
emit(
    "CHAPTER_CHECK_DONE",
    pages=len(reports),
    path=report_path,
    broken_links=totals["broken_links"],
    diagram_problems=totals["diagrams_failing"],
    unclosed_fences=totals["unclosed_fences"],
)
if render:
    emit("CHAPTER_CHECK_MARKUP", **{kind: totals[kind] for kind in _MARKUP_KINDS})
if any("missing_symbols" in report for report in reports):  # pages with verified facts
    emit("CHAPTER_CHECK_FACTS", **{kind: totals[kind] for kind in _FACT_KINDS})
return document

The function aggregates issue counts across all pages into the totals dictionary and counts distinct failing diagrams. The complete results are serialized to chapter_check.json at output_path. Summary status events (CHAPTER_CHECK_DONE, and conditionally CHAPTER_CHECK_MARKUP and CHAPTER_CHECK_FACTS) are emitted before returning the aggregated document.

Signature: def source_context(files_data: list) -> tuple[dict, set]:

Description: Prepares source code context for run_chapter_check from raw crawled files. It normalizes file paths to POSIX-style forward slashes and collects the set of all alphanumeric word tokens across the codebase for type validation.

Parameters:

  • files_data (list[tuple[str, str]]): List of (filepath, content) tuples for crawled repository files.

    • known_words: Set of all identifier tokens extracted from the source files.

Example:

known_words = {word for content in sources.values() for word in re.findall(r"\w+", content)}
return sources, known_words

This helper converts system-specific directory separators to forward slashes across all file paths in files_data and extracts every \w+ token from each file into a unified set.
