docs.title: crawl_local_files()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def crawl_local_files( directory, include_patterns=None, exclude_patterns=None, max_file_size=None, use_relative_paths=True, ):

Description: Recursively walks the specified local directory to collect, filter, and extract file contents into a standardized dictionary structure. The function enforces root and nested .gitignore compliance, evaluates custom glob exclusion and inclusion rules, validates file sizes against byte limits, decodes text using utf-8-sig to safely strip Byte Order Marks (BOM), and emits comprehensive progress metrics.

Parameters:

  • directory (str): The target filesystem path pointing to the root directory to crawl.
  • include_patterns (set | None): Optional set of glob expressions (e.g., {"*.py", "*.js"}) restricting the crawler strictly to matching file paths.
  • exclude_patterns (set | None): Optional set of glob expressions (e.g., {"tests/*", "*.pyc"}) specifying directories and files to exclude.
  • max_file_size (int | None): Optional maximum file size threshold in bytes. Files exceeding this ceiling are excluded from ingestion.
  • use_relative_paths (bool): Flag indicating whether dictionary keys should be normalized relative to directory (defaults to True) or maintained as absolute/raw filesystem paths.

Returns:

  • dict: A dictionary containing a single "files" key mapped to an inner dictionary {filepath: content}, where each path points to its decoded UTF-8 string payload.

Raises:

  • ValueError: Raised if the target directory argument does not exist or fails os.path.isdir().

Example:

files_data = crawl_local_files(
    "..",
    exclude_patterns={
        "*.pyc",
        "__pycache__/*",
        ".venv/*",
        ".git/*",
        "docs/*",
        "output/*",
    },
)

docs.title: Phase 1: Directory Validation and Gitignore Initialization
docs.text:
if not os.path.isdir(directory):
        raise ValueError(f"Directory does not exist: {directory}")

    files_dict = {}

    # --- Counters ---
    entry_num = 0
    count_processed = 0
    count_excluded = 0
    count_size_limit = 0
    count_non_text = 0
    skipped_size_limit = []
    skipped_non_text = []

    # --- Gitignore specs: {abs_dir_path: pathspec} ---
    gitignore_specs = {}
    root_gi_path = os.path.join(directory, ".gitignore")
    if os.path.exists(root_gi_path):
        spec = _load_gitignore(root_gi_path)
        if spec:
            gitignore_specs[os.path.abspath(directory)] = spec
            emit("CRAWL_GITIGNORE_LOADED", path=root_gi_path)

    # Translated reason strings (looked up once)
    reason_excluded = get("CRAWL_REASON_EXCLUDED")
    reason_gitignore = get("CRAWL_REASON_GITIGNORE")

The function begins by verifying that the target filesystem path points to an accessible directory; if not, it raises a ValueError immediately. It initializes tracking counters for crawl telemetry, empty lists for skipped items, and the main files_dict container. It then inspects the crawl root for an initial .gitignore file, parses it into a pathspec.PathSpec object mapped to the directory's absolute path, and retrieves localized rejection reason strings once via utils.output.get to avoid redundant dictionary lookups throughout the traversal.

docs.title: Phase 2: Directory Traversal and Pruning
docs.text:
# --- Single-pass: walk, filter, and process inline ---
    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(directory):
        abs_root = os.path.abspath(root)

        # Check for nested .gitignore in current directory (skip root, already loaded)
        if abs_root != os.path.abspath(directory):
            nested_gi = os.path.join(root, ".gitignore")
            if os.path.exists(nested_gi):
                spec = _load_gitignore(nested_gi)
                if spec:
                    gitignore_specs[abs_root] = spec

        # --- Directory filtering ---
        excluded_dirs = set()
        for d in sorted(dirs):
            abs_d = os.path.join(abs_root, d)
            dirpath_rel = os.path.relpath(abs_d, directory)

            reason = None
            if _matches_any_gitignore(gitignore_specs, abs_d, is_dir=True):
                reason = reason_gitignore
            elif exclude_patterns:
                for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                    dir_pattern = pattern.removesuffix("/*")
                    if fnmatch.fnmatch(dirpath_rel, dir_pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(d, dir_pattern):
                        reason = reason_excluded
                        break

            if reason:
                excluded_dirs.add(d)
                entry_num += 1
                count_excluded += 1
                emit("CRAWL_DIR_EXCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=dirpath_rel, reason=reason)

        for d in dirs.copy():
            if d in excluded_dirs:
                dirs.remove(d)

        # Sort remaining dirs for consistent traversal order
        dirs.sort()

The crawler initiates a single-pass os.walk through the filesystem hierarchy. At each traversed directory level, it detects and loads any nested .gitignore file into gitignore_specs to enforce scoped ignoring rules for child subtrees. Candidate child directories are evaluated against both loaded .gitignore specifications and user-supplied exclude_patterns. Any matched directory is pruned directly from dirs in-place using dirs.remove(d), which halts os.walk from descending into that entire filesystem subtree and conserves significant I/O and CPU cycles.

docs.title: Phase 3: File Filtering Chain
docs.text:
# --- File processing (inline, sorted) ---
        for filename in sorted(files):
            filepath = os.path.join(root, filename)
            abs_filepath = os.path.abspath(filepath)
            relpath = os.path.relpath(filepath, directory) if use_relative_paths else filepath
            entry_num += 1

            # Check gitignore (all levels)
            if _matches_any_gitignore(gitignore_specs, abs_filepath):
                count_excluded += 1
                emit("CRAWL_FILE_GITIGNORE", num=entry_num, path=relpath)
                continue

            # Check exclude patterns
            excluded = False
            if exclude_patterns:
                for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                    if fnmatch.fnmatch(relpath, pattern):
                        excluded = True
                        break
            if excluded:
                count_excluded += 1
                emit("CRAWL_FILE_EXCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=relpath)
                continue

            # Check include patterns
            if include_patterns:
                matched = False
                for pattern in include_patterns:
                    if fnmatch.fnmatch(relpath, pattern):
                        matched = True
                        break
                if not matched:
                    count_excluded += 1
                    emit("CRAWL_FILE_NOT_INCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=relpath)
                    continue

For every file located within an unpruned directory, the crawler executes an ordered filtering pipeline. Files are first matched against all active .gitignore rules across all hierarchy levels via _matches_any_gitignore(). If permitted, the relative file path is checked against the set of exclude_patterns using fnmatch.fnmatch. Finally, if include_patterns were explicitly configured, the path must positively match at least one pattern, or else it is rejected and tagged with a CRAWL_FILE_NOT_INCLUDED telemetry event.

docs.title: Phase 4: Content Reading and Encoding Normalization
docs.text:
# Check size limit
            if max_file_size and os.path.getsize(filepath) > max_file_size:
                count_size_limit += 1
                skipped_size_limit.append(relpath)
                size_kb = os.path.getsize(filepath) / 1024
                emit("CRAWL_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT", num=entry_num, path=relpath, size=f"{size_kb:.0f}")
                continue

            # Try to read as text
            try:
                with open(filepath, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                    content = f.read()
                files_dict[relpath] = content
                count_processed += 1
                emit("CRAWL_FILE_PROCESSED", num=entry_num, path=relpath)
            except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError):
                count_non_text += 1
                skipped_non_text.append(relpath)
                emit("CRAWL_FILE_NOT_TEXT", num=entry_num, path=relpath)
            except Exception as e:
                count_non_text += 1
                skipped_non_text.append(relpath)
                emit("CRAWL_FILE_ERROR", num=entry_num, path=relpath, error=e)

Files that survive the pattern filters undergo a byte-size check if max_file_size is specified; files exceeding the limit are skipped, and their size in kilobytes is reported. Surviving files are opened using utf-8-sig encoding, ensuring UTF-8 compatibility while transparently stripping leading Byte Order Marks. If the read operation triggers a UnicodeDecodeError or ValueError (indicating a binary file), or any other filesystem I/O exception, the file is safely caught, categorized as non-text, recorded in skipped_non_text, and omitted from files_dict.

docs.title: Phase 5: Telemetry Summary and Payload Return
docs.text:
# --- Summary ---
    total_fetched = count_processed + count_excluded + count_size_limit + count_non_text
    emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_HEADER")
    emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_TOTAL", count=total_fetched)
    emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_PROCESSED", count=count_processed)
    if count_excluded > 0:
        emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_EXCLUDED", count=count_excluded)
    if count_size_limit > 0:
        emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_SIZE_LIMIT", count=count_size_limit)
        for f in skipped_size_limit:
            emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_ITEM", name=f)
    if count_non_text > 0:
        emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_NON_TEXT", count=count_non_text)
        for f in skipped_non_text:
            emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_ITEM", name=f)

    return {"files": files_dict}

Once os.walk finishes traversing the filesystem tree, the crawler aggregates metric totals across processed, excluded, oversized, and non-text categories. It transmits structured telemetry events to utils.output.emit, itemizing skipped oversized files and unreadable binaries for pipeline audit logs. Finally, the collected in-memory dictionary containing relative paths mapped to decoded source strings is packaged into {"files": files_dict} and returned to the caller.

docs.title: _load_gitignore()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _load_gitignore(gitignore_path):

Description: Opens a specified .gitignore file using utf-8-sig encoding and compiles its rules into a pathspec.PathSpec instance utilizing the standard gitwildmatch pattern syntax. If the file cannot be opened or parsed due to permission errors or encoding issues, a warning log is transmitted through emit_raw, and the function returns None.

Parameters:

  • gitignore_path (str): Filesystem path pointing directly to a .gitignore file.

Returns:

  • pathspec.PathSpec | None: A compiled pattern matcher instance if successfully parsed, or None if an exception occurred.

Raises:

  • No exceptions are raised directly; all read and parsing errors are caught internally.

Example:

root_gi_path = os.path.join(directory, ".gitignore")
if os.path.exists(root_gi_path):
    spec = _load_gitignore(root_gi_path)
    if spec:
        gitignore_specs[os.path.abspath(directory)] = spec
        emit("CRAWL_GITIGNORE_LOADED", path=root_gi_path)

def _load_gitignore(gitignore_path):
    """Load a .gitignore file and return a PathSpec, or None on failure."""
    try:
        with open(gitignore_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
            return pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", f.readlines())
    except Exception as e:
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"Failed to load .gitignore at {gitignore_path}: {e}", dest="LOG")
        return None

The helper encapsulates file ingestion and pattern compilation for Git ignore rules. By parsing lines using pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", ...), it faithfully reproduces standard Git wildcard behavior (such as handling glob stars, leading slashes, and negation rules). Wrapping the entire operation in a defensive try...except block ensures that malformed or inaccessible .gitignore files log a diagnostic warning without aborting the parent crawl operation.

docs.title: _matches_any_gitignore()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _matches_any_gitignore(gitignore_specs, abs_path, is_dir=False):

Description: Determines whether an absolute filesystem path matches any active pathspec.PathSpec rule across loaded .gitignore instances. The evaluation calculates the candidate path relative to each .gitignore's containing directory, skipping specs that do not encompass the path's subtree. For directory evaluations, it ensures a trailing slash is appended to conform to Git wildcard directory syntax.

Parameters:

  • gitignore_specs (dict): Dictionary mapping absolute directory paths to their corresponding compiled pathspec.PathSpec objects.
  • abs_path (str): The absolute path of the file or directory being evaluated.
  • is_dir (bool): Optional boolean indicating whether the target path represents a directory (defaults to False).

Returns:

  • bool: True if the path matches at least one governing .gitignore rule; otherwise False.

Raises:

  • No exceptions are raised.

Example:

if _matches_any_gitignore(gitignore_specs, abs_d, is_dir=True):
    reason = reason_gitignore

def _matches_any_gitignore(gitignore_specs, abs_path, is_dir=False):
    """Check if a path matches ANY loaded .gitignore spec.

    Each spec is checked with the path relative to its own .gitignore directory.
    For directories, a trailing '/' is appended for proper gitignore matching.

    Args:
        gitignore_specs: dict of {abs_dir_path: pathspec.PathSpec}
        abs_path: absolute path of the file or directory to check
        is_dir: True if checking a directory
    Returns:
        True if the path matches any gitignore rule
    """
    for gi_dir, spec in gitignore_specs.items():
        rel = os.path.relpath(abs_path, gi_dir)
        # Skip if the path is not under this gitignore's scope
        if rel.startswith(".."):
            continue
        match_path = rel.replace("\\", "/")
        if is_dir:
            match_path = match_path.rstrip("/") + "/"
        if spec.match_file(match_path):
            return True
    return False

This function performs multi-level Gitignore resolution across hierarchical scopes. When checking a path, it calculates the relative path from each cached .gitignore directory using os.path.relpath. Any relative path prefixed with .. indicates that the target path lies outside that specific ignore file's subtree and is skipped immediately. Windows backslashes are normalized to forward slashes to guarantee cross-platform consistency with POSIX gitwildmatch rules, and directories have trailing slashes appended so that rules targeting directories specifically (e.g., build/) match correctly.

docs.title: Local crawler file results
docs.text:
The primary dictionary returned by crawl_local_files() provides downstream nodes with immediate access to in-memory file content mapped by normalized path keys.

Field Type Description files dict[str, str] Key-value store where each key is a file path (relative to the crawled root directory when use_relative_paths=True) and each value is the raw decoded file content as a string.

Example dictionary returned by crawl_local_files():

{
    "files": {
        "main.py": "import os\n\ndef run():\n    pass\n",
        "utils/files.py": "def read_file(path):\n    return open(path).read()\n",
    }
}

docs.title: Gitignore specification mapping
docs.text:
An internal mapping constructed dynamically during filesystem traversal to track active scoping rules across directory subtrees.

Key Type Description abs_dir_path str Absolute filesystem path of the directory containing the .gitignore file. spec pathspec.PathSpec Compiled pattern matcher configured with the gitwildmatch syntax for that specific directory subtree.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
• Root Directory Validation (ValueError): At invocation, crawl_local_files() checks os.path.isdir(directory). If the target does not exist or points to a non-directory file, a ValueError is raised immediately with the message f"Directory does not exist: {directory}".
  • Gitignore Parsing Tolerances (Exception): Inside _load_gitignore(), all filesystem I/O and syntax parsing failures are trapped by an untyped except Exception as e: block. The error is routed to logging via emit_raw("WARNING", ..., dest="LOG"), returning None so that invalid or locked ignore files do not interrupt the broader crawl.
  • Non-Text and Encoding Errors (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError): When reading file payloads, the crawler attempts decoding using utf-8-sig. If decoding fails due to binary content, invalid UTF-8 sequences, or embedded null characters, the exception is caught, the counter count_non_text is incremented, the path is appended to skipped_non_text, and a CRAWL_FILE_NOT_TEXT event is emitted.
  • Filesystem Read Faults (Exception): Any unexpected OS-level I/O faults during file reads (such as read permission denials or broken symlinks) are caught by an untyped except Exception as e: block. The crawler increments count_non_text, records the path, and logs the diagnostic event CRAWL_FILE_ERROR with the exception object.

docs.title: exclude_patterns.py
docs.text: Source: utils/exclude_patterns.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
utils/exclude_patterns.py defines the default baseline pattern set used by filesystem and repository crawling modules across the system, including crawl_local_files.py and crawl_github_files.py. The module centralizes file and directory exclusion rules into a single immutable configuration constant, DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS. During repository traversal, crawlers match discovered paths against these patterns to prevent ingestion of binary assets, compiled artifacts, third-party vendor directories, lockfiles, temporary files, and sensitive credentials.

The patterns rely on standard Unix shell-style glob syntax evaluated via fnmatch. Directory patterns terminate with a trailing wildcard suffix (/*), signaling to recursive crawlers (such as os.walk) that any directory matching the prefix should be pruned before descending into its subtree. File patterns leverage wildcard extension matching (such as *.png or *.pyc), exact basename matching (such as package-lock.json or .DS_Store), and depth-independent wildcard path prefixes (such as */.env or */id_rsa) to intercept files located at arbitrary filesystem depths.

Excluding irrelevant content at the ingestion boundary is essential for the documentation generation pipeline. Parsing binary media files or massive dependency trees (such as node_modules or Python virtual environments) causes excessive memory consumption, decoding failures, and token limit exhaustion when payloads are sent to Large Language Models (LLMs). Furthermore, the exclusion of cryptographic keys, environment variables, and SSH credentials prevents secrets from being cached on disk or transmitted across network boundaries to LLM inference providers.

docs.title: Default exclusion pattern set
docs.text:
The file defines DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS as a standard Python set[str]. Each element in the set represents a path or file pattern evaluated using fnmatch.fnmatch(). The set adheres to three structural conventions:

Pattern Category Syntax Pattern Matching Behavior Target Scope Directory Subtree directory_name/* Trailing wildcard indicating that any directory matching the prefix should be omitted, allowing crawlers to mutate dirnames in-place and skip subtrees. Top-level or nested directories (e.g., dist/*, venv/*, node_modules/*). Glob Extension *.extension Suffix wildcard matching any filename with the specified file extension, regardless of directory location. Binary assets, media files, compiled bytecode, libraries (e.g., *.png, *.pyc, *.dll). Basename Literal filename Exact match against the file basename; applies when the filename appears in any discovered path. Environment files, lockfiles, OS files (e.g., .env, .DS_Store, package-lock.json). Arbitrary Depth Wildcard */pattern Wildcard prefix matching files or directories located inside any parent directory. Nested secrets and credentials (e.g., */.env, */id_rsa, */id_ed25519).

The breakdown of patterns across the 7 functional categories defined in DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS is summarized below:

Category Index Category Description Representative Entries Primary Rationale 1 Media, Data, & Static Assets *.png, *.jpg, *.mp4, *.pdf, *.zip, assets/* Avoid binary decoding errors and unnecessary payload volume. 2 Build, Distribution, & Caches dist/*, build/*, target/*, .next/*, *.log Eliminate minified bundles, compiler targets, and non-source logs. 3 Environments, Lockfiles, & Secrets .env, */id_rsa, *.pem, node_modules/*, *.lock Prevent secret exfiltration and eliminate redundant lockfile token load. 4 Language-Specific Artifacts __pycache__/*, *.class, *.so, *.dylib, ios/Pods/* Exclude compiled platform-specific binaries and runtime caches. 5 OS & Version Control .git/*, .github/*, .svn/*, .DS_Store, Thumbs.db Skip VCS object databases and local OS file manager metadata. 6 Classic IDEs .vscode/*, .idea/*, *.iml, .eclipse/*, .vs/* Omit developer-specific workstation and project configuration files. 7 AI Agents & AI IDEs .cursor/*, .cursorrules, .windsurf/*, .cline/* Avoid prompt pollution or conflicting instructions from other AI agent frameworks.

docs.title: facts.py
docs.text: Source: utils/facts.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The utils/facts.py module implements deterministic, language-agnostic code fact verification across the repository. In the documentation generation pipeline, Large Language Models (LLMs) inspect repository files and emit structured assertions regarding symbols, module dependencies, configuration keys, and error conditions, accompanied by line-level quote evidence. Rather than employing language-specific Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) parsers, this module verifies whether LLM claims correspond verbatim to physical source lines, resolves their line boundaries, verifies lexical enclosing structures, and tracks module dependencies across multi-package projects.

Source files undergo text normalization and indexing via SourceIndex, which prepares Unicode NFC-normalized views, whitespace-collapsed single-line representations, fully squashed character offsets, and an inverted word-token line index. Quoted evidence is matched using a tiered search strategy: single-line collapsed string matching, multi-line squashed matching bounded by a line window, and ordered token subsequence searches. Symbols are bound to their declared parents by tracking hierarchical indentation blocks and container keywords across diverse programming language conventions.

For cross-module analysis, ModuleTable aggregates project manifests (such as package.json, Cargo.toml, or pom.xml), directory structures, and unique symbol ownership maps. It resolves raw import strings—including relative imports, path aliases, package barrel exports, and wildcard namespaces—against actual project files. The module enforces the strict "evidence rule": a claimed dependency is accepted only if the quoted line names the target module, references a path matching the module, or uses a symbol owned exclusively by that module.

docs.title: split_lines()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def split_lines(content: str) -> list[str]:

Description: Splits source code into line strings matching the line numbering semantics used by text editors, GitHub, and LLMs. Unlike Python's standard str.splitlines(), which breaks on form feeds (\f), vertical tabs (\v), and Unicode line break characters (U+2028), this function splits exclusively on carriage return (\r) and newline (\n) delimiters, preserving terminal empty lines without trailing newline artifacts.

Parameters:

  • content (str): Raw file content string.

Returns:

  • list[str]: A list of individual line strings.

Example:

lines = split_lines(_nfc(content))
view = code_view(lines)
imports = {n for n, line in enumerate(view) if import_statement_like(line)} | import_block_lines(view)

The function regularizes multi-platform line breaks (\r\n, \r, \n) into a predictable list of string lines. The final empty element produced by a trailing newline is trimmed to preserve exact 1-based editor line correspondences across downstream operations.

docs.title: SourceIndex
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: class SourceIndex:

Description: An in-memory search index built for a single source file. It normalizes text via Unicode NFC, maintains whitespace-collapsed and whitespace-free ("squashed") linear buffers with line-offset indexes, and indexes word tokens in an inverted map for multi-line and token-fallback matching.

docs.title: SourceIndex.__init__()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def __init__(self, content: str):

Description: Initializes the SourceIndex instance by splitting and normalizing content, calculating cumulative line offsets for exact and squashed buffers, and constructing inverted token indexes.

Parameters:

  • content (str): Raw source file content.

Returns:

  • None

Example:

def __init__(self, content: str):
    self.lines = split_lines(_nfc(content))
    self.collapsed = [_collapse(line) for line in self.lines]
    # Collapsed lines joined by "\n" (never inside a collapsed line or quote, so no match spans two lines)
    self.collapsed_text = "\n".join(self.collapsed) + "\n"
    self.collapsed_offsets = list(accumulate((len(line) + 1 for line in self.collapsed), initial=0))
    squashed = [_squash(line) for line in self.lines]
    # All lines without whitespace, back to back, with each line's start offset: one str.find per quote
    self.squashed_text = "".join(squashed)
    self.offsets = list(accumulate((len(line) for line in squashed), initial=0))
    self.words = [_words(line) for line in self.lines]
    self.word_sets = [set(words) for words in self.words]
    self.word_lines = defaultdict(list)  # word → lines it occurs on, for the token fallback
    for number, words in enumerate(self.word_sets):
        for word in words:
            self.word_lines[word].append(number)
    self._chains = None  # block_chain(), built on first use

The constructor computes cumulative length offsets using itertools.accumulate for both the whitespace-collapsed lines buffer (collapsed_offsets) and the whitespace-removed squashed buffer (offsets). It pre-tokenizes each line into word lists and populates word_lines, mapping every token to the list of line indices where it appears. Block hierarchy chains (self._chains) are initialized as None and lazily calculated when requested.

docs.title: SourceIndex.block_chain()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def block_chain(self, line: int) -> tuple:

Description: Returns the chain of enclosing lexical blocks surrounding a given line, ordered from innermost enclosing block to outermost.

Parameters:

  • line (int): 0-based index of the line.

Returns:

  • tuple: A tuple of tuples, where each entry represents (indent, text, kind, named).

Example:

def block_chain(self, line: int) -> tuple:
    """The blocks *line* sits in, innermost first: ``(indent, text, kind, named)`` per enclosing line
    (``_block_chains``)."""
    if self._chains is None:
        self._chains = _block_chains(self.lines)
    return self._chains[line]

This method delegates to _block_chains upon its first invocation to build an indentation-aware stack of enclosing scopes across all lines in the file. Results are cached on self._chains to optimize repeated lookups during parent-symbol resolution.

docs.title: SourceIndex.text()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def text(self, first: int, last: int) -> str:

Description: Returns the raw source text spanning lines from first to last (inclusive), joined by newline characters.

Parameters:

  • first (int): 0-based starting line index.
  • last (int): 0-based ending line index.

Returns:

  • str: The un-collapsed, raw source lines joined by \n.

Example:

def text(self, first: int, last: int) -> str:
    return "\n".join(self.lines[first : last + 1])

The method slices the underlying pre-split self.lines list from index first through last + 1 and joins them with standard newline delimiters. It preserves original indentation and source character formatting.

docs.title: SourceIndex.locate()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def locate(self, quote, start: int = 0, end: int | None = None) -> list[tuple[int, int, str]]:

Description: Finds 0-based line ranges matching a target quote within the line window between start and end. Executes a three-tiered fallback search: exact single-line collapsed matching, multi-line squashed matching within a sliding window, and ordered token sequence matching.

Parameters:

  • quote (Any): The search string or object convertible to string representing the quote evidence.
  • start (int): 0-based line index at which to begin searching. Defaults to 0.
  • end (int | None): 0-based line index upper boundary. Defaults to None (searches to end of file).

Returns:

  • list[tuple[int, int, str]]: A list of matches formatted as (first_line, last_line, match_mode), where match_mode is "exact", "joined", or "tokens".

Example:

end = len(self.lines) if end is None else min(end, len(self.lines))
collapsed = _collapse(quote)
if not collapsed or start >= end:
    return []
exact = []
pos = self.collapsed_text.find(collapsed, self.collapsed_offsets[start])
while 0 <= pos < self.collapsed_offsets[end]:
    line = bisect_right(self.collapsed_offsets, pos) - 1
    exact.append((line, line, "exact"))
    pos = self.collapsed_text.find(collapsed, self.collapsed_offsets[line + 1])  # next line: one hit per line
if exact:
    return exact
# ...

The matching hierarchy begins with single-line collapsed string matching against collapsed_text. Binary search via bisect_right resolves character positions to line indices. If no exact match occurs, it searches squashed_text for joined multi-line matches spanning at most window lines. If joined matching fails, it evaluates ordered word tokens using the rarest token in word_lines as a search anchor.

docs.title: SourceIndex.excerpt()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def excerpt(self, first: int, last: int, quote) -> tuple[str, bool]:

Description: Extracts a representative snippet of source code spanning lines first through last, capped at _EXCERPT (300) characters. If the snippet exceeds this threshold, it centers a 300-character window around the matched quote.

Parameters:

  • first (int): 0-based starting line index.
  • last (int): 0-based ending line index.
  • quote (Any): The quote string to center around if truncation is required.

Returns:

  • tuple[str, bool]: A tuple containing (excerpt_text, is_truncated).

Example:

def excerpt(self, first: int, last: int, quote) -> tuple[str, bool]:
    text = self.text(first, last).strip()
    if len(text) <= _EXCERPT:
        return text, False
    flat, wanted = _collapse(text), _collapse(quote)
    pos = max(flat.find(wanted), 0)
    start = max(0, min(pos - max(0, (_EXCERPT - len(wanted)) // 2), len(flat) - _EXCERPT))
    return flat[start : start + _EXCERPT], True

The method retrieves the raw text slice between first and last. When the length is within 300 characters, it returns the text unmodified with False. For longer text, it collapses whitespace and calculates an excerpt window centered on the target quote, returning the 300-character slice marked as True for truncation.

docs.title: verify_file_claims()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def verify_file_claims(claims: dict, content: str) -> dict:

Description: Audits LLM-extracted claims for a single file against its source content. Verifies symbols, dependencies, configuration keys, and errors, calculating physical 1-based line numbers, multi-line spans, excerpt strings, and error handling roles.

docs.title: Phase 1: Symbol Verification and Top-level Resolution
docs.text:
index = SourceIndex(content)
result = {key: [] for key in CLAIM_KEYS}
rejected = []
claimed = 0
unparsed = claims.get("unparsed", 0) if isinstance(claims, dict) and isinstance(claims.get("unparsed"), int) else 0
if unparsed:
    claimed += unparsed
    rejected.extend({"kind": "unparsed", "reason": "reply item that is not valid YAML"} for _ in range(unparsed))

symbols = _claim_list(claims, "symbols")
claimed += len(symbols)
kept, symbol_rejects = _verify_symbols(symbols, index)
result["symbols"] = kept
rejected += symbol_rejects

The function constructs a SourceIndex over the file content. Any pre-flagged unparsed YAML reply items are counted toward total claims and directly appended to the rejected queue. Symbol claims are extracted and processed via _verify_symbols, which establishes parent-child relationships and checks signatures.

docs.title: Phase 2: Dependency Evidence Matching
docs.text:
for item in _claim_list(claims, "dependencies"):
    claimed += 1
    target, evidence = _as_text(item.get("target")).strip(), _as_text(item.get("evidence"))
    matches = index.locate(evidence) if target else []
    if not matches:
        rejected.append({"kind": "dependency", "target": target, "evidence": evidence, "reason": "evidence not in source"})
        continue
    first, last, how = matches[0]
    text, truncated = index.excerpt(first, last, evidence)
    entry = {"target": target, "line": first + 1, **_end(first, last), "evidence": text, "match": how}
    result["dependencies"].append({**entry, "truncated": True} if truncated else entry)

Each dependency claim is checked by searching for its evidence quote in the SourceIndex. If the quote cannot be located in the file, the dependency claim is rejected. When located, the entry records 1-based line numbers, matching technique (exact, joined, or tokens), and excerpted evidence text.

docs.title: Phase 3: Configuration and Error Span Extension
docs.text:
for key in ("config", "errors"):
    for item in _claim_list(claims, key):
        claimed += 1
        name, evidence = _as_text(item.get("name")).strip(), _as_text(item.get("evidence"))
        matches = []
        for first, last, how in index.locate(evidence) if name else []:
            if _names_in(index.text(first, last), name):
                matches.append((first, last, how, False))
                continue
            end = _call_span(index, first, last)
            if end > last and _names_in(index.text(first, end), name):
                matches.append((first, end, how, True))
        if not matches:
            rejected.append({"kind": key, "name": name, "evidence": evidence, "reason": "name/evidence not in source"})
            continue
        roles = {m: _error_role(index, m[0], m[1], name) for m in matches} if key == "errors" else {}
        matches.sort(key=lambda m: (_ROLE_RANK.get(roles.get(m), 0), _name_rank(index.text(m[0], m[1]), name), m[3]))
        first, last, how, extended = matches[0]
        # ...

Config keys and error claims are matched against the index. If an evidence quote begins a multi-line function call (such as argparse.add_argument() but the argument name appears on a subsequent line, _call_span extends the line boundary. For error claims, _error_role inspects surrounding keywords to classify the error as raised, caught, or mentioned.

docs.title: Phase 4: Fact Deduplication and Span Narrowing
docs.text:
for key, fields in (("symbols", ("parent", "name")), ("dependencies", ("target",)), ("config", ("name",)), ("errors", ("name",))):
    seen, unique = set(), []
    for entry in result[key]:
        marker = (*(entry.get(field) for field in fields), entry["line"])
        if marker not in seen:
            seen.add(marker)
            unique.append(entry)
    if key in ("config", "errors"):
        narrow_first = sorted(unique, key=lambda e: e.get("end_line", e["line"]) - e["line"])
        kept_spans = []
        for entry in narrow_first:
            low, high = entry["line"], entry.get("end_line", entry["line"])
            if not any(other["name"] == entry["name"] and low <= other["line"] <= high for other in kept_spans):
                kept_spans.append(entry)
        unique = [entry for entry in unique if any(entry is other for other in kept_spans)]
    claimed -= len(result[key]) - len(unique)
    result[key] = unique
result["rejected"] = rejected
result["claimed"] = claimed
result["found"] = claimed - len(rejected)
return result

Duplicate claims sharing identical identities and start lines are pruned. For configuration and error items where overlapping matches occur across expanded and unexpanded spans, the narrowest line span is preserved. The final dictionary reports verified claims, rejected claims with diagnostic reasons, total claimed items, and confirmed items found.

Parameters:

  • claims (dict): Raw dictionary of claims returned by an LLM prompt.
  • content (str): Decoded source file text.

Returns:

  • dict: Verified claims dictionary structured with keys symbols, dependencies, config, errors, rejected, claimed, and found.

docs.title: code_view()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def code_view(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:

Description: Returns a sanitized view of the source lines with comments, docstrings, and multi-line string literals blanked out while preserving exact line numbers and column alignments. Skips globs such as lib/*.sh and ensures block comments are correctly paired.

Parameters:

  • lines (list[str]): List of raw source lines.

Returns:

  • list[str]: Sanitized lines where comments and block strings are replaced with whitespace or empty quotes.

Example:

lines = split_lines(_nfc(content))
view = code_view(lines)
imports = {n for n, line in enumerate(view) if import_statement_like(line)} | import_block_lines(view)

The function executes a reverse scan to index the terminal positions of block comment closers (*/, """, '''). It then performs a single-pass tokenization across lines, removing single-line comments (#, //, --) and replacing block comments/docstrings with spaces or empty strings. This prevents false positives when scanning code for declarations and import statements.

docs.title: declaration_like()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def declaration_like(line: str) -> bool:

Description: Language-agnostic heuristic that determines whether a source line represents an identifiable top-level or member declaration (e.g., class, function, struct, interface, type alias, constant).

Parameters:

  • line (str): A single line of code.

Returns:

  • bool: True if the line matches structural declaration patterns, otherwise False.

Example:

declarations = {n for n, line in enumerate(view) if n not in imports and enclosing[n] != "function" and declaration_like(line)}

The function strips leading modifiers and annotations before checking for keywords in _DECLARATION_WORDS, _TOP_LEVEL_WORDS, SQL CREATE patterns, Haskell type signatures, C/C++ return type patterns, and upper-case constant assignments. It filters out control flow constructs (if, for, while) and call sites that accept callbacks.

docs.title: import_statement_like()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def import_statement_like(line: str) -> bool:

Description: Determines whether a source line is an import statement. Handles diverse language conventions including Python (import, from ... import), JavaScript/TypeScript (import, require()), C/C++ (#include), Go (import), Rust (use, mod), Ruby (require), and Shell (. path/to/env).

Parameters:

  • line (str): A single line of code.

Returns:

  • bool: True if the line behaves as a module import statement, otherwise False.

Example:

if any(import_statement_like(line) or _GO_BLOCK_LINE_RE.match(line) for line in lines) or re.search(rf"[\"'`<]{quoted}[\"'`>]", evidence):
    return True

The function ignores comments, assignments (e.g., source = value), and call sites containing inline imports inside string literals. It verifies that leading words match _IMPORT_WORDS and validates that following tokens represent module specifiers rather than arithmetic operators or prose punctuation.

docs.title: import_block_lines()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def import_block_lines(lines: list[str]) -> set[int]:

Description: Detects 0-based line indices that reside inside Go-style multi-line import ( ... ) blocks, where package paths are listed as bare quoted strings without repeating the import keyword.

Parameters:

  • lines (list[str]): List of code lines (typically pre-filtered via code_view).

Returns:

  • set[int]: Set of 0-based line numbers corresponding to lines within an import block.

Example:

lines = code_view(split_lines(_nfc(content)))
block = import_block_lines(lines)
for number, line in enumerate(lines):
    if not (import_statement_like(line) or number in block):
        continue

The function maintains an inside state flag, toggled on when encountering ^import\s*\($ and toggled off upon reaching ^). Lines inside the block that match _GO_BLOCK_LINE_RE (bare or aliased quoted strings) are collected into the returned set.

docs.title: enclosing_blocks()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def enclosing_blocks(lines: list[str]) -> list[str | None]:

Description: Analyzes indentation hierarchy to classify the enclosing block kind for every line. Identifies whether a line sits inside a function, container (class/struct/module), or at the top level (None).

Parameters:

  • lines (list[str]): List of code lines.

Returns:

  • list[str | None]: A list parallel to lines indicating the block kind of each line's parent scope.

Example:

enclosing = enclosing_blocks(view)
declarations = {n for n, line in enumerate(view) if n not in imports and enclosing[n] != "function" and declaration_like(line)}

The function tracks an indentation stack of (indent, kind) tuples. For each line, the stack is popped until the top element's indentation is strictly less than the current line's indentation. The nearest non-control ancestor block is assigned as the enclosing block kind.

docs.title: completeness_hints()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def completeness_hints(content: str, checked: dict, claims: dict | None = None) -> dict:

Description: Identifies source lines that appear to contain declarations or import statements but were omitted from LLM claims. Serves as a diagnostic recall mechanism to prompt follow-up extraction passes.

Parameters:

  • content (str): Raw file content.
  • checked (dict): The verified claims dictionary returned by verify_file_claims.
  • claims (dict | None): Optional raw LLM claims to credit repeated evidence across calls.

Returns:

  • dict: Dictionary with 1-based line lists: {"import_lines", "declaration_lines", "uncovered"}.

Example:

def completeness_hints(content: str, checked: dict, claims: dict | None = None) -> dict:
    lines = split_lines(_nfc(content))
    view = code_view(lines)
    imports = {n for n, line in enumerate(view) if import_statement_like(line)} | import_block_lines(view)
    enclosing = enclosing_blocks(view)
    declarations = {n for n, line in enumerate(view) if n not in imports and enclosing[n] != "function" and declaration_like(line)}

    import_numbers, import_texts = set(), set()
    for entry in checked.get("dependencies", []):
        span = range(entry["line"] - 1, entry.get("end_line", entry["line"]))
        import_numbers.update(span)
        import_texts.update(_collapse(lines[n]) for n in span if n < len(lines))
    # ...

The function computes all potential import lines and declaration lines outside function bodies using code_view and enclosing_blocks. It aggregates all lines covered by verified symbol and dependency spans. The set difference between detected structural lines and covered lines is returned as uncovered.

docs.title: unexplained_names()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def unexplained_names(content: str, source_path: str, depends_on: list[dict], table) -> list[dict]:

Description: Detects symbols defined exclusively by exactly one other module in the project and referenced in the current file without an explicit import statement or verified dependency edge.

Parameters:

  • content (str): Source code of the file.
  • source_path (str): Relative repository path of the current file.
  • depends_on (list[dict]): List of verified dependency edges for this file.
  • table (ModuleTable): Global module resolution table.

Returns:

  • list[dict]: List of missing dependency records: [{"name": symbol_name, "module": module_path}].

Example:

def unexplained_names(content: str, source_path: str, depends_on: list[dict], table) -> list[dict]:
    # ...
    linked = {edge["module"] for edge in depends_on}
    own = table.all_symbols.get(source_path, set())
    found = []
    for name, module in sorted(table.symbol_owner.items()):
        hit = (name in dotted or name.split(".")[-1] in used) if "." in name else name in used
        if module != source_path and module not in linked and name not in own and name not in bound and hit:
            found.append({"name": name, "module": module})
    return found

The function extracts code tokens while discarding comments and string literals (retaining string interpolations and environment variables). It subtracts names bound locally via variable declarations, loop targets, assignments, or keyword arguments. Any remaining name matching table.symbol_owner whose owning module is not linked in depends_on is flagged.

docs.title: merge_claims()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def merge_claims(first: dict, second: dict) -> dict:

Description: Merges two dictionaries of claims (such as an initial extraction pass and a completeness follow-up pass), deduplicating items based on composite identity keys.

Parameters:

  • first (dict): Initial claims dictionary.
  • second (dict): Secondary or follow-up claims dictionary.

Returns:

  • dict: Unified claims dictionary with deduplicated fact entries and combined unparsed counts.

Example:

def merge_claims(first: dict, second: dict) -> dict:
    merged = {}
    for key in CLAIM_KEYS:
        seen, items = set(), []
        for item in [*_claim_list(first or {}, key), *_claim_list(second or {}, key)]:
            marker = tuple(_collapse(_as_text(item.get(field))) for field in _IDENTITY_FIELDS[key])
            if marker not in seen:
                seen.add(marker)
                items.append(item)
        merged[key] = items
    merged["unparsed"] = (first or {}).get("unparsed", 0) + (second or {}).get("unparsed", 0)
    return merged

The function iterates over each category in CLAIM_KEYS and builds identity marker tuples derived from _IDENTITY_FIELDS (e.g., (parent, name, signature) for symbols). When duplicates are encountered, the entry from the earlier pass is preserved.

docs.title: normalize_name()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def normalize_name(text: str) -> str:

Description: Normalizes package, crate, and module names for canonical comparison across different ecosystems by case-folding and replacing hyphens with underscores.

Parameters:

  • text (str): Raw name string (e.g., "shop-core").

Returns:

  • str: Normalized name string (e.g., "shop_core").

Example:

def normalize_name(text: str) -> str:
    """Case-folded, ``-`` as ``_``: package, crate and distribution names compare equal across spellings
    (``shop-core`` in Cargo.toml, ``shop_core`` in ``use shop_core::store``)."""
    return _nfc(text).strip().casefold().replace("-", "_")

The normalization applies Unicode NFC composition, strips bounding whitespace, case-folds ASCII and Unicode characters, and maps - to _. This guarantees that Cargo packages, Python distribution names, and Go packages match import specifiers consistently.

docs.title: verify_manifest_claims()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def verify_manifest_claims(claims: dict, content: str, manifest_path: str) -> dict:

Description: Audits LLM-extracted provides and aliases claims from project manifest files against actual manifest file contents.

Parameters:

  • claims (dict): Manifest claims returned by LLMs.
  • content (str): Raw text of the manifest file.
  • manifest_path (str): Relative repository path to the manifest file.

Returns:

  • dict: Verification results dictionary containing provides, aliases, rejected, claimed, and found.

Example:

for item in _claim_list(claims, "provides"):
    claimed += 1
    name, evidence = _as_text(item.get("name")).strip(), _as_text(item.get("evidence"))
    matches = [m for m in (index.locate(evidence) if name else []) if _collapse(name) in _collapse(index.text(m[0], m[1]))]
    if not matches:
        result["rejected"].append({"kind": "provides", "name": name, "evidence": evidence, "reason": "name/evidence not in the manifest"})
        continue
    line = _collapse(index.text(matches[0][0], matches[0][1]))
    if not _declares_name(line, name):
        result["rejected"].append(
            {"kind": "provides", "name": name, "evidence": evidence, "reason": "the line does not declare the name (a dependency?)"}
        )
        continue
    # ...

The function searches for package names and path aliases within the manifest content. It calls _declares_name to ensure that a claimed package name represents an actual project identifier declaration (e.g., "name": "my-pkg") rather than an external dependency specification (e.g., "dependencies": { "my-pkg": "^1.0" }).

docs.title: manifest_rules()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def manifest_rules(manifests: dict) -> tuple[list, list]:

Description: Transforms verified manifest claims across the project into normalized package descriptors and path alias rules for ModuleTable.

Parameters:

  • manifests (dict): Mapping of manifest paths to their verify_manifest_claims outputs.

Returns:

  • tuple[list, list]: A tuple (packages, aliases) where packages are sorted with longest segment counts first.

Example:

def manifest_rules(manifests: dict) -> tuple[list, list]:
    packages, aliases = [], []
    for path, verified in (manifests or {}).items():
        directory = posixpath.dirname(path)
        for provided in verified.get("provides", []):
            if "*" in provided["name"]:
                continue
            entry = provided.get("entry")
            entry_path = posixpath.normpath(posixpath.join(directory, entry)) if entry else None
            packages.append({"segments": _name_segments(provided["name"]), "name": provided["name"], "dir": directory, "entry": entry_path})
        # ...
    packages.sort(key=lambda package: -len(package["segments"]))
    return packages, aliases

The function iterates over verified manifest records, normalizes directory paths via posixpath, and determines whether aliases represent wildcard (star), prefix, or exact path substitutions. Package descriptors include parsed path segments and optional root entrypoint files.

docs.title: ModuleTable
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: class ModuleTable:

Description: Central repository index coordinating module resolution. Maintains documented file paths, directory memberships, manifest package rules, path aliases, and unique symbol ownership maps.

docs.title: ModuleTable.__init__()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def __init__(self, paths: list[str], symbols_by_path: dict, contents: dict | None = None, manifests: dict | None = None):

Description: Constructs the ModuleTable index by compiling symbol ownership, directory listings, and manifest rules.

Parameters:

  • paths (list[str]): List of all documented relative module file paths.
  • symbols_by_path (dict): Dictionary mapping file paths to lists of verified symbol records.
  • contents (dict | None): Optional dictionary mapping file paths to raw source strings.
  • manifests (dict | None): Optional dictionary mapping manifest paths to verified manifest data.

Returns:

  • None

Example:

def __init__(self, paths: list[str], symbols_by_path: dict, contents: dict | None = None, manifests: dict | None = None):
    self.paths = list(paths)
    self.contents = contents or {}
    self.packages, self.aliases = manifest_rules(manifests)
    self.segments = {path: _segments(path) for path in self.paths}
    self.extensions = {os.path.splitext(path)[1] for path in self.paths if os.path.splitext(path)[1]}
    self.by_dir = defaultdict(list)
    for path in self.paths:
        self.by_dir[posixpath.dirname(path)].append(path)
    owners = defaultdict(set)
    self.top_symbols, self.all_symbols = {}, {}
    for path, symbols in symbols_by_path.items():
        self.all_symbols[path] = {symbol["name"] for symbol in symbols}
        self.top_symbols[path] = {symbol["name"] for symbol in symbols if symbol.get("kind") not in _OWNER_EXCLUDED_KINDS}
        for name in self.top_symbols[path]:
            if len(name) >= 3:
                owners[name].add(path)
    self.symbol_owner = {name: next(iter(paths)) for name, paths in owners.items() if len(paths) == 1}
    self.owned = defaultdict(set)
    for name, path in self.symbol_owner.items():
        self.owned[path].add(name)
    for package in self.packages:
        package["extensions"] = {os.path.splitext(path)[1] for path in self.paths if not package["dir"] or path.startswith(package["dir"] + "/")}

The constructor maps directory trees in self.by_dir and parses file extension sets. It filters out generic methods (_OWNER_EXCLUDED_KINDS) to prevent common verbs like get or to_h from falsely claiming file ownership. If a symbol with 3 or more characters is defined in exactly one module across the repository, symbol_owner maps that symbol directly to its owning module path.

docs.title: ModuleTable.normalize()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def normalize(self, target: str) -> tuple[list[str], str]:

Description: Deconstructs raw import target strings (e.g., utils.output, crate::store::Repo, @/http, net/socket.h) into clean segment lists and recognized file extensions.

Parameters:

  • target (str): Import specifier string.

Returns:

  • tuple[list[str], str]: A tuple (segments, extension).

Example:

def normalize(self, target: str) -> tuple[list[str], str]:
    text = target.strip().strip("\"'`<>()[];,")
    for prefix in ("@/", "~/", "$/"):
        text = text.removeprefix(prefix)
    ext = os.path.splitext(text)[1]
    if ext in self.extensions:
        text = text[: -len(ext)]
    else:
        ext = ""
    text = text.replace("::", "/").replace("\\", "/").replace(".", "/")
    parts = [part.strip() for part in text.split("/")]
    return [part for part in parts if part and part not in ("*", "crate", "super", "self") and _SEGMENT_RE.match(part)], ext

The method strips string delimiters and framework alias prefixes (@/, ~/). It checks whether the target ends with a file extension recognized in self.extensions. Path separators, namespace colons (::), backslashes, and dots are converted to forward slashes, filtering out syntax keywords such as self or super.

docs.title: ModuleTable.resolve_manifest()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def resolve_manifest(self, target: str, source_path: str, source_words: set, prefer_local: bool = False) -> tuple[list[str], str] | None:

Description: Resolves an import target that references a manifest-defined package name or path alias against the module index.

docs.title: Phase 1: Target Normalization and Local Preference Check
docs.text:
text = re.sub(r"^[A-Za-z][\w+.-]*:(?![/:\\])", "", target.strip().strip("\"'`<>()[];,"))
if not text or text.startswith(("./", "../", ".\\", "..\\")) or re.match(r"^\.+\w", text):
    return None
written = [part for part in re.split(r"::|[./\\:]+", _nfc(text).strip()) if part]
source_dir = posixpath.dirname(source_path)
if prefer_local and len(written) == 1 and self._resolve_rooted(posixpath.join(source_dir, written[0]), source_path, source_words):
    return None

URI schemes (node:, package:, jsr:) and file-relative dot notations are stripped or bypassed. If prefer_local is enabled and a single segment matches an adjacent local file, manifest resolution yields to relative resolution.

docs.title: Phase 2: Alias Matching and Template Expansion
docs.text:
in_scope = [alias for alias in self.aliases if not alias["dir"] or source_path.startswith(alias["dir"] + "/")]
for alias in sorted(in_scope, key=lambda alias: (-alias["dir"].count("/") - bool(alias["dir"]), -len(alias["prefix"]))):
    prefix, template, mode = alias["prefix"], alias["template"], alias["mode"]
    if mode == "exact":
        if text != prefix and not text.startswith(prefix + "/"):
            continue
        rest = text[len(prefix) :].lstrip("/")
    elif not text.startswith(prefix):
        continue
    else:
        rest = text[len(prefix) :]
    if "*" in template:
        base = posixpath.normpath(template.replace("*", rest, 1))
    else:
        base = posixpath.normpath(posixpath.join(template, rest)) if rest else template
    resolved = self._resolve_rooted(base, source_path, source_words)
    if resolved:
        return resolved[0], prefix

Applicable aliases declared in the current or ancestor directory are evaluated in order of path depth and prefix length. If an alias matches, the template is expanded and resolved via _resolve_rooted.

docs.title: Phase 3: Package Matching and In-Package Resolution
docs.text:
segments = _name_segments(text)
extension = os.path.splitext(source_path)[1]
for package in self.packages:
    if package["segments"] and segments[: len(package["segments"])] == package["segments"] and extension in package["extensions"]:
        found = self._resolve_in_package(package, written[len(package["segments"]) :], source_path, source_words)
        if found:
            return found, package["name"]

If the specifier begins with a declared package name segment and matches the language's expected extension, resolution delegates to _resolve_in_package to locate entry files or sub-modules.

docs.title: Phase 4: Sibling and External Heuristic Evaluation
docs.text:
if len(segments) > 1 and any(len(p["segments"]) > 1 and p["segments"][0] == segments[0] for p in self.packages):
    if self.namespace_members(text, source_path, source_words) or self._matches_whole(text, source_path):
        return None  # a sibling namespace or module of the same organization that no manifest declares
    return [], ""
if (self.packages or self.aliases) and text[:1] in ("@", "#", "~", "$"):  # a scoped or aliased name nothing declares
    return [], ""
return None

Multi-part targets that share an organization scope with a known package but resolve to no known module are categorized as external imports (([], "")). Undeclared scoped sigils (@, #) are similarly marked external.

Parameters:

  • target (str): Import specifier string.
  • source_path (str): Relative path of the importing file.
  • source_words (set): Pre-tokenized word set of the importing file.
  • prefer_local (bool): When True, prioritizes adjacent sibling files over packages.

Returns:

  • tuple[list[str], str] | None: (resolved_module_paths, matched_prefix) or None.

docs.title: ModuleTable.resolve()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def resolve(self, target: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> tuple[list[str], str]:

Description: Resolves any arbitrary import specifier string to a list of project module paths.

docs.title: Phase 1: Relative Import Resolution
docs.text:
relative = self._resolve_relative(target, source_path, source_words)
if relative is not None:
    return relative

If the target begins with relative dot notation (./, ../) or Rust's super::, _resolve_relative evaluates it against the source file's directory.

docs.title: Phase 2: Suffix and Directory Matching
docs.text:
parts, ext = self.normalize(target)
for size in range(len(parts), 0, -1):
    tail = parts[-size:]
    hits = self._suffix_hits(tail, ext, source_path)
    if len(hits) == 1:
        return (hits, "path") if self._corroborated(target, parts, size, hits[0], source_path, source_words) else ([], "external")
    if hits:
        return [], "ambiguous"
    dirs = [d for d in self.by_dir if d and d.split("/")[-size:] == tail]
    if len(dirs) == 1:
        members = [path for path in self.by_dir[dirs[0]] if path != source_path]
        index_file = self._index_file(dirs[0])  # mod http; / import pkg / require('./lib') mean it too
        used = [path for path in members if path == index_file or self.used_names(path, source_path, source_words)]
        if used:
            return used, "package"

The normalized segment list is matched from longest suffix to shortest against module paths (_suffix_hits) and known directories (self.by_dir). Single matches must pass corroboration checks (_corroborated) to prevent accidental partial path collisions.

docs.title: Phase 3: Owned Symbol Fallback
docs.text:
if parts and parts[-1] in self.symbol_owner and self.symbol_owner[parts[-1]] != source_path:
    return [self.symbol_owner[parts[-1]]], "symbol"
return [], "external"

If path matching yields no candidates, the terminal segment is checked against self.symbol_owner. If that name is uniquely defined in one module across the repository, that module is returned with resolution mode "symbol".

Parameters:

  • target (str): Raw import specifier.
  • source_path (str): Repository path of the importing file.
  • source_words (set): Word tokens found in the source file.

Returns:

  • tuple[list[str], str]: A tuple containing (paths, how), where how is "path", "package", "symbol", "ambiguous", or "external".

docs.title: ModuleTable.used_names()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def used_names(self, path: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> set:

Description: Identifies non-method symbols defined by path that appear within source_words and are not declared by source_path itself.

Parameters:

  • path (str): Target module path.
  • source_path (str): Importing module path.
  • source_words (set): Word tokens of the importing module.

Returns:

  • set: Set of symbol names owned by path and referenced in source_words.

Example:

def used_names(self, path: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> set:
    names = self.top_symbols.get(path, set()) - self.all_symbols.get(source_path, set())
    return {name for name in names if name in source_words or name.split(".")[-1] in source_words}

This method filters out symbols defined locally in source_path. It matches remaining symbols against the token set source_words, checking both full names and the terminal segments of dotted names.

docs.title: ModuleTable.namespace_members()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def namespace_members(self, target: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> list[str]:

Description: Resolves namespace wildcard import statements (such as C# using Acme.Accounting;) that do not directly correspond to filesystem directory structures.

Parameters:

  • target (str): Namespace specifier.
  • source_path (str): Importing source path.
  • source_words (set): Tokens found in the importing file.

Returns:

  • list[str]: List of module paths that declare the target namespace and export symbols utilized by source_path.

Example:

def namespace_members(self, target: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> list[str]:
    name = target.strip().strip("\"'`<>()[];,").removesuffix(".*").removesuffix("::*")
    if len(re.split(r"::|[./\\]", name)) < 2:
        return []
    return [
        path
        for path in self.paths
        if path != source_path
        and declares_namespace(self.contents.get(path, ""), name)
        and self.used_names(path, source_path, source_words) & self.owned[path]
    ]

The method removes wildcard suffixes (.*, ::*) and iterates over all project paths. Modules that explicitly declare the namespace via declares_namespace and define at least one uniquely owned symbol used by the calling source are returned.

docs.title: evidence_names_module()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def evidence_names_module( evidence: str, target_path: str, source_path: str, table: ModuleTable, how: str, relative_style: bool = False, per_line: bool = False ) -> bool:

Description: Evaluates the core "evidence rule": verifies whether a quoted evidence line explicitly refers to the resolved module path via a path string, import keyword, uniquely owned symbol, directory name, or declared namespace.

Parameters:

  • evidence (str): The quoted source line(s) asserting the dependency.
  • target_path (str): Resolved candidate module path.
  • source_path (str): Path of the importing module.
  • table (ModuleTable): Global module index.
  • how (str): Resolution mode ("path", "package", "symbol", "namespace").
  • relative_style (bool): True if relative path imports are standard for this language.
  • per_line (bool): True if multi-line token matches require per-line validation.

Returns:

  • bool: True if the evidence confirms the dependency, otherwise False.

Example:

words = set(_words(evidence))
checked = re.sub(r"[\"'`][\w-]+[\"'`]", " ", evidence) if relative_style else evidence
name = target_path.split("/")[-2] if how == "package" and "/" in target_path else _stem(target_path)
extension = "" if how == "package" else os.path.splitext(target_path)[1]
lines = split_lines(checked) if per_line else [checked]
word_clause = not relative_style and any(
    _import_like(line) and _plain_occurrence(_without_bindings(line), name, extension, table.extensions) for line in lines
)
if name in set(_words(checked)) and (_names_path(checked, name, extension, table.extensions) or word_clause):
    return True
# ...

The evidence rule prevents hallucinated dependencies. In languages adhering to relative import conventions (e.g., JavaScript), bare quoted strings are stripped to avoid matching external packages with similar names. A match is verified if the evidence includes the file stem as part of a path, quotes an import statement mentioning the file, uses an owned symbol, or references the parent directory in conjunction with an imported name.

docs.title: declares_namespace()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def declares_namespace(content: str, dotted: str) -> bool:

Description: Determines whether a file's content includes a formal namespace, module, or package declaration corresponding to dotted.

Parameters:

  • content (str): Raw file content.
  • dotted (str): Dotted or segmented namespace name (e.g., "Acme.Accounting").

Returns:

  • bool: True if a matching declaration line exists, otherwise False.

Example:

def declares_namespace(content: str, dotted: str) -> bool:
    for line in split_lines(content):
        words = _words(line)
        if words and words[0] in _NAMESPACE_WORDS and dotted in line:
            return True
    return False

The function scans each line of the file. If the first word matches _NAMESPACE_WORDS (such as namespace, package, defmodule, or module) and dotted is a substring of the line, it returns True.

docs.title: scan_import_candidates()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def scan_import_candidates(content: str, source_path: str, table: ModuleTable, relative_style: bool = False) -> set[str]:

Description: Scans code for import statements naming documented project modules. Functions as a diagnostic recall check to identify dependencies missed by LLM extraction passes.

Parameters:

  • content (str): Raw file content.
  • source_path (str): Repository path of the current file.
  • table (ModuleTable): Global module index.
  • relative_style (bool): True if relative imports are required for local files.

Returns:

  • set[str]: Set of module paths named on import lines.

Example:

def scan_import_candidates(content: str, source_path: str, table: ModuleTable, relative_style: bool = False) -> set[str]:
    found = set()
    lines = code_view(split_lines(_nfc(content)))
    block = import_block_lines(lines)
    for number, line in enumerate(lines):
        if not (import_statement_like(line) or number in block):
            continue
        if relative_style:
            line = re.sub(r"[\"'`][\w-]+[\"'`]", " ", line)
        words = set(_words(line))
        for path in table.paths:
            if path == source_path:
                continue
            stem = _stem(path)
            if stem in words and _names_path(line, stem, os.path.splitext(path)[1], table.extensions):
                found.add(path)
    return found

The method cleans lines with code_view and filters for lines matching import_statement_like or import_block_lines. For each documented path in table.paths, it checks whether the file stem appears in a path context on that line.

docs.title: relative_import_extensions()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def relative_import_extensions(located: dict) -> set:

Description: Discovers file extensions where the project employs relative path imports (./, ../).

Parameters:

  • located (dict): Dictionary mapping file paths to lists of located dependency claims.

Returns:

  • set: Set of file extension strings (e.g., {".ts", ".js"}).

Example:

def relative_import_extensions(located: dict) -> set:
    return {os.path.splitext(path)[1] for path, claims in located.items() if any(_is_relative(claim["target"]) for claim in claims)}

This inspection allows the resolution engine to infer language conventions dynamically. If files with a specific extension use ./ or ../ anywhere in the project, bare package names in those files are treated as external third-party dependencies rather than same-named local modules.

docs.title: target_written()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def target_written(target: str, evidence: str) -> bool:

Description: Verifies whether a claimed dependency target string is physically written within the evidence quote rather than being an LLM paraphrase or hallucination.

Parameters:

  • target (str): Claimed target string.
  • evidence (str): Quoted source evidence line.

Returns:

  • bool: True if the target is literally present, otherwise False.

Example:

def target_written(target: str, evidence: str) -> bool:
    text = _collapse(target.strip().strip("\"'`<>()[];,"))
    if not text:
        return False
    if re.search("[\"'`]", text) and text in _collapse(evidence):  # the whole expression copied: __DIR__ . '/src/Db.php'
        return True
    first = (_words(text) or [""])[0]
    quoted = [q for q in re.findall(r"(?=[\"'`<]([^\"'`<>\s]+)[\"'`>])", evidence) if re.search(r"[/.]", q) or (first and first in _words(q))]
    if quoted:
        bare = _bare_path(text)
        if any(_bare_path(q) == bare or q.endswith("/" + bare) for q in quoted):
            return True
    # ...

When evidence contains quoted specifiers, the target must match one of the quoted substrings (normalizing leading slashes and dot prefixes). For non-quoted languages (e.g., Python from a.b import c), the target tokens must appear in exact sequential order in the evidence text, excluding imported local aliases.

docs.title: judge_dependency()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def judge_dependency( claim: dict, source_path: str, source_words: set, table: ModuleTable, relative_style: bool, shadowed: frozenset = frozenset() ) -> tuple[str, list]:

Description: Evaluates a single located dependency claim, determining whether it represents an internal dependency ("depends_on"), an external library ("external"), or an invalid claim ("rejected").

Parameters:

  • claim (dict): The located dependency claim dictionary.
  • source_path (str): Relative repository path of the importing file.
  • source_words (set): Tokens from the source file.
  • table (ModuleTable): Global module index.
  • relative_style (bool): Whether the file type uses relative path imports.
  • shadowed (frozenset): Names of external packages that shadow local modules.

Returns:

  • tuple[str, list]: A tuple (verdict, details). verdict is "depends_on", "external", or "rejected". details provides matched (module_path, how) pairs or rejection reasons.

Example:

target, evidence = claim["target"], claim["evidence"]
if _BARE_NAME_RE.match(target) and normalize_name(target) in shadowed:
    return "external", []
written = target_written(target, evidence)
per_line = claim.get("match") == "tokens"
manifest = table.resolve_manifest(target, source_path, source_words, prefer_local=not relative_style)
if manifest is not None:
    targets, _prefix = manifest
    if not targets:
        return "external", []
    if written and _imports_target(evidence, target):
        return "depends_on", [(module, "manifest") for module in targets]
    return "rejected", [(module, "evidence does not import the declared package or alias") for module in targets]
# ...

The function checks if the target is shadowed by an external library. It then evaluates manifest rules via resolve_manifest. If unhandled by manifests, it delegates to table.resolve. If the target is verified by target_written and conforms to evidence_names_module, it is confirmed as an internal edge.

docs.title: shadowed_names()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def shadowed_names(claims: list[dict], verdicts: list[tuple]) -> frozenset:

Description: Computes the set of bare module names that represent external packages in a file without also being imported from internal modules.

Parameters:

  • claims (list[dict]): List of dependency claim dictionaries for a file.
  • verdicts (list[tuple]): List of evaluation results from judge_dependency.

Returns:

  • frozenset: Set of bare names that refer exclusively to external packages.

Example:

def shadowed_names(claims: list[dict], verdicts: list[tuple]) -> frozenset:
    def last(claim):
        segments = _name_segments(claim["target"])
        return segments[-1] if len(segments) > 1 else None

    external = {last(claim) for claim, (verdict, _) in zip(claims, verdicts, strict=True) if verdict == "external"} - {None}
    internal = {last(claim) for claim, (verdict, _) in zip(claims, verdicts, strict=True) if verdict == "depends_on"} - {None}
    return frozenset(external - internal)

If a file imports an external library like example.com/other/store, the terminal identifier store shadows any local module named store.py. This ensures that references like store.ErrNotFound are classified as external rather than linking incorrectly to internal modules.

docs.title: verify_dependencies()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def verify_dependencies(located: dict, contents: dict, table: ModuleTable) -> dict:

Description: Coordinates dependency resolution across all repository modules, resolving verified internal dependency edges, cataloging external libraries, logging rejected claims, and identifying missed imports.

docs.title: Phase 1: Relative Extension Analysis
docs.text:
results = {}
relative_extensions = relative_import_extensions(located)

The function scans all located claims across the codebase to identify file extensions that use relative imports (./, ../), informing the relative_style flag for each file.

docs.title: Phase 2: Dependency Judgment and Shadow Detection
docs.text:
for path, claims in located.items():
    words = set(_words(contents.get(path, "")))
    depends_on, external, rejected, seen = [], [], [], set()
    relative_style = os.path.splitext(path)[1] in relative_extensions
    verdicts = [judge_dependency(claim, path, words, table, relative_style) for claim in claims]
    shadowed = shadowed_names(claims, verdicts)
    if shadowed:
        verdicts = [judge_dependency(claim, path, words, table, relative_style, shadowed) for claim in claims]

Each claim in the file is evaluated via judge_dependency. If external package imports shadow local names, a second evaluation pass is executed with the shadowed set populated.

docs.title: Phase 3: Result Consolidation and Missed Import Detection
docs.text:
for claim, (verdict, detail) in zip(claims, verdicts, strict=True):
        if verdict == "external":
            external.append({"name": claim["target"], "line": claim["line"]})
        elif verdict == "rejected":
            rejected.extend(
                {"kind": "dependency", **claim, **({"module": module} if module else {}), "reason": reason} for module, reason in detail
            )
        else:
            for module, how in detail:
                if module not in seen:
                    seen.add(module)
                    depends_on.append(
                        {"module": module, "target": claim["target"], "line": claim["line"], "evidence": claim["evidence"], "via": how}
                    )
    missed = sorted(scan_import_candidates(contents.get(path, ""), path, table, relative_style) - seen)
    results[path] = {"depends_on": depends_on, "external": external, "rejected": rejected, "missed": missed}
return results

The loop aggregates validated dependencies into depends_on, external imports into external, and rejected claims into rejected. It then invokes scan_import_candidates to find un-extracted import candidates and records them in missed.

Parameters:

  • located (dict): Dictionary mapping file paths to lists of located dependency claims.
  • contents (dict): Dictionary mapping file paths to source text.
  • table (ModuleTable): Initialized global module table.

Returns:

  • dict: Results mapped by module path containing depends_on, external, rejected, and missed.

docs.title: facts_hash()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def facts_hash(signature: str, path: str, content: str) -> str:

Description: Computes an MD5 hex digest over a combined string of signature, file path, and file content. Used for cache invalidation.

Parameters:

  • signature (str): Extraction prompt or validator signature.
  • path (str): Repository file path.
  • content (str): Source text content.

Returns:

  • str: A 32-character MD5 hexadecimal hash string.

Example:

def facts_hash(signature: str, path: str, content: str) -> str:
    return hashlib.md5(f"{signature}|{path}|{content}".encode()).hexdigest()

The input strings are concatenated using pipe delimiters (|) and encoded to UTF-8 bytes before generating the MD5 hash.

docs.title: source_commit()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def source_commit(local_dir) -> str | None:

Description: Retrieves the Git HEAD commit SHA-1 hash for a local checkout directory.

Parameters:

  • local_dir (str | os.PathLike): Filesystem path to the local git repository root.

Returns:

  • str | None: The 40-character commit SHA string, or None if git execution fails.

Example:

def source_commit(local_dir) -> str | None:
    if not local_dir or not os.path.isdir(local_dir):
        return None
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", local_dir, "rev-parse", "HEAD"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10, check=False)
    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
        return None
    return (out.stdout.strip() or None) if out.returncode == 0 else None

The function executes git -C <local_dir> rev-parse HEAD with a 10-second timeout. Any OSError or SubprocessError is caught, returning None instead of raising an unhandled exception.

docs.title: build_facts_document()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def build_facts_document(project_name: str, commit, modules: dict, manifests: dict | None = None) -> dict:
