Description: Formats the final facts document payload containing schema version, project metadata, commit SHA, module facts, and manifest data.

Parameters:

  • project_name (str): The project identifier.
  • commit (str | None): Git commit SHA string or None.
  • modules (dict): Dictionary mapping module paths to verified fact entries.
  • manifests (dict | None): Optional dictionary of verified manifest data.

Returns:

  • dict: Complete dictionary matching FACTS_SCHEMA specifications.

Example:

def build_facts_document(project_name: str, commit, modules: dict, manifests: dict | None = None) -> dict:
    return {
        "schema": FACTS_SCHEMA,
        "project": project_name,
        "commit": commit,
        "note": (
            "Every symbol, dependency, config key and error below was found in the source at the given line. "
            "Presence is verified, completeness is not: 'coverage' compares verified to claimed facts per module."
        ),
        "modules": modules,
        "manifests": manifests or {},
    }

The function wraps the verified module and manifest data within standard envelope metadata, including schema version, project name, git commit hash, and a disclaimer regarding verification boundaries.

docs.title: load_facts()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def load_facts(path: str, section: str = "modules") -> dict:

Description: Loads and deserializes a specific section from an existing facts.json file. Verifies schema compatibility.

Parameters:

  • path (str): Filesystem path to facts.json.
  • section (str): Top-level section key to return (default: "modules").

Returns:

  • dict: The extracted section dictionary, or {} if loading fails or schema version mismatches.

Example:

def load_facts(path: str, section: str = "modules") -> dict:
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            document = json.load(f)
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return {}
    entries = document.get(section) if isinstance(document, dict) else None
    return entries if isinstance(entries, dict) and document.get("schema") == FACTS_SCHEMA else {}

The file is opened with UTF-8 encoding. Any OSError or ValueError (such as invalid JSON) is handled by returning {}. It also verifies that document["schema"] == FACTS_SCHEMA before returning the requested section.

docs.title: save_facts()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def save_facts(path: str, document: dict) -> None:

Description: Serializes and writes a facts document to disk using an atomic write strategy via a temporary file.

Parameters:

  • path (str): Destination filesystem path.
  • document (dict): Complete facts document payload.

Returns:

  • None

Example:

def save_facts(path: str, document: dict) -> None:
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
    tmp_path = f"{path}.tmp"
    with open(tmp_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(document, f, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
    os.replace(tmp_path, path)

The function ensures the target parent directories exist via os.makedirs. It formats the JSON with 1-space indentation and writes to a temporary .tmp file before atomically renaming it over the destination path using os.replace.

docs.title: facts_path()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def facts_path(output_dir: str, project_name: str, is_mkdocs: bool) -> str:

Description: Determines the filesystem path for facts.json based on whether the documentation site is built with MkDocs.

Parameters:

  • output_dir (str): Output root directory.
  • project_name (str): Project identifier string.
  • is_mkdocs (bool): True if using MkDocs site generation layout.

Returns:

  • str: Relative or absolute filesystem path to facts.json.

Example:

def facts_path(output_dir: str, project_name: str, is_mkdocs: bool) -> str:
    """docs/api/facts.json under --mkdocs (published with the site and kept by CI's docs cache), else next to the pages."""
    base = os.path.join(output_dir, project_name)
    return os.path.join(base, "docs", "api", FACTS_FILENAME) if is_mkdocs else os.path.join(base, FACTS_FILENAME)

When is_mkdocs is True, the facts file is located at <output_dir>/<project_name>/docs/api/facts.json, allowing MkDocs to bundle it with static site assets. Otherwise, it sits in the root of the project output folder.

docs.title: Private Constants and Regular Expressions
docs.text:
The module defines constants and compiled regular expressions supporting lexical scanning, normalization, and language detection:

Constant Type Description / Value _WINDOW int 8 — Line search window size for squashed and token fallback searches. _MIN_TOKEN_QUOTE int 3 — Minimum word tokens required to trust an ordered token fallback match. _EXCERPT int 300 — Character limit for preserved source code excerpts. _CALL_SPAN_LINES int 12 — Maximum line span to look forward when closing unbalanced call parentheses. _ROLE_RANK dict {"raised": 0, "mentioned": 1, "caught": 2} — Preference ranking for error roles. _QUALIFIERS set {"./\\:\"'<"}` — Path delimiter and quote characters. _CLOSERS set {"\"'>"}` — Terminal characters closing paths and specifiers. _MODIFIERS set Access and storage modifiers (pub, private, protected, static, etc.). _CONTAINER_KINDS set Container classifications (class, struct, interface, enum, module, etc.). _OWNER_EXCLUDED_KINDS set {"method"} — Excluded from module ownership due to cross-type ambiguity. _NAMESPACE_WORDS set Namespace keywords (namespace, package, module, defmodule, etc.). _INDEX_STEMS tuple Index filenames ("mod", "index", "__init__", "init", "main", "lib"). _STRING_RE re.Pattern Matches single-line quoted string literals. _HANDLER_RE re.Pattern Detects exception catching keywords (except, catch, rescue, recover). _RAISE_RE re.Pattern Detects error raising expressions (raise, throw, panic, Errorf, etc.). _COMMENT_START_RE re.Pattern Identifies line comment starts (#, //, /*, *, --). _LABEL_RE re.Pattern Identifies access labels and keywords (e.g., public slots:, private:). _NAME str Identifier regex pattern (r"[^\W\d][\w$]*"). _KEYWORD_BINDS_RE re.Pattern Matches variable bindings via let, var, val, const, for. _LINE_BINDS_RE re.Pattern Matches assignments at line start (a, b := ..., x = ...). _KWARG_BINDS_RE re.Pattern Matches keyword argument bindings (f(name=...)). _FIRST_NAME_RE re.Pattern Matches non-dotted identifier references. _DOTTED_RE re.Pattern Matches dot-separated or namespace-separated paths (a.b.c, a::b). _SHELL_VAR_RE re.Pattern Matches shell variables ($VAR, ${VAR}). _INTERPOLATION_RE re.Pattern Matches string interpolation syntax (${...}, #{...}, \(...)). _WORD_RE re.Pattern Matches alphanumeric word sequences. _LINE_BREAK_RE re.Pattern Matches carriage returns and line feeds (\r\n|\r|\n). _BARE_NAME_RE re.Pattern Matches package identifiers containing no path separators. _SEGMENT_RE re.Pattern Matches individual path segments. _GO_BLOCK_LINE_RE re.Pattern Matches bare quoted strings in Go import blocks.

docs.title: _nfc()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _nfc(text) -> str:

Description: Normalizes text into Unicode Normalization Form C (NFC), ensuring that composed character representations generated by LLMs match source files.

Parameters:

  • text (Any): Text to normalize.

Returns:

  • str: NFC normalized string.

Example:

def _nfc(text) -> str:
    return unicodedata.normalize("NFC", str(text))

This helper wraps unicodedata.normalize with form "NFC", converting input arguments to strings beforehand.

docs.title: _collapse()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _collapse(text: str) -> str:

Description: Normalizes a string by converting it to NFC and collapsing all contiguous whitespace sequences into single spaces.

Parameters:

  • text (str): Raw string.

Returns:

  • str: Single-space collapsed string with bounding whitespace removed.

Example:

def _collapse(text: str) -> str:
    return " ".join(_nfc(text).split())

The function calls _nfc on text, applies split() with no arguments to tokenize across all whitespace types, and reassembles tokens separated by a single space.

docs.title: _squash()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _squash(text: str) -> str:

Description: Normalizes text to NFC and strips all whitespace characters.

Parameters:

  • text (str): Input text.

Returns:

  • str: Squashed string with zero whitespace.

Example:

def _squash(text: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"\s+", "", _nfc(text))

Uses re.sub to substitute every whitespace character with an empty string, enabling joined multi-line matches across flexible formatting layouts.

docs.title: _words()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _words(text: str) -> list[str]:

Description: Extracts a list of alphanumeric word tokens from NFC-normalized text.

Parameters:

  • text (str): Raw text.

Returns:

  • list[str]: List of extracted word tokens.

Example:

def _words(text: str) -> list[str]:
    return _WORD_RE.findall(_nfc(text))

Applies _WORD_RE.findall over _nfc(text) to yield all contiguous word substrings.

docs.title: SourceIndex._words_in_order()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _words_in_order(self, words: list[str], first: int, end: int) -> int | None:

Description: Scans lines starting at first up to end to determine if words appear in sequential order across line tokens.

Parameters:

  • words (list[str]): Target sequence of token strings.
  • first (int): 0-based starting line index.
  • end (int): 0-based ending line index.

Returns:

  • int | None: The 0-based index of the line containing the final token, or None if the sequence is incomplete.

Example:

def _words_in_order(self, words: list[str], first: int, end: int) -> int | None:
    position = 0
    for line in range(first, end):
        for word in self.words[line]:
            if word == words[position]:
                position += 1
                if position == len(words):
                    return line
    return None

The method iterates through pre-tokenized words on each line in the range. If every token in words is matched in order, it returns the line index where the final word was encountered.

docs.title: _has_words()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _has_words(text: str, name: str) -> bool:

Description: Checks whether the word tokens of name occur in sequential order within text.

Parameters:

  • text (str): Container text.
  • name (str): Target identifier or name string.

Returns:

  • bool: True if all words in name appear sequentially in text.

Example:

def _has_words(text: str, name: str) -> bool:
    wanted, have = _words(name), _words(text)
    if not wanted:
        return False
    position = 0
    for word in have:
        if word == wanted[position]:
            position += 1
            if position == len(wanted):
                return True
    return False

Tokenizes both arguments into word lists and performs an ordered walk over have to match tokens in wanted.

docs.title: _names_in()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _names_in(text: str, name: str) -> bool:

Description: Determines if name occurs in text. For alphanumeric identifiers, delegates to _has_words. For identifiers containing operator punctuation (e.g., operator==, []), verifies verbatim squashed inclusion.

Parameters:

  • text (str): Search text.
  • name (str): Target name.

Returns:

  • bool: True if name is found in text.

Example:

def _names_in(text: str, name: str) -> bool:
    if re.fullmatch(r"\w+", _nfc(name)):
        return _has_words(text, name)
    return _squash(name) in _squash(text) and (not _words(name) or _has_words(text, name))

If name consists solely of word characters, _has_words handles boundary-safe matching. Otherwise, it verifies squashed inclusion while confirming that any word tokens embedded in the name maintain sequential ordering.

docs.title: _as_text()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _as_text(value) -> str:

Description: Safely casts input values to string representations, converting booleans and None to empty strings.

Parameters:

  • value (Any): Input value of arbitrary type.

Returns:

  • str: String representation.

Example:

def _as_text(value) -> str:
    if isinstance(value, bool) or value is None:
        return ""
    return value if isinstance(value, str) else str(value) if isinstance(value, (int, float)) else ""

Guards against YAML and JSON parsing quirks where unquoted strings might parse as booleans or nulls.

docs.title: _claim_list()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _claim_list(claims: dict, key: str) -> list[dict]:

Description: Extracts a list of dictionary items from a claims container for a given key, filtering out non-dictionary entries.

Parameters:

  • claims (dict): Claims mapping.
  • key (str): Target key name.

Returns:

  • list[dict]: List of claim dictionaries.

Example:

def _claim_list(claims: dict, key: str) -> list[dict]:
    items = claims.get(key) if isinstance(claims, dict) else None
    return [item for item in items if isinstance(item, dict)] if isinstance(items, list) else []

Guarantees type safety when processing loosely-typed JSON or YAML payloads from LLMs.

docs.title: _verify_symbols()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _verify_symbols(symbols: list[dict], index: SourceIndex) -> tuple[list, list]:

Description: Locates symbol declarations in source code, prioritizing top-level declarations before scoping members to their enclosing parents.

docs.title: Phase 1: Dependency Order and Top-Level Isolation
docs.text:
kept, rejected, placed = [], [], {}
pending, unscoped = sorted(symbols, key=lambda item: bool(_as_text(item.get("parent")).strip())), False
while pending:
    pending_names = {_as_text(item.get("name")).strip() for item in pending}
    waiting = []
    for item in pending:
        name, parent = _as_text(item.get("name")).strip(), _as_text(item.get("parent")).strip()
        if not unscoped and parent and parent != name and parent not in placed and parent in pending_names:
            waiting.append(item)
            continue
        # ...

Claims are sorted so unparented top-level symbols are evaluated first. If a symbol claims a parent that has not yet been placed but is present in pending_names, it is deferred to the next iteration.

docs.title: Phase 2: Scoped Search within Parent Spans
docs.text:
signature = _as_text(item.get("signature"))
        matches, scoped = [], False
        tops = sorted(entry["line"] - 1 for entry in kept if not entry["parent"])
        containers = sorted((entry["line"] - 1, entry["name"]) for entry in kept if entry["kind"] in _CONTAINER_KINDS)
        if parent in placed:
            start = placed[parent]
            end = next((line for line in tops if line > start), None)
            matches = [
                m
                for m in index.locate(signature, start, end)
                if name and _names_in(index.text(m[0], m[1]), name) and _parent_verdict(index, m, parent) is not False
            ]
            scoped = bool(matches)

When a parent symbol has been placed, searches for its members are bounded between the parent's start line and the next top-level symbol line, ensuring duplicate method names (e.g., def run(self)) map to the correct class.

docs.title: Phase 3: Unscoped Fallback and Block Chain Verification
docs.text:
if not matches:
            matches = [m for m in index.locate(signature) if name and _names_in(index.text(m[0], m[1]), name)]
            if parent:
                matches = [m for m in matches if _in_parent(index, m, parent, containers)]
        if not matches or (len(matches) > 1 and parent and not scoped):
            if not matches:
                reason = "signature not in source" if not index.locate(signature) else "name not in its signature, or outside its parent"
            else:
                reason = "signature matches several lines; the parent does not tell them apart"
            rejected.append({"kind": "symbol", "name": name, "parent": parent, "signature": signature, "reason": reason})
            continue

If scoped lookup finds no match, a file-wide search is performed, invoking _in_parent to evaluate Rust-style impl blocks or Swift extension blocks that reside away from the original type declaration. Ambiguous matches that cannot be differentiated by parent context are rejected.

docs.title: Phase 4: Signature Call Span Extension and Excerpting
docs.text:
first, last, how = matches[0]
        last = _call_span(index, first, last)
        text, truncated = index.excerpt(first, last, signature)
        entry = {
            "name": name,
            "kind": _as_text(item.get("kind")).strip() or "symbol",
            "parent": parent,
            "visibility": _as_text(item.get("visibility")).strip() or None,
            "line": first + 1,
            **_end(first, last),
            "signature": text,
            "match": how,
        }
        if truncated:
            entry["truncated"] = True
        if len(matches) > 1:
            entry["ambiguous_lines"] = [m[0] + 1 for m in matches]
        kept.append(entry)
        placed.setdefault(name, first)
    unscoped = len(waiting) == len(pending)
    pending = waiting
kept.sort(key=lambda entry: entry["line"])
return kept, rejected

If signatures span across parameter lists, _call_span extends the boundary to include closing parentheses. Excerpt text is created, and verified records are appended to kept, recording 1-based lines and any alternate ambiguous_lines.

Parameters:

  • symbols (list[dict]): Raw symbol claims.
  • index (SourceIndex): File index.

Returns:

  • tuple[list, list]: (kept_symbols, rejected_symbols).

docs.title: _end()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _end(first: int, last: int) -> dict:

Description: Constructs a dictionary containing the 1-based end_line key if a match spans multiple lines.

Parameters:

  • first (int): 0-based starting line.
  • last (int): 0-based ending line.

Returns:

  • dict: {"end_line": last + 1} if last > first, otherwise {}.

Example:

def _end(first: int, last: int) -> dict:
    return {"end_line": last + 1} if last > first else {}

This helper standardizes the inclusion of multi-line boundary markers across fact categories.

docs.title: _enclosing()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _enclosing(containers: list[tuple[int, str]], line: int) -> str | None:

Description: Finds the name of the nearest container symbol declared prior to line.

Parameters:

  • containers (list[tuple[int, str]]): List of (line_index, container_name) pairs.
  • line (int): Target line index.

Returns:

  • str | None: Nearest container name, or None.

Example:

def _enclosing(containers: list[tuple[int, str]], line: int) -> str | None:
    names = [name for start, name in containers if start < line]
    return names[-1] if names else None

Filters containers whose declared start line is less than line and returns the last element.

docs.title: _parent_verdict()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _parent_verdict(index: SourceIndex, match: tuple, parent: str) -> bool | None:

Description: Evaluates the lexical block chain surrounding a matched line to decide if it belongs to a claimed parent container.

Parameters:

  • index (SourceIndex): Source index.
  • match (tuple): Match record (first_line, last_line, match_mode).
  • parent (str): Claimed parent name.

Returns:

  • bool | None: True if blocks confirm parent ownership, False if enclosed by a different named container, or None if indeterminate.

Example:

def _parent_verdict(index: SourceIndex, match: tuple, parent: str) -> bool | None:
    if parent in _words(index.text(match[0], match[1])):
        return True
    if not _indent(index.lines[match[0]], 8):
        return None
    for indent, text, kind, named in index.block_chain(match[0]):
        if _names_in(text, parent):
            return True
        if named:
            return False
        if not indent:
            return True if kind == "container" else False if kind == "function" else None
    return None

Checks whether the signature itself explicitly names the parent (e.g., C++ Class::method or Go method receiver (c *Client)). If unindented, it returns None. Otherwise, it walks upward through block_chain: if an enclosing block line names the parent, it returns True; if another named container is encountered first, it returns False.

docs.title: _in_parent()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _in_parent(index: SourceIndex, match: tuple, parent: str, containers: list) -> bool:

Description: Determines whether a file-wide match of a member belongs to a specified parent.

Parameters:

  • index (SourceIndex): Source index.
  • match (tuple): Match record.
  • parent (str): Parent identifier.
  • containers (list): Known container declarations.

Returns:

  • bool: True if the match is within the parent scope.

Example:

def _in_parent(index: SourceIndex, match: tuple, parent: str, containers: list) -> bool:
    verdict = _parent_verdict(index, match, parent)
    return verdict if verdict is not None else _enclosing(containers, match[0]) in (None, parent)

Consults _parent_verdict. If inconclusive (None), falls back to checking whether the nearest preceding container in _enclosing matches parent.

docs.title: _call_span()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _call_span(index: SourceIndex, first: int, last: int) -> int:

Description: Extends a match span forward by up to _CALL_SPAN_LINES (12 lines) if lines open more parentheses ( or brackets [ than they close.

Parameters:

  • index (SourceIndex): Source index.
  • first (int): Starting line index.
  • last (int): Ending line index.

Returns:

  • int: Updated ending line index.

Example:

def _call_span(index: SourceIndex, first: int, last: int) -> int:
    depth = 0
    for number in range(first, min(len(index.lines), last + 1 + _CALL_SPAN_LINES)):
        code = _STRING_RE.sub('""', index.lines[number])
        depth += code.count("(") + code.count("[") - code.count(")") - code.count("]")
        if number >= last and depth <= 0:
            return number
    return last

String literals are blanked to prevent unbalanced quotes or brackets inside strings from distorting depth calculations. Once depth balances to 0 or less at or after last, that line is returned. Curly braces { are intentionally ignored to prevent function bodies from expanding into signatures.

docs.title: _name_rank()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _name_rank(text: str, name: str) -> int:

Description: Ranks the quality of an evidence match: 0 when name appears in executable code, 1 when written as an exact string literal, or 2 when embedded inside a longer string or comment.

Parameters:

  • text (str): Matched line text.
  • name (str): Identifier name.

Returns:

  • int: Quality rank (0, 1, or 2).

Example:

def _name_rank(text: str, name: str) -> int:
    if _names_in(_STRING_RE.sub('""', text), name):
        return 0
    return 1 if any(m.group()[1:-1] == _nfc(name) for m in _STRING_RE.finditer(_nfc(text))) else 2

Blanks string literals to check if name occurs in code (rank 0). If absent, inspects string literals to see if any match name exactly (rank 1). Otherwise assigns rank 2.

docs.title: _error_role()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _error_role(index: SourceIndex, first: int, last: int, name: str) -> str:

Description: Categorizes an error reference as "raised", "caught", or "mentioned" by scanning keywords preceding the error name.

Parameters:

  • index (SourceIndex): Source index.
  • first (int): 0-based starting line.
  • last (int): 0-based ending line.
  • name (str): Error class or symbol name.

Returns:

  • str: "raised", "caught", or "mentioned".

Example:

def _error_role(index: SourceIndex, first: int, last: int, name: str) -> str:
    pattern = re.compile(r"(?<![\w$])" + re.escape(_nfc(name)) + r"(?![\w$])")
    for number in range(first, last + 1):
        code = _STRING_RE.sub('""', _nfc(index.lines[number]))
        found = pattern.search(code)
        if not found:
            continue
        head = code[: found.start()]
        handler = max((m.end() for m in _HANDLER_RE.finditer(head)), default=-1)
        if re.search(r"(?<![\w.$])on\s+$", head):
            handler = len(head)
        raiser = max((m.end() for m in _RAISE_RE.finditer(head)), default=-1)
        return "caught" if handler > raiser else "raised" if raiser >= 0 else "mentioned"
    return "mentioned"

The function searches for the error name across lines with string literals blanked. It inspects preceding text on the line: if a handler keyword (catch, except, rescue) appears closer to the name than a raising keyword (raise, throw), it classifies it as "caught". If a raising keyword dominates, it assigns "raised". If neither keyword is present, it returns "mentioned".

docs.title: _find_closer()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _find_closer(line: str, closer: str, start: int) -> int:

Description: Locates the position of a block comment closer (such as */) within a line, ignoring occurrences that form path globs (e.g., build/*/).

Parameters:

  • line (str): Line string.
  • closer (str): Closing delimiter string.
  • start (int): Column offset to begin searching.

Returns:

  • int: Position index, or -1 if absent.

Example:

def _find_closer(line: str, closer: str, start: int) -> int:
    position = line.find(closer, start)
    while closer == "*/" and position > 0 and line[position - 1] == "/":
        position = line.find(closer, position + 1)
    return position

Guards against misidentifying path wildcards as C-style comment closers by checking if a preceding character is /.

docs.title: _rfind_closer()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _rfind_closer(line: str, closer: str) -> int:

Description: Searches backward from the end of a line for a block delimiter closer, filtering out path globs.

Parameters:

  • line (str): Line string.
  • closer (str): Closing delimiter.

Returns:

  • int: Position index, or -1.

Example:

def _rfind_closer(line: str, closer: str) -> int:
    position = line.rfind(closer)
    while closer == "*/" and position > 0 and line[position - 1] == "/":
        position = line.rfind(closer, 0, position)
    return position

Performs a reverse search via rfind, discarding matches preceded by /.

docs.title: _lead()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _lead(stripped: str) -> tuple[list[str], str | None, str, str]:

Description: Splits a stripped code line into its leading declaration modifiers, primary keyword, subsequent whitespace/separator, and remaining line content.

Parameters:

  • stripped (str): Whitespace-stripped line.

Returns:

  • tuple[list[str], str | None, str, str]: (modifiers, word, separator, rest).

Example:

def _lead(stripped: str) -> tuple[list[str], str | None, str, str]:
    text, modifiers = _ANNOTATIONS_RE.sub("", stripped.lstrip("$")), []
    while True:
        text = re.sub(r"^(\w+)\(\w+\)\s+", r"\1 ", text)  # private(set) var → private var
        lead = _WORD_AT_RE.match(text)
        if not lead:
            return modifiers, None, "", text
        word, separator = lead.group(1), lead.group(2)
        rest = text[lead.end() :]
        is_modifier = word in _DECLARATION_MODIFIERS or (word == "case" and re.match(r"(?:class|object)\b", rest))
        if is_modifier and separator and not separator.strip():
            modifiers.append(word)
            text = rest
            continue
        return modifiers, word, separator, rest

Removes annotations and strips parameterized access modifiers like Swift's private(set). Iteratively shifts words present in _DECLARATION_MODIFIERS into modifiers until reaching a non-modifier token.

docs.title: _indent()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _indent(line: str, tab: int = 4) -> int:

Description: Calculates the leading indentation column width of a line, expanding tab characters into spaces.

Parameters:

  • line (str): Line string.
  • tab (int): Number of spaces per tab character (default: 4).

Returns:

  • int: Indentation width.

Example:

def _indent(line: str, tab: int = 4) -> int:
    expanded = line.expandtabs(tab)
    return len(expanded) - len(expanded.lstrip())

Uses expandtabs(tab) before subtracting the length of the left-stripped string from the total length.

docs.title: _block_kind()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _block_kind(line: str) -> str | None:

Description: Determines the structural scope opened by a line: "function", "container", "control", or "other".

Parameters:

  • line (str): Code line.

Returns:

  • str | None: Structural classification, or None if the line does not open a block.

Example:

def _block_kind(line: str) -> str | None:
    stripped = line.strip()
    if not re.search(r"\w", stripped) or stripped[0] in ")]}" or re.fullmatch(r"end\b\W*", stripped):
        return None
    _modifiers, word, separator, rest = _lead(stripped)
    if word in _FUNCTION_WORDS:
        return "function"
    if word in _CONTAINER_WORDS:
        return "container"
    if word in _BLOCK_CONTROL_WORDS:
        return "control"
    if _CLOSURE_RE.search(stripped) or (word and _METHOD_RE.match(f"{word}{separator}{rest}") and re.search(r"[)\]{:]\s*$", stripped)):
        return "function"
    return "other"

Evaluates the leading keyword against _FUNCTION_WORDS, _CONTAINER_WORDS, and _BLOCK_CONTROL_WORDS. Lines opening closures, lambdas, or method headers ending in { or : are categorized as "function".

docs.title: _nameless()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _nameless(text: str) -> bool:

Description: Checks if a container block header declares an anonymous construct (e.g., Kotlin companion object {, Ruby class << self, C typedef struct {).

Parameters:

  • text (str): Header line text.

Returns:

  • bool: True if anonymous, False if named.

Example:

def _nameless(text: str) -> bool:
    rest = _ANNOTATIONS_RE.sub("", text.strip())
    while True:
        rest = re.sub(r"^<[^<>]*>\s*", "", rest)
        word = re.match(r"([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*", rest)
        if word and (word.group(1) in _CONTAINER_WORDS or word.group(1) in _DECLARATION_MODIFIERS):
            rest = rest[word.end() :]
            continue
        return not re.match(r"[A-Za-z_$]", rest)

Strips generic type parameter brackets and container keywords. If no identifier remains, the container is identified as nameless.

docs.title: _block_chains()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _block_chains(lines: list[str]) -> list[tuple]:

Description: Computes a list parallel to lines, recording the tuple of enclosing block contexts for each line based on indentation stacking.

Parameters:

  • lines (list[str]): File lines.

Returns:

  • list[tuple]: List of tuples of (indent, text, kind, named).

Example:

def _block_chains(lines: list[str]) -> list[tuple]:
    chains, stack = [], []
    for text in code_view(lines):
        indent = _indent(text, 8)
        chains.append(tuple(entry for entry in reversed(stack) if entry[0] < indent))
        if not re.search(r"\w", text) or _COMMENT_START_RE.match(text):
            continue
        kind = _block_kind(text)
        label = _LABEL_RE.fullmatch(text)
        if kind is None or (label and kind != "container" and (label.group(1) or label.group(2)) not in _BLOCK_CONTROL_WORDS):
            continue
        while stack and stack[-1][0] >= indent:
            stack.pop()
        stack.append((indent, text, kind, kind == "container" and not _nameless(text)))
    return chains

Uses 8-column tab expansions. For each line, the current enclosing stack is snapshotted in reverse order (innermost block first). Lines that open blocks are pushed onto the stack after popping lines with equal or deeper indentation.

docs.title: _name_segments()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _name_segments(text: str) -> list[str]:

Description: Splits a package or module name into normalized segments using delimiters ::, /, \, ., and :.

Parameters:

  • text (str): Raw module or package string.

Returns:

  • list[str]: List of normalized segment strings.

Example:

def _name_segments(text: str) -> list[str]:
    return [part for part in re.split(r"::|[./\\:]+", normalize_name(text)) if part]

Applies normalize_name before splitting on path and namespace separators.

docs.title: _declares_name()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _declares_name(line: str, name: str, keys: set | None = None) -> bool:

Description: Checks whether a manifest line defines a package name as its own identifier rather than referencing it as an external dependency.

Parameters:

  • line (str): Manifest line text.
  • name (str): Candidate package name.
  • keys (set | None): Allowed key names (defaults to _NAME_KEYS).

Returns:

  • bool: True if the line declares the name.

Example:

def _declares_name(line: str, name: str, keys: set | None = None) -> bool:
    before = line.split(_collapse(name), 1)[0]
    words = _words(before)[-3:]
    key_at = max((before.rfind(word) for word in words if word.casefold() in (keys or _NAME_KEYS)), default=-1)
    return key_at >= 0 and not re.search(r"[{(]", before[:key_at])

Splits the line before the name and examines preceding words. If a recognized naming key (e.g., name, package, artifactid) precedes the name without intervening { or ( brackets, it confirms a declaration.

docs.title: _stem()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _stem(path: str) -> str:

Description: Extracts the filename stem (basename without file extension) from a path.

Parameters:

  • path (str): Filesystem path.

Returns:

  • str: Basename without extension.

Example:

def _stem(path: str) -> str:
    return os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(path))[0]

Extracts basename and drops the extension using os.path.splitext.

docs.title: _segments()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _segments(path: str) -> list[str]:

Description: Deconstructs a POSIX path (extension omitted) into a list of non-empty directory and file segments.

Parameters:

  • path (str): File path.

Returns:

  • list[str]: Path segments.

Example:

def _segments(path: str) -> list[str]:
    return [part for part in os.path.splitext(path)[0].split("/") if part]

Strips extension and splits on /.

docs.title: _is_relative()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _is_relative(target: str) -> bool:

Description: Determines whether an import path begins with relative navigation prefixes (./ or ../).

Parameters:

  • target (str): Path string.

Returns:

  • bool: True if path is relative.

Example:

def _is_relative(target: str) -> bool:
    return target.replace("\\", "/").startswith(("./", "../"))

Normalizes backslashes to forward slashes before testing for relative prefixes.

docs.title: ModuleTable._suffix_hits()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _suffix_hits(self, tail: list[str], ext: str, source_path: str) -> list[str]:

Description: Identifies documented module paths whose terminal segments match tail, prioritizing exact case matches over case-folded matches.

Parameters:

  • tail (list[str]): Path segment suffix.
  • ext (str): File extension constraint.
  • source_path (str): Path of importing file.

Returns:

  • list[str]: Matching module paths.

Example:

def _suffix_hits(self, tail: list[str], ext: str, source_path: str) -> list[str]:
    for fold in (str, str.casefold):
        wanted = [fold(part) for part in tail]
        hits = [
            path
            for path in self.paths
            if path != source_path and (not ext or path.endswith(ext)) and [fold(part) for part in self.segments[path][-len(tail) :]] == wanted
        ]
        if len(hits) > 1:
            near = [path for path in hits if posixpath.dirname(path) == posixpath.dirname(source_path)]
            if len(near) == 1:
                return near
        if hits:
            return hits
    return []

Checks exact case matches first. If multiple candidates are found, it prioritizes a sibling file located in the importing module's directory before returning candidates.

docs.title: ModuleTable._index_file()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _index_file(self, directory: str) -> str | None:

Description: Identifies an index or entrypoint file (e.g., __init__.py, index.ts, mod.rs) within a directory according to _INDEX_STEMS.

Parameters:

  • directory (str): Directory path.

Returns:

  • str | None: Path to the index file, or None.

Example:

def _index_file(self, directory: str) -> str | None:
    members = {_stem(path): path for path in self.by_dir.get(directory, [])}
    return next((members[stem] for stem in _INDEX_STEMS if stem in members), None)

Iterates over _INDEX_STEMS (mod, index, __init__, init, main, lib) and returns the first matching file present in directory.

docs.title: ModuleTable._resolve_relative()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _resolve_relative(self, target: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> tuple[list[str], str] | None:

Description: Resolves relative path import specifiers (./, ../, Rust super::, Python leading dots .models) against the importing file's directory.

Parameters:

  • target (str): Specifier string.
  • source_path (str): Importing module path.
  • source_words (set): Tokens in importing file.

Returns:

  • tuple[list[str], str] | None: (paths, how) or None.

Example:

def _resolve_relative(self, target: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> tuple[list[str], str] | None:
    text = target.strip().strip("\"'`<>()[];,").replace("\\", "/")
    parent = re.match(r"^super(?:::(.*))?$", text)
    if parent:
        directory = posixpath.dirname(source_path)
        if _stem(source_path) in _INDEX_STEMS:
            directory = posixpath.dirname(directory)
        rest = [part for part in (parent.group(1) or "").split("::") if part and _SEGMENT_RE.match(part)]
        for size in range(len(rest), 0, -1):
            base = posixpath.join(directory, *rest[:size])
            hits = [path for path in self.paths if path != source_path and os.path.splitext(path)[0] == base]
            if len(hits) == 1:
                return hits, "path"
        index_file = self._index_file(directory)
        return ([index_file], "package") if index_file and index_file != source_path else ([], "external")
    # ...

Converts Python leading dots into relative path segments. Normalizes paths via posixpath.normpath and delegates resolution to _resolve_rooted.

docs.title: ModuleTable._resolve_rooted()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _resolve_rooted(self, base: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> tuple[list[str], str] | None:

Description: Resolves a project-root-relative path against known file stems and directories.

Parameters:

  • base (str): Rooted path without extension.
  • source_path (str): Importing source path.
  • source_words (set): Importing file tokens.

Returns:

  • tuple[list[str], str] | None: (paths, how) or None.

Example:

def _resolve_rooted(self, base: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> tuple[list[str], str] | None:
    base = "" if base in (".", "") else base
    stem_match = [path for path in self.paths if path != source_path and (os.path.splitext(path)[0] == base or path == base)]
    if not stem_match:
        stem_match = [
            path
            for path in self.paths
            if path != source_path and posixpath.join(posixpath.dirname(path), posixpath.basename(path).split(".")[0]) == base
        ]
    if len(stem_match) == 1:
        return stem_match, "path"
    if not stem_match and base in self.by_dir:
        index_file = self._index_file(base)
        used = [
            path for path in self.by_dir[base] if path != source_path and (path == index_file or self.used_names(path, source_path, source_words))
        ]
        if used:
            return used, "package"
    return None

Matches base against files with any extension. If no exact file matches, it checks if base is a directory; if so, it returns the directory's index file and any sibling files whose symbols appear in source_words.

docs.title: ModuleTable._matches_whole()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _matches_whole(self, target: str, source_path: str) -> bool:

Description: Verifies whether every segment of a target matches the terminal segments of a documented module or directory path.

Parameters:

  • target (str): Target import specifier.
  • source_path (str): Importing file path.

Returns:

  • bool: True if all segments match an internal path.

Example:

def _matches_whole(self, target: str, source_path: str) -> bool:
    parts, _ = self.normalize(target)
    return bool(parts) and (
        any(path != source_path and self.segments[path][-len(parts) :] == parts for path in self.paths)
        or any(d.split("/")[-len(parts) :] == parts for d in self.by_dir if d)
    )

Ensures that multi-part Java package imports (e.g., com.acme.shipping.Label) mapping cleanly to .../com/acme/shipping/Label.java are recognized.

docs.title: ModuleTable._resolve_in_package()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _resolve_in_package(self, package: dict, rest: list[str], source_path: str, source_words: set) -> list[str]:

Description: Resolves sub-paths or symbols referenced within a manifest-declared package directory.

Parameters:

  • package (dict): Package descriptor dictionary.
  • rest (list[str]): Path segments following the package name.
  • source_path (str): Importing source path.
  • source_words (set): Words in importing file.

Returns:

  • list[str]: Resolved module paths.

Example:

def _resolve_in_package(self, package: dict, rest: list[str], source_path: str, source_words: set) -> list[str]:
    directory = package["dir"]
    under = [path for path in self.paths if path != source_path and (not directory or path.startswith(directory + "/"))]
    root = self._package_root(package, under, source_path, source_words)
    if not rest:
        return root
    for size in range(len(rest), 0, -1):
        tail = rest[:size]
        for fold in (str, str.casefold):
            wanted = [fold(part) for part in tail]
            hits = [path for path in under if [fold(part) for part in self.segments[path][-len(tail) :]] == wanted]
            if len(hits) == 1:
                return hits
            # ...

Filters modules located under package["dir"]. If rest is empty, returns the package root. Otherwise, checks suffixes against paths and subdirectories under the package, falling back to symbols re-exported by the package root or owned by specific files.

docs.title: ModuleTable._package_root()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _package_root(self, package: dict, under: list[str], source_path: str, source_words: set) -> list[str]:

Description: Locates the primary entrypoint file for a package (e.g., explicit manifest entry, index file in src or lib, or file named after the package).

Parameters:

  • package (dict): Package descriptor.
  • under (list[str]): Modules residing under the package.
  • source_path (str): Importing module path.
  • source_words (set): Tokens in importing file.

Returns:

  • list[str]: List of entrypoint module paths.

Example:

def _package_root(self, package: dict, under: list[str], source_path: str, source_words: set) -> list[str]:
    directory, entry, last = package["dir"], package["entry"], package["segments"][-1] if package["segments"] else ""
    if entry:
        hits = [path for path in under if path == entry or os.path.splitext(path)[0] == os.path.splitext(entry)[0]]
        if hits:
            return hits[:1]
    for sub in ("", "src", "lib", last, f"src/{last}"):
        index_file = self._index_file(posixpath.join(directory, sub).rstrip("/") if sub else directory)
        if index_file and index_file in under:
            return [index_file]
    # ...

Evaluates explicit manifest entries, common directory conventions (src, lib), and files matching the package name (e.g., lib/shop.rb).

docs.title: ModuleTable._corroborated()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _corroborated(self, target: str, parts: list[str], size: int, path: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> bool:

Description: Confirms whether a partial path match is corroborated by aliases, namespace declarations, directory ancestry, or referenced symbol names.

Parameters:

  • target (str): Specifier string.
  • parts (list[str]): Parsed segments.
  • size (int): Matched suffix segment length.
  • path (str): Candidate module path.
  • source_path (str): Importing source path.
  • source_words (set): Tokens in importing file.

Returns:

  • bool: True if corroborated.

Example:

def _corroborated(self, target: str, parts: list[str], size: int, path: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> bool:
    if size < len(parts):
        dropped = parts[: len(parts) - size]
        alias = not re.match(r"\w", dropped[0]) and not (self.packages or self.aliases)
        return alias or declares_namespace(self.contents.get(path, ""), dropped[-1]) or bool(self.used_names(path, source_path, source_words))
    if len(parts) == 1 and not _is_relative(target):
        directory, source_dir = posixpath.dirname(path), posixpath.dirname(source_path)
        ancestor = not directory or source_dir == directory or source_dir.startswith(directory + "/")
        return ancestor or bool(self.used_names(path, source_path, source_words))
    return True

If leading segments were discarded (e.g., matching app/utils.py for email.utils), corroboration requires a sigil alias, a matching namespace declaration in the target, or shared symbol usage. Bare single-part names matching distant directories require directory ancestry or shared symbols.

docs.title: _names_path()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _names_path(evidence: str, name: str, extension: str, extensions: set) -> bool:

Description: Verifies if name occurs in evidence as part of a path or qualified module specifier rather than a standalone identifier.

Parameters:

  • evidence (str): Quoted line text.
  • name (str): Stem or segment name.
  • extension (str): Target file extension.
  • extensions (set): Known project file extensions.

Returns:

  • bool: True if formatted as a path or specifier.

Example:

def _names_path(evidence: str, name: str, extension: str, extensions: set) -> bool:
    for match in re.finditer(rf"(?<!\w){re.escape(name)}(?!\w)", evidence):
        before = evidence[match.start() - 1] if match.start() else ""
        after = evidence[match.end() :]
        written = re.match(r"\.\w+", after)
        if written and written.group() in extensions and written.group() != extension:
            continue
        if before in _QUALIFIERS or (extension and after.startswith(extension)) or (after and after[0] in _CLOSERS):
            return True
    return False

Scans occurrences of name. Checks if it is preceded by _QUALIFIERS (e.g., /, ., :, ") or followed by the expected file extension or closing delimiter.

docs.title: _plain_occurrence()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _plain_occurrence(evidence: str, name: str, extension: str, extensions: set) -> bool:

Description: Verifies that name appears in evidence without being suffixed by a different documented extension (preventing socket.h from falsely matching socket.cpp).

Parameters:

  • evidence (str): Evidence string.
  • name (str): Base symbol or stem.
  • extension (str): Target extension.
  • extensions (set): All project extensions.

Returns:

  • bool: True if a valid plain occurrence exists.

Example:

def _plain_occurrence(evidence: str, name: str, extension: str, extensions: set) -> bool:
    for match in re.finditer(rf"(?<!\w){re.escape(name)}(?!\w)", evidence):
        written = re.match(r"\.\w+", evidence[match.end() :])
        if not (written and written.group() in extensions and written.group() != extension):
            return True
    return False

Ensures that when multiple files share a basename with different extensions, imports specifying one extension do not match the other.

docs.title: _names_directory()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _names_directory(evidence: str, directory: str) -> bool:

Description: Determines if evidence names directory via its terminal path segments.

Parameters:

  • evidence (str): Evidence line text.
  • directory (str): Directory path string.

Returns:

  • bool: True if evidence names the directory path.

Example:

def _names_directory(evidence: str, directory: str) -> bool:
    tail = [re.escape(part) for part in directory.split("/")[-2:]]
    return re.search(r"(?<!\w)" + r"(?:\.|/|\\|::)".join(tail) + r"(?!\w)", evidence) is not None

Takes the last two segments of directory and checks whether they appear joined by path delimiters (/, \, ., ::) in the evidence string.

docs.title: _import_like()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _import_like(evidence: str) -> bool:

Description: Tests whether the first non-modifier word of evidence belongs to _IMPORT_WORDS.

Parameters:

  • evidence (str): Quoted line.

Returns:

  • bool: True if prefixed with an import keyword.

Example:

def _import_like(evidence: str) -> bool:
    words = _words(evidence.lstrip().lstrip("#@"))
    while words and words[0] in _MODIFIERS:
        words = words[1:]
    return bool(words) and words[0] in _IMPORT_WORDS

Strips annotations and access modifiers before checking the leading word against _IMPORT_WORDS.

docs.title: _without_bindings()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _without_bindings(line: str) -> str:

Description: Strips local alias bindings introduced by imports (e.g., Python as billing, C# using Env =, JS import Foo =) from a line.

Parameters:

  • line (str): Import line string.

Returns:

  • str: Sanitized line string with aliases removed.

Example:

def _without_bindings(line: str) -> str:
    line = re.sub(r"\bas\s+[\w$]+", " ", line)
    line = re.sub(r"=>\s*[\w$]+", " ", line)
    return re.sub(r"^(\s*(?:global\s+)?(?:using|import)\s+)[\w$]+\s*=(?!=)", r"\1", line)

Removes local alias names so they cannot be mistaken for imported module names or external libraries.

docs.title: _bare_path()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _bare_path(text: str) -> str:

Description: Removes leading relative navigation slashes and dots (./, ../, /, .) from a path string.

Parameters:

  • text (str): Raw path string.

Returns:

  • str: Clean path without leading navigation syntax.

Example:

def _bare_path(text: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"^(?:\.{1,2}/|/|\.+)+", "", text)

Strips relative path prefixes using regex substitution.

docs.title: _imports_target()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _imports_target(evidence: str, target: str) -> bool:

Description: Checks if evidence imports target via an import statement, a Go import block, a quoted specifier, or inline qualified code usage.

Parameters:

  • evidence (str): Evidence text.
  • target (str): Target module name.

Returns:

  • bool: True if evidence imports the target.

Example:

def _imports_target(evidence: str, target: str) -> bool:
    lines = split_lines(evidence)
    quoted = re.escape(target.strip().strip("\"'`<>"))
    if any(import_statement_like(line) or _GO_BLOCK_LINE_RE.match(line) for line in lines) or re.search(rf"[\"'`<]{quoted}[\"'`>]", evidence):
        return True
    for line in lines:
        stripped = line.strip()
        if stripped.startswith(("//", "#", "/*", "*", "--", ";")):
            continue
        code = re.sub(r"\"(?:\\.|[^\"\\])*\"|'(?:\\.|[^'\\])*'|`[^`]*`", " ", line)
        if re.search(rf"(?<![\w-]){quoted}(?:::|\.)\w", code):
            return True
    return False

Checks for import statement keywords, quoted specifiers, and qualified inline usage (e.g., shop_core::money::total(...)).

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module employs defensive error isolation patterns to prevent invalid LLM inputs or missing files from interrupting the documentation generation process:

  • Unparsed Claim Recovery: Malformed JSON/YAML blocks identified during extraction passes are passed as claims["unparsed"]. verify_file_claims increments the claimed count and adds corresponding entries to rejected with descriptive reasons rather than raising exceptions.
  • Corrupted Cache Handling: In load_facts(), file read failures (OSError) or JSON decoding errors (ValueError) are caught, returning an empty dictionary ({}). Schema version mismatches are checked silently to trigger cache invalidation.
  • Atomic File Writes: save_facts() writes JSON documents to an adjacent temporary file (f"{path}.tmp") and swaps it via os.replace(). This prevents corrupted facts files if execution terminates during disk writes.
  • Subprocess Isolation: Git command execution in source_commit() uses timeout=10 and handles OSError and subprocess.SubprocessError, returning None if the local directory lacks a Git environment or fails to respond.
  • Ambiguity Rejection: In _verify_symbols() and judge_dependency(), when an identifier matches multiple candidate lines or modules without sufficient context to differentiate them, the claim is rejected with reason "signature matches several lines" or "target matches several modules".

docs.title: files.py
docs.text: Source: utils/files.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
utils/files.py provides lightweight, in-memory file organization and selective content retrieval utilities for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder pipeline. Operating downstream from crawler modules—such as local filesystem scans and remote GitHub repository ingestors—the module processes collections of codebase files represented as sequential pairs of relative file paths and decoded text content. It addresses two core requirements in Large Language Model (LLM) codebase documentation workflows: generating a compact, token-efficient representation of the repository's directory hierarchy, and retrieving the raw source text of specific files on demand using zero-based index lookups.

The structural formatting logic is implemented in build_directory_tree(), which groups files by parent directory, sorts both directory paths and file basenames lexicographically, and annotates each filename with its integer index (idx:{i}). This formatted tree string is passed into prompt templates across multiple extraction stages—including abstraction identification, relationship mapping, and chapter compilation—enabling the LLM to understand the repository's layout and reference files by index without requiring full file contents in the initial context window. Complementing this, get_content_for_indices() extracts source text exclusively for designated file indices, constructing an indexed mapping that downstream pipeline nodes supply to targeted evaluation prompts.

The module is stateless, deterministic, and self-contained, relying exclusively on Python standard library modules (os and collections.defaultdict). It implements defensive safeguards, including out-of-bounds index suppression to prevent runtime termination and path normalization that resolves root-level files to . rather than empty directory strings. By enforcing consistent alphanumeric ordering across all directory branches and file entries, the module guarantees stable prompt payloads across executions.

docs.title: build_directory_tree()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def build_directory_tree(files_data):

Description: Generates a compact, human-readable directory tree string from a sequence of file tuples. Each file is grouped under its parent directory path and labeled with its zero-based index in files_data. Directories and filenames are sorted in ascending alphanumeric order to produce deterministic output across different environments and operating systems.

Parameters:

  • files_data (list[tuple[str, str]]): A list of two-element tuples, where each tuple contains the relative file path and its decoded string content.

Returns:

  • str: A formatted multi-line string representing the directory tree, with directories suffixed by / and indented filenames annotated with (idx:{i}).

Raises:

  • None: The function handles empty inputs and missing parent directories without raising exceptions.

Example:

def build_directory_tree(files_data):
    """Build a compact directory tree string from the list of (path, content) tuples.

    Groups files by directory and formats as a hierarchical tree with file indices.
    Used by ContextRouter, IdentifyAbstractions, MapAbstractions, and CombineTutorial
    to give LLMs structural context about the project layout.
    """
    dir_files = defaultdict(list)
    for i, (path, _content) in enumerate(files_data):
        dirname = os.path.dirname(path) or "."
        basename = os.path.basename(path)
        dir_files[dirname].append(f"{basename} (idx:{i})")

    lines = []
    for dirname in sorted(dir_files.keys()):
        lines.append(f"{dirname}/")
        lines.extend(f"  {fname}" for fname in sorted(dir_files[dirname]))
    return "\n".join(lines)

The function iterates over files_data using enumerate to preserve the original integer index of each file record. For every file, os.path.dirname(path) determines the parent directory; if the path resides at the repository root, os.path.dirname yields an empty string, which the fallback or "." normalizes to the current directory identifier. The basename is formatted into a descriptor string "{basename} (idx:{i})" and appended to the directory's list in a collections.defaultdict. Once all entries are aggregated, the directory keys are sorted lexicographically, and each directory is rendered as a header line ending with / followed by two-space indented, sorted file entries. This structure minimizes token overhead when passed to language models while retaining index coordinates for downstream content retrieval.

docs.title: get_content_for_indices()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def get_content_for_indices(files_data, indices):

Description: Retrieves the text content of specific files from files_data matching the provided collection of integer indices. It constructs a dictionary mapping contextual composite keys ("{index} # {path}") to their corresponding source file contents, safely skipping any indices that fall outside valid list bounds.

Parameters:

  • files_data (list[tuple[str, str]]): The master list of (path, content) tuples representing the ingested codebase files.
  • indices (Iterable[int]): An iterable collection of integer indices designating which files to extract.

Returns:

  • dict[str, str]: A dictionary where each key is formatted as "{index} # {path}" and each value is the corresponding raw file content string.

Raises:

  • None: Out-of-bounds or negative indices are silently ignored via guard conditions.

Example:

def get_content_for_indices(files_data, indices):
    """Get file content for specific indices from files_data list."""
    content_map = {}
    for i in indices:
        if 0 <= i < len(files_data):
            path, content = files_data[i]
            content_map[f"{i} # {path}"] = content  # Use index + path as key for context
    return content_map

The function initializes an empty dictionary content_map and iterates through the provided indices sequence. For each candidate index i, it executes a bounds-checking guard condition 0 <= i < len(files_data) to prevent IndexError exceptions caused by hallucinated or invalid LLM index references. Valid entries are unpacked into path and content variables and inserted into the dictionary using the composite key template f"{i} # {path}". Including both the numerical index and the file path in the key provides contextual anchoring for downstream LLM prompts, ensuring that the model maintains awareness of which specific repository path each code block represents.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
utils/files.py adopts a non-raising, defensive design pattern across its functions:

  • Index Bounds Guarding: In get_content_for_indices(), the index validation expression 0 <= i < len(files_data) protects against negative integers and indices exceeding the list length. Rather than raising IndexError, out-of-range indices are skipped, allowing execution to continue when an LLM requests non-existent file indices.
  • Root Path Normalization: In build_directory_tree(), calling os.path.dirname(path) on top-level paths (such as main.py or README.md) returns an empty string "". The expression os.path.dirname(path) or "." ensures top-level files are organized under the explicit directory key . instead of producing invalid or missing directory headers.
  • Deterministic Output: Directory paths and filenames are sorted using Python's built-in sorted() before formatting, preventing variation in prompt strings across runs caused by non-deterministic dictionary key ordering.

docs.title: i18n.py
docs.text: Source: utils/i18n.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
utils/i18n.py provides the internationalization (i18n) and automated translation subsystem for user interface strings within the repository. Originally factored out of utils/output.py, this module breaks a circular dependency cycle (output.py → call_llm.py → token_utils.py → output.py). By isolating the inference dependencies required for string localization into a dedicated component, output.py can delegate translation jobs to i18n.py without coupling itself directly to LLM orchestration infrastructure.

The module inspects the localized string registry (strings.csv), identifies entries missing translations for a requested target language, and compiles missing key-value pairs into a structured translation payload. It dynamically loads the translation prompt template, logs token estimation telemetry, and dispatches an LLM inference call through utils.call_llm.call_llm. If the target language column does not yet exist in strings.csv, the module dynamically provisions it.

Once the language model returns translated values, the module extracts the JSON response via regular expressions, parses the translated keys, and persists them back to disk using UTF-8 with Byte Order Mark (utf-8-sig) encoding. This encoding preserves special characters across varying operating systems and ensures compatibility with spreadsheet applications such as Microsoft Excel. If translation fails due to network issues, malformed LLM outputs, or unparseable JSON, the module emits a diagnostic warning and falls back to default English strings without halting application execution.

docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def auto_translate(lang_col, language, csv_path, use_cache, thinking_level):

Description: Discovers missing translation keys for a given language column in strings.csv, executes an LLM inference pass to translate them, and persists the updated records back to the CSV file. If translations are written, it signals callers to reload localized caches.

Parameters:

  • lang_col (str): Lowercase language column name in the CSV file (e.g., "vietnamese").
  • language (str): Capitalized human-readable language display name (e.g., "Vietnamese").
  • csv_path (str): Absolute file path to strings.csv.
  • use_cache (bool): Flag indicating whether LLM caching should be used for the call.
  • thinking_level (str | int): Model reasoning effort or thinking level passed to the LLM backend.

Returns:

  • bool: True if new translations were successfully written to disk (signaling the caller to reload its string cache), or False if no translations were needed or if an error occurred.

Raises:

  • None directly. All file I/O, token estimation, network inference, and parsing exceptions are caught internally and handled with diagnostic warnings.

docs.title: Phase 1: Input Validation and Translation Inspection
docs.text:
from utils.output import emit_raw

    if lang_col == "english":
        return False

    if not csv_path or not os.path.exists(csv_path):
        return False

    # Collect strings that have no translation in the target language column
    missing = {}
    is_new_column = False
    with open(csv_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
        fieldnames = list(reader.fieldnames)
        is_new_column = lang_col not in fieldnames
        for row in reader:
            key = row.get("STRING_KEY", "").strip()
            if not key or key.startswith("#"):
                continue
            # Check if the language column exists and has a value
            lang_text = row.get(lang_col, "").strip() if lang_col in fieldnames else ""
            if lang_text:
                continue  # Already translated

            english_text = row.get("english", "").strip()
            if english_text:
                missing[key] = english_text

    if not missing:
        return False

This initial phase validates preconditions and inspects the persistent storage file. If the requested language is "english", or if csv_path is invalid or missing, the function terminates early with False. The file is opened using utf-8-sig encoding to handle potential byte order marks cleanly. As rows are parsed, comments prefixed with # and empty keys are bypassed. If the target column does not yet exist or contains an empty string for a given key, the corresponding English string is placed into the missing dictionary. If no untranslated keys are identified, execution exits without incurring network overhead.

docs.title: Phase 2: Prompt Formatting and Token Telemetry
docs.text:
# Report what we found
    if is_new_column:
        emit_raw("PROGRESS", f"[i18n] New language '{language}' — adding column to strings.csv")
    emit_raw("PROGRESS", f"[i18n] {len(missing)} strings need translation to {language}")

    # Batch translate via LLM
    try:
        from utils.call_llm import call_llm

        entries_json = json.dumps(missing, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)

        # Load prompt template from prompts/common/translate_strings.md
        prompt_path = os.path.join(
            os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))),
            "prompts",
            "common",
            "translate_strings.md",
        )
        with open(prompt_path, encoding="utf-8") as pf:
            prompt_template = pf.read()
        prompt = prompt_template.format(language=language, entries=entries_json)

        emit_raw("PROGRESS", f"[i18n] Calling LLM to translate {len(missing)} strings...")
        from utils.token_utils import log_token_estimation, resolve_max_tokens

        try:
            context_tokens = resolve_max_tokens({})
        except Exception:
            context_tokens = 0
        log_token_estimation("TranslateStrings", prompt, context_tokens)

In the second phase, telemetry notices inform the user of newly introduced language columns and the count of strings requiring translation. The missing dictionary is serialized to formatted JSON without escaping Unicode characters (ensure_ascii=False). The system loads the prompt template from prompts/common/translate_strings.md relative to the module root and interpolates the language name and serialized entries. Before dispatching the request, token usage is estimated via log_token_estimation, safely resolving maximum tokens through resolve_max_tokens with an exception guard that falls back to 0.

docs.title: Phase 3: LLM Dispatch, Parsing, and Persistence
docs.text:
response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=use_cache, thinking_level=thinking_level, step="translate_strings")

        # Extract JSON from response
        json_match = re.search(r"\{[^{}]*(?:\{[^{}]*\}[^{}]*)*\}", response, re.DOTALL)
        if json_match:
            translations = json.loads(json_match.group())
            translated_count = len(translations)

            # Write translations back into strings.csv
            _write_translations_to_csv(csv_path, lang_col, fieldnames, translations)
            emit_raw("SUCCESS", f"[i18n] Translated {translated_count}/{len(missing)} strings — saved to strings.csv")
            return True
        emit_raw("WARNING", "[i18n] LLM response did not contain valid JSON — falling back to English")

    except Exception as e:
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"[i18n] Translation failed: {e} — falling back to English")

    return False

The final phase invokes call_llm with the step identifier "translate_strings". To isolate the translated dictionary from potential conversational preamble or markdown code blocks returned by the model, the response is filtered using a balanced regular expression matching nested JSON braces. Once parsed by json.loads, the dictionary is dispatched to _write_translations_to_csv for atomic in-place persistence. If the model output fails regex matching or raises an unhandled exception, a warning is emitted via emit_raw, and the function returns False, allowing the application to continue using default English text.

Example:

reload_needed = auto_translate(
    lang_col="vietnamese",
    language="Vietnamese",
    csv_path="/path/to/project/utils/strings.csv",
    use_cache=True,
    thinking_level="low",
)
if reload_needed:
    # Reload localized dictionary from strings.csv
    pass

docs.title: _write_translations_to_csv()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _write_translations_to_csv(csv_path, lang_col, fieldnames, translations):

Description: Updates existing rows and introduces new language columns into strings.csv, persisting translated key-value pairs back to disk for subsequent runs.

Parameters:

  • csv_path (str): Absolute file system path to the target strings.csv file.
  • lang_col (str): Column header name corresponding to the target language.
  • fieldnames (list[str]): List of current CSV header fields from the original read pass.
  • translations (dict[str, str]): Key-value mapping of string identifiers to their translated text.

Returns:

  • None: Mutates the file on disk directly.

Raises:

  • OSError: If the target path cannot be read or written due to file system permission issues.
def _write_translations_to_csv(csv_path, lang_col, fieldnames, translations):
    """Write LLM translations back into strings.csv, persisting them for future runs.

    If the target language column doesn't exist, it is added to the CSV.
    """
    rows = []

    with open(csv_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
        fieldnames = list(reader.fieldnames)
        # Add language column if it doesn't exist
        if lang_col not in fieldnames:
            fieldnames.append(lang_col)
        for row in reader:
            key = row.get("STRING_KEY", "").strip()
            if key in translations:
                row[lang_col] = translations[key]
            rows.append(row)

    # Write with BOM so Excel opens as UTF-8 without extra import steps
    with open(csv_path, "w", encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as f:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fieldnames)
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerows(rows)

The function performs a two-pass update against the persistent storage file. First, it re-reads strings.csv with utf-8-sig encoding, ensuring fieldnames contains lang_col by appending it to the list if previously absent. For each row parsed by csv.DictReader, if STRING_KEY is present in the translations dictionary, the row dictionary is updated with the translated text. In the second pass, the updated row objects are written out using csv.DictWriter with encoding="utf-8-sig" and newline="", ensuring that spreadsheet applications render multi-byte Unicode strings properly without corrupting line endings.

Example:

# Internal invocation inside auto_translate():
_write_translations_to_csv(
    csv_path="/path/to/strings.csv",
    lang_col="vietnamese",
    fieldnames=["STRING_KEY", "english"],
    translations={"PROMPT_START": "Bắt đầu tiến trình", "PROMPT_END": "Hoàn tất"},
)

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
utils/i18n.py implements defensive boundaries to prevent localization errors from causing workflow crashes:

  • Missing File and Precondition Guards: auto_translate verifies file existence and validates that lang_col is not "english". If these checks fail, it exits immediately with False.
  • Token Estimation Resilience: Resolving token bounds can fail in environments lacking configuration attributes. The call to resolve_max_tokens({}) is wrapped in a dedicated try/except block, defaulting context_tokens to 0 on failure so logging can continue.
  • Non-JSON LLM Output Interception: Large language models occasionally prepend markdown formatting or explanations. The module uses a regular expression (re.search(r"\{[^{}]*(?:\{[^{}]*\}[^{}]*)*\}", response, re.DOTALL)) to isolate JSON blocks. If no JSON structure is detected, it logs a warning via emit_raw("WARNING", ...) and returns False.
  • Global Translation Safety Net: The entire inference and persistence sequence is encapsulated in a generic except Exception as e: block. Any transport errors, file lock contentions, or deserialization failures emit a descriptive warning and gracefully degrade execution back to English.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
llm_anthropic.py implements the native Anthropic Claude provider adapter for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder architecture. Dispatched by utils/call_llm.py, the module encapsulates all Claude-specific request serialization, streaming transport handling, reasoning budget configuration, and multi-tier usage accounting. By isolating vendor-specific logic, the file ensures that the core orchestration engine remains decoupled from Anthropic SDK dependencies, allowing users targeting alternative providers to run without the anthropic Python package installed.

The module is optimized for the Claude 5 model family (defaulting to claude-sonnet-5) while maintaining backwards compatibility with Claude 4.6 and legacy models such as Claude Haiku 4.5. Every interaction executes over Anthropic's streaming API (client.messages.stream), ensuring that extended reasoning chains and large token generations (up to 128K output tokens) never trigger client-side read or HTTP timeouts. The module features automated token budgeting that clamps requests against context window margins, single-shot budget expansion retries when responses are prematurely truncated, opt-in server-side safety fallbacks via Anthropic beta headers, and calibration feedback loops that reconcile tiktoken estimations against observed Claude token counts.
