docs.title: get_model_limits()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def get_model_limits(model: str) -> tuple[int, int]:

Description: Retrieves the context window and maximum allowable output tokens for a specified Claude model. It queries the remote Anthropic Models API via the SDK client, caches the result in an in-memory dictionary, and falls back to hardcoded offline limits if the API call encounters network or authentication issues.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The model identifier string whose limits are being queried.

Returns:

  • tuple[int, int]: A two-element tuple containing (context_window, max_output_tokens).

Example:

def get_model_limits(model: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Return (context_window, max_output_tokens) from the Models API, with offline fallback."""
    if model in _model_limits_cache:
        return _model_limits_cache[model]
    fallback = next((v for k, v in _MODEL_LIMITS.items() if model.startswith(k)), _DEFAULT_LIMITS)
    try:
        info = _get_client().models.retrieve(model)
        limits = (getattr(info, "max_input_tokens", None) or fallback[0], getattr(info, "max_tokens", None) or fallback[1])
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"Anthropic Models API | model={model} | context={limits[0]:,} | max_output={limits[1]:,}", dest="LOG")
    except anthropic.APIError as e:
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_MODEL_LOOKUP", model=model, error=str(e))
        limits = fallback
    _model_limits_cache[model] = limits
    return limits

This method protects prompt generation from token overflow by establishing hard generation boundaries. It checks the module-level dictionary _model_limits_cache to eliminate redundant remote lookups. If the remote endpoint raises anthropic.APIError, a structured telemetry warning is emitted via utils/output.py and static limits from _MODEL_LIMITS or _DEFAULT_LIMITS (1_000_000, 128_000) are applied.

docs.title: normalize_effort()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def normalize_effort(model: str, level: str | None) -> str | None:

Description: Maps a generic thinking level string to an effort setting accepted by the specified Anthropic model, accounting for model-family constraints.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The target model identifier.
  • level (str | None): The requested thinking level (e.g., "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max", or None).

Returns:

  • str | None: The normalized effort string accepted by the model family, or None if effort configuration should fall back to model defaults.

Example:

def normalize_effort(model: str, level: str | None) -> str | None:
    """Map a thinking level to an effort value the model accepts (None = model default)."""
    effort = anthropic_effort(model, level)  # minimal → low; xhigh → high on the 4.6 family
    if level and effort is None:
        emit("WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_INVALID", level=level.lower(), model=model, supported=str(list(EFFORT_LEVELS)))
    return effort

The function delegates mapping logic to anthropic_effort() in utils/llm_config.py. For instance, Claude 4.6 models do not support "xhigh", so the value is automatically downgraded to "high". If the requested level cannot be mapped to any valid tier, an emission warning WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_INVALID is published and None is returned to allow default provider behavior.

docs.title: call_anthropic()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def call_anthropic(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Coordinates the complete end-to-end single-turn prompt execution against Anthropic Claude models. The function handles token pre-estimation, request formatting, streaming message reception, automatic expansion retries upon budget truncation, server-side fallback detection, refusal interception, and usage accounting.

docs.title: Phase 1: Request Sizing and Parameter Assembly
docs.text:
model = get_model()
    effort = normalize_effort(model, thinking_level)
    raw_tokens = count_tokens_raw(prompt)  # memoized: the node already counted this prompt
    max_tokens, ceiling = _resolve_max_tokens(int(raw_tokens * token_ratio()), model, effort)
    params, betas = _build_request(prompt, model, effort, max_tokens)
    emit_raw(
        "DEBUG",
        f"Anthropic request | model={model} | effort={effort or 'default'} | max_tokens={max_tokens:,} | "
        f"fallbacks={'on' if betas else 'off'} | prompt_cache={'on' if 'cache_control' in params else 'off'}",
        dest="LOG",
    )

    start = time.time()
    message = _send(params, betas)

The execution flow begins by querying the active model and mapping the thinking level to a valid effort parameter. Raw prompt tokens are obtained from utils/token_utils.py and multiplied by the current runtime token calibration ratio. _resolve_max_tokens() calculates the planned budget and context ceiling, after which _build_request() formats the payload and determines required Anthropic beta headers before dispatching via _send().

docs.title: Phase 2: Stream Execution and Adaptive Truncation Retry
docs.text:
if message.stop_reason == "max_tokens" and max_tokens < ceiling:
        # Thinking + reply outgrew the budget: retry once at the largest budget that fits.
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_TRUNCATED_RETRY", max_tokens=f"{max_tokens:,}", cap=f"{ceiling:,}")
        _record_usage(message, raw_tokens, effort, time.time() - start, model=model, observe=False)  # same prompt: observe once
        params, betas = _build_request(prompt, model, effort, ceiling)
        start = time.time()
        message = _send(params, betas)

If the generation halts prematurely because reasoning tokens and response content exceeded the planned max_tokens allocation, the function checks whether unused headroom remains below the absolute context ceiling. If available, a one-time automatic retry occurs at the full ceiling limit. The initial truncated attempt is billed into the usage ledger without repeating prompt calibration observations, ensuring fair cost tracking while attempting completion recovery.

docs.title: Phase 3: Telemetry, Server Fallbacks, and Refusal Interception
docs.text:
_record_usage(message, raw_tokens, effort, time.time() - start, model=model)
    if is_debug():
        _log_thinking(message)

    if _served_by_fallback(message) and message.stop_reason != "refusal":
        count_event("ANTHROPIC", "fallbacks")
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_FALLBACK_SERVED", model=model, served_by=getattr(message, "model", "unknown"))

    if message.stop_reason == "refusal":
        count_event("ANTHROPIC", "refusals")
        details = getattr(message, "stop_details", None)
        category = getattr(details, "category", None) if details else None
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_REFUSAL", model=model, category=category or "unknown")
        raise LLMRefusalError(model, category, provider="ANTHROPIC")

Once a terminal response is received, _record_usage() logs comprehensive token accounting and updates calibration metrics. If debug logging is active, reasoning summaries are extracted and emitted. The response is audited to detect whether server-side safety fallback infrastructure routed the prompt to an alternate model. If the stop reason indicates a safety refusal, telemetry events are recorded and an LLMRefusalError is raised immediately to halt retry loops.

docs.title: Phase 4: Text Extraction and Truncation Evaluation
docs.text:
text = _extract_text(message)
    if message.stop_reason in _TRUNCATION_STOPS:
        count_event("ANTHROPIC", "truncations")
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_TRUNCATED", max_tokens=f"{params['max_tokens']:,}")
        return TruncatedResponse(text)
    if not text:
        emit("LLM_EMPTY_REPLY", provider="Anthropic", reason=message.stop_reason)
    return text

Finally, textual content blocks are extracted from the message container. If the generation terminated under a truncation stop reason (e.g., reaching the context limit or output cap even after retry), the response string is wrapped inside a TruncatedResponse container, signaling utils/call_llm.py to bypass caching. If the reply is empty, a diagnostic warning is published before returning the result.

Parameters:

  • prompt (str): The complete prompt text to submit to Claude.
  • thinking_level (str | None, optional): The reasoning effort tier requested for this execution step. Defaults to None.

Returns:

  • str: The decoded response text string, or a TruncatedResponse wrapper if truncated by context or token exhaustion.

Raises:

  • LLMRefusalError: When Claude declines the request due to policy or safety classifiers.

Example:

# Invocation from utils.call_llm._call_llm_anthropic:
reply = call_anthropic(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)

Description: Internal logging interceptor class designed to hook into Anthropic's private client logger (anthropic._base_client). It extracts attempt counters, HTTP status codes, wait times, and failure reasons from raw SDK debug logs and translates them into pipeline telemetry events.

docs.title: __call__()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def __call__(self, record):

Description: Evaluates logging records emitted by anthropic._base_client, parsing retry patterns to emit unified LLM_HTTP_RETRY notifications.

Parameters:

  • record (logging.LogRecord): The standard Python logging record intercepted from the SDK logger.

Returns:

None.

Example:

    def __call__(self, record):
        message = record.getMessage()
        if message.startswith("Retrying due to status code"):
            self.cause = f"HTTP {message.rsplit(' ', 1)[-1]}"
        elif message.startswith("Retrying as header"):
            self.cause = "x-should-retry"
        elif message.startswith("Encountered") and record.exc_info and record.exc_info[1] is not None:
            self.cause = f"{type(record.exc_info[1]).__name__}: {record.exc_info[1]}"
        elif re.match(r"^\d+ retr(?:y|ies) left$", message):
            self.left = int(message.split()[0])
        elif message.startswith("Retrying request to") and len(record.args or ()) == 2:
            attempt = _SDK_MAX_RETRIES - self.left + 1 if self.left is not None else "?"
            wait = f"{float(record.args[1]):.1f}"
            emit("LLM_HTTP_RETRY", provider="Anthropic", attempt=attempt, attempts=_SDK_MAX_RETRIES + 1, error=brief(self.cause or "?"), wait=wait)
            self.cause, self.left = "", None

The method matches incoming log messages against regex patterns and known SDK phrasing. When a log line announces a pending retry, it computes the current attempt number relative to _SDK_MAX_RETRIES, formats the wait time in seconds, and triggers emit("LLM_HTTP_RETRY") via utils/output.py before clearing internal state.

docs.title: _get_client()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _get_client():

Description: Lazily constructs and caches the singleton instance of anthropic.Anthropic. It connects the SDK internal logger to the _SdkRetryRecords interceptor via open_sdk_logger.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • anthropic.Anthropic: The initialized Anthropic SDK client.

Example:

def _get_client():
    global _client
    if _client is None:
        # SDK resolves credentials (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / AUTH_TOKEN / ant profile) and
        # ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL itself. SDK retries 408/409/429/5xx with backoff (announced:
        # _SdkRetryRecords); PocketFlow node retries sit on top of this.
        _client = anthropic.Anthropic(max_retries=_SDK_MAX_RETRIES)
        open_sdk_logger("anthropic._base_client", logging.DEBUG, _SdkRetryRecords())
    return _client

This factory method manages client lifecycle state. The SDK automatically resolves credentials from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, or local authentication profiles, and reads ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL if present. Hooking _SdkRetryRecords into open_sdk_logger ensures that transport-level retries are visible across the telemetry layer.

docs.title: _fallback_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _fallback_config(model: str) -> tuple[list[str], dict]:

Description: Evaluates environment settings and model capabilities to generate server-side safety fallback configurations and necessary beta request headers.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The primary model identifier being invoked.

Returns:

  • tuple[list[str], dict]: A tuple consisting of a list of beta header strings and an extra_body dictionary specifying the fallback strategy.

Example:

def _fallback_config(model: str) -> tuple[list[str], dict]:
    """Return (betas, extra_body) for server-side refusal fallbacks, or empty when disabled."""
    setting = (os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_FALLBACKS") or "default").strip()
    if _fallbacks_disabled or setting.lower() == "off":
        return [], {}
    if setting.lower() == "default":
        if not _matches(model, _FALLBACK_PREFIXES):
            return [], {}
        return [_FALLBACK_DEFAULT_BETA], {"fallbacks": "default"}
    targets = [m.strip() for m in setting.split(",") if m.strip()]
    return [_FALLBACK_LIST_BETA], {"fallbacks": [{"model": m} for m in targets]}

This helper inspects ANTHROPIC_FALLBACKS. If set to "default", it enables fallbacks only for models in _FALLBACK_PREFIXES (Opus and Fable variants subject to classifier false positives). If a comma-separated list of target models is provided, it configures explicit fallback routing using _FALLBACK_LIST_BETA.

docs.title: _build_request()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _build_request(prompt: str, model: str, effort: str | None, max_tokens: int) -> tuple[dict, list[str]]:

Description: Assembles the complete parameters dictionary and beta header list required for the Anthropic Messages streaming API call.

Parameters:

  • prompt (str): The user prompt content.
  • model (str): The target model identifier.
  • effort (str | None): The normalized thinking effort tier.
  • max_tokens (int): The maximum output tokens allocated for the call.

Returns:

  • tuple[dict, list[str]]: A tuple containing (params, betas) where params is the keyword argument dictionary for the SDK and betas contains active beta feature flags.

Example:

def _build_request(prompt: str, model: str, effort: str | None, max_tokens: int) -> tuple[dict, list[str]]:
    params = {
        "model": model,
        "max_tokens": max_tokens,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
    }
    if uses_adaptive_thinking(model):
        if effort or _matches(model, _THINKING_BY_DEFAULT_PREFIXES):
            thinking = {"type": "adaptive"}
            if is_debug():
                # Readable reasoning summaries go to the log file (never to stdout).
                thinking["display"] = "summarized"
            params["thinking"] = thinking
        if effort:
            params["output_config"] = {"effort": effort}
    elif effort:
        budget = min(_BUDGET_BY_LEVEL[effort], max_tokens - 1_024)
        if budget >= 1_024:
            params["thinking"] = {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": budget}

    if (os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_PROMPT_CACHE") or "off").strip().lower() == "on":
        params["cache_control"] = {"type": "ephemeral"}

    betas, extra_body = _fallback_config(model)
    if extra_body:
        params["extra_body"] = extra_body
    return params, betas

The function constructs the base message payload and configures thinking mode according to model architecture. For adaptive models, it configures thinking = {"type": "adaptive"} and attaches output_config.effort; under debug logging, display: summarized is added to capture readable reasoning logs. For older models, it maps effort tiers to discrete budget_tokens. Finally, it injects ephemeral cache controls if ANTHROPIC_PROMPT_CACHE is enabled and attaches fallback configuration bodies.

docs.title: _resolve_max_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _resolve_max_tokens(prompt_tokens: int, model: str, effort: str | None) -> tuple[int, int]:

Description: Calculates the optimal output token allocation and maximum ceiling limit, taking into account model output limits, prompt sizes, safety margins, and environment overrides.

Parameters:

  • prompt_tokens (int): The calibrated input prompt token estimate.
  • model (str): The target model identifier.
  • effort (str | None): The normalized thinking effort setting.

Returns:

  • tuple[int, int]: A tuple of (wanted, ceiling) representing the planned token budget and the maximum allowable token limit.

Example:

def _resolve_max_tokens(prompt_tokens: int, model: str, effort: str | None) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Return (max_tokens, ceiling): the planned budget and the largest budget allowed.

    `prompt_tokens` is the raw tiktoken count scaled by token_utils.token_ratio() (calibrated).
    The ceiling respects the model output cap, the context window (prompt + output +
    ANTHROPIC_CONTEXT_MARGIN — the same margin input_token_budget reserves), and
    ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS when set.
    """
    context_window, output_cap = get_model_limits(model)
    cap = anthropic_output_cap()
    wanted = anthropic_planned_output(model, effort)  # same value input_token_budget reserved

    room = max(context_window - prompt_tokens - ANTHROPIC_CONTEXT_MARGIN, 4_096)
    ceiling = min(output_cap, room, cap) if cap else min(output_cap, room)
    if ceiling < wanted:
        # Small shortfalls (template overhead on a budget-packed prompt) are expected; only report real cuts.
        if ceiling < wanted * 0.9:
            emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_OUTPUT_CLAMPED", wanted=f"{wanted:,}", available=f"{ceiling:,}")
        wanted = ceiling
    return wanted, ceiling

The resolution logic balances planned output needs against physical context boundaries. The available context room is determined by subtracting prompt tokens and ANTHROPIC_CONTEXT_MARGIN from the total context window. The hard ceiling is clamped by the model output cap, available context room, and any optional ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS override. If the ceiling forces a budget reduction exceeding 10%, a warning WARN_ANTHROPIC_OUTPUT_CLAMPED is emitted.

docs.title: _stream_message()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _stream_message(params: dict, betas: list[str]):

Description: Executes the streaming API call against either the standard messages endpoint or the beta messages endpoint.

Parameters:

  • params (dict): Keyword argument parameters for the request.
  • betas (list[str]): List of beta feature headers.

Returns:

  • anthropic.types.Message: The finalized message object compiled at stream termination.

Example:

def _stream_message(params: dict, betas: list[str]):
    client = _get_client()
    if betas:
        with client.beta.messages.stream(betas=betas, **params) as stream:
            return stream.get_final_message()
    with client.messages.stream(**params) as stream:
        return stream.get_final_message()

This helper abstracts the difference between beta and standard message streams. Utilizing Python context managers (with ... as stream:), it maintains the open streaming HTTP connection and extracts the final aggregated message via stream.get_final_message(), ensuring resources are released immediately after transfer.

docs.title: _fallback_rejected()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _fallback_rejected(error_text: str, params: dict) -> bool:

Description: Inspects HTTP 400 Bad Request error strings to determine if the failure was caused by unsupported server-side fallback beta headers rather than invalid user input.

Parameters:

  • error_text (str): The error message string returned by the API.
  • params (dict): The request parameters that triggered the exception.

Returns:

  • bool: True if the error reflects an unsupported fallback feature; otherwise False.

Example:

def _fallback_rejected(error_text: str, params: dict) -> bool:
    """True when a 400 rejects the fallback feature itself (beta header not enabled, or
    `fallbacks: "default"` unsupported for this model/account) — not a user config error."""
    text = error_text.lower()
    if "anthropic-beta" in text and "server-side-fallback" in text:
        return True
    return params.get("extra_body", {}).get("fallbacks") == "default" and "fallbacks" in text

The function performs text matching across the error payload. It checks whether the API returned an unrecognized header error regarding anthropic-beta: server-side-fallback or indicated that fallbacks: default is unavailable for the current account or model tier.

docs.title: _send()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _send(params: dict, betas: list[str]):

Description: Dispatches a streamed request and handles fallback de-escalation if the server rejects beta fallback headers.

Parameters:

  • params (dict): Serialized message parameters.
  • betas (list[str]): Active beta header list.

Returns:

  • anthropic.types.Message: The completed response message.

Raises:

  • anthropic.BadRequestError: If the API rejects the request for reasons unrelated to fallback feature availability.

Example:

def _send(params: dict, betas: list[str]):
    """Send one streamed request; disable fallbacks for the run if the feature is unavailable."""
    global _fallbacks_disabled
    try:
        return _stream_message(params, betas)
    except anthropic.BadRequestError as e:
        if "extra_body" in params and _fallback_rejected(str(e), params):
            _fallbacks_disabled = True
            emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_FALLBACK_DISABLED", error=str(e))
            retry_params = {k: v for k, v in params.items() if k != "extra_body"}
            return _stream_message(retry_params, [])
        raise

This method guards request dispatch with defensive retry logic. If a BadRequestError indicates that server-side fallbacks are rejected by Anthropic's gateway, the helper sets the module-level flag _fallbacks_disabled = True, logs WARN_ANTHROPIC_FALLBACK_DISABLED, strips extra_body from the parameters, and immediately retries the request as a standard non-fallback call.

docs.title: _price()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _price(model: str, tokens_in: int, tokens_out: int, cache_read: int, cache_write: int) -> float | None:

Description: Computes the estimated USD cost of a message invocation by matching the model identifier against pricing tables.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The model identifier.
  • tokens_in (int): Standard prompt input tokens.
  • tokens_out (int): Generated completion tokens.
  • cache_read (int): Input tokens read from prompt cache.
  • cache_write (int): Input tokens written to prompt cache.

Returns:

  • float | None: The total cost in USD, or None if the model cannot be matched to known pricing records.

Example:

def _price(model: str, tokens_in: int, tokens_out: int, cache_read: int, cache_write: int) -> float | None:
    price = next((_PRICING[k] for k in sorted(_PRICING, key=len, reverse=True) if (model or "").startswith(k)), None)
    if price is None:
        return None
    p_in, p_out, p_read = price
    return (tokens_in * p_in + tokens_out * p_out + cache_read * p_read + cache_write * p_in * 1.25) / 1_000_000

The pricing calculation uses longest-prefix matching across the _PRICING dictionary. Costs are calculated on a per-million-token basis, with ephemeral 5-minute cache write operations priced at 1.25x the standard prompt token input rate.

docs.title: _declined_before_output()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _declined_before_output(message) -> bool:

Description: Checks whether a response was rejected by safety classifiers before any output tokens were generated.

Parameters:

  • message (anthropic.types.Message): The received response message.

Returns:

  • bool: True if stop_reason is "refusal" and output tokens equal zero; otherwise False.

Example:

def _declined_before_output(message) -> bool:
    """A refusal with no output tokens at all is not billed (the same rule as for fallback iterations)."""
    return getattr(message, "stop_reason", None) == "refusal" and not (getattr(message.usage, "output_tokens", 0) or 0)

In accordance with Anthropic billing conventions, safety refusals generated before any output tokens are emitted are unbilled. This helper detects such occurrences to prevent billing zero-output refusals in the usage ledger.

docs.title: _billed_entries()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _billed_entries(message) -> list:

Description: Isolates the billed usage items from a message, extracting valid fallback iterations or top-level usage blocks.

Parameters:

  • message (anthropic.types.Message): The received message.

Returns:

  • list: A list of usage entry objects representing billed attempts.

Example:

def _billed_entries(message) -> list:
    """Usage entries of the billed attempts: every usage.iterations entry with output (server-side
    fallbacks), else the top-level usage unless the request was declined before any output."""
    iterations = getattr(message.usage, "iterations", None) or []
    if iterations:
        return [entry for entry in iterations if (getattr(entry, "output_tokens", 0) or 0) > 0]
    return [] if _declined_before_output(message) else [message.usage]

When server-side fallbacks occur, Anthropic returns an iterations list detailing every attempt. The helper filters this list to include only iterations that generated output, or falls back to top-level usage if no iterations exist and the request was not declined prior to output generation.

docs.title: _billed_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _billed_tokens(message) -> tuple[int, int, int, int, int]:

Description: Aggregates token counts across all billed attempts to align totals with estimated financial costs.

Parameters:

  • message (anthropic.types.Message): The message containing usage details.

Returns:

  • tuple[int, int, int, int, int]: A 5-tuple formatted as (total_in, out, cache_read, cache_write, thinking).

Example:

def _billed_tokens(message) -> tuple[int, int, int, int, int]:
    """(total input incl. cache read/write, output, cache_read, cache_write, thinking) summed over the
    billed attempts (_billed_entries), so token totals match _message_cost."""
    total_in = out = cache_read = cache_write = thinking = 0
    for entry in _billed_entries(message):
        tokens_in, tokens_out, read, write = _tokens(entry)
        total_in += tokens_in + read + write
        out += tokens_out
        cache_read += read
        cache_write += write
        thinking += _thinking_tokens(entry)
    return total_in, out, cache_read, cache_write, thinking

The helper iterates over _billed_entries(message) and sums all input tokens (standard input plus cached reads and writes), generated output, and reasoning tokens to produce accurate usage aggregates.

docs.title: _message_cost()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _message_cost(message, served_model: str) -> float | None:

Description: Estimates the total cost in USD for a response message, factoring in multi-attempt fallback iterations.

Parameters:

  • message (anthropic.types.Message): The message payload.
  • served_model (str): The identifier of the model that served the response.

Returns:

  • float | None: The calculated cost in USD, 0.0 if unbilled, or None if model rates are unknown.

Example:

def _message_cost(message, served_model: str) -> float | None:
    """Estimated USD cost of one response. With server-side fallbacks, usage.iterations holds the
    per-attempt usage (each billed at its own model's rate; an attempt declined before any output is
    unbilled); top-level usage covers only the attempt that produced the returned message."""
    iterations = getattr(message.usage, "iterations", None) or []
    if iterations:
        total, known = 0.0, True
        for entry in iterations:
            tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_read, cache_write = _tokens(entry)
            if tokens_out == 0:
                continue  # declined before any output (primary or fallback attempt): not billed
            cost = _price(getattr(entry, "model", None) or served_model, tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_read, cache_write)
            known = known and cost is not None
            total += cost or 0.0
        return total if known else None
    if _declined_before_output(message):
        return 0.0  # declined before any output: not billed
    return _price(served_model, *_tokens(message.usage))

This function accounts for multi-model fallback iterations. If usage.iterations is present, each attempt is evaluated against its respective model's pricing rates, ignoring zero-output refusals. If no iterations exist, the calculation evaluates the top-level usage against served_model.

docs.title: _record_usage()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _record_usage(message, raw_prompt_tokens: int, effort: str | None, elapsed: float, model: str = "", observe: bool = True) -> None:

Description: Records execution metrics into the global usage ledger, updates runtime prompt token calibration ratios, and outputs diagnostic traces.

docs.title: Phase 1: Ledger Iterations and Entry Recording
docs.text:
served_model = getattr(message, "model", "") or ""
    has_iterations = bool(getattr(message.usage, "iterations", None))
    entries = _billed_entries(message)
    if not entries:
        record_usage("ANTHROPIC", served_model, cost=0.0, measured=False)  # declined before any output: not billed
    # One ledger request per billed attempt (primary + fallback each billed at its own model's rate), so
    # request counts, per-request estimate deviation and the model list stay correct.
    for entry in entries:
        t_in, t_out, read, write = _tokens(entry)
        entry_model = (getattr(entry, "model", None) or served_model) if has_iterations else served_model
        record_usage(
            "ANTHROPIC",
            entry_model,
            input_tokens=t_in + read + write,
            output_tokens=t_out,
            thinking_tokens=_thinking_tokens(entry),
            cache_read=read,
            cache_write=write,
            cost=_price(entry_model, t_in, t_out, read, write) if has_iterations else _message_cost(message, served_model),
        )
    total_in, tokens_out, cache_read, cache_write, thinking = _billed_tokens(message)  # totals for the debug line
    cost = _message_cost(message, served_model)

The function identifies billed attempts via _billed_entries() and commits individual usage records to record_usage() in utils/llm_common.py. Billed fallback attempts are recorded under their respective model identifiers to ensure granular cost tracking.

docs.title: Phase 2: Token Ratio Calibration and Debug Logging
docs.text:
# Observed Claude/tiktoken ratio of the attempt that produced this message (top-level usage),
    # fed to the calibration unless another model (server-side fallback) served it.
    tokens_in, _, read, write = _tokens(message.usage)
    attempt_in = tokens_in + read + write
    ratio = attempt_in / raw_prompt_tokens if raw_prompt_tokens else 0.0
    if observe and model and not _served_by_fallback(message):
        observe_prompt_tokens("ANTHROPIC", model, raw_prompt_tokens, attempt_in, served_model=served_model)
    emit_raw(
        "DEBUG",
        f"ANTHROPIC USAGE | model={served_model} | effort={effort or 'default'} | stop={message.stop_reason} | "
        f"in={total_in:,} | out={tokens_out:,} | thinking={thinking:,} | cache_read={cache_read:,} | cache_write={cache_write:,} | "
        f"est_cost={'$' + format(cost, '.4f') if cost is not None else 'n/a'} | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s | observed_token_ratio={ratio:.2f}",
        dest="BOTH",
    )

The actual input token count is compared against the initial raw tiktoken count to calculate the observed token ratio. If observation is enabled and the request was served directly (not by a fallback model), the metric is submitted to observe_prompt_tokens() in utils/token_utils.py to dynamically calibrate future budgeting estimates. A structured debug summary is then emitted to console and log targets.

Parameters:

  • message (anthropic.types.Message): The completed response message.
  • raw_prompt_tokens (int): Uncalibrated input token count.
  • effort (str | None): Active thinking effort tier.
  • elapsed (float): Request duration in seconds.
  • model (str, optional): Requested model name. Defaults to "".
  • observe (bool, optional): Whether to record token calibration metrics. Defaults to True.

Returns:

None.

Example:

_record_usage(message, raw_tokens, effort, time.time() - start, model=model)

def _log_thinking(message) -> None:

docs.title: _served_by_fallback()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _served_by_fallback(message) -> bool:

Description: Determines whether a response was generated by a fallback target rather than the initially requested model.

Parameters:

  • message (anthropic.types.Message): The received response message.

Returns:

  • bool: True if fallback blocks or iteration descriptors are detected; otherwise False.

Example:

def _served_by_fallback(message) -> bool:
    if any(getattr(block, "type", None) == "fallback" for block in message.content):
        return True
    iterations = getattr(message.usage, "iterations", None) or []
    return any(getattr(entry, "type", None) == "fallback_message" for entry in iterations)

The helper inspects content blocks for fallback indicators and checks usage.iterations for entries marked with type == "fallback_message".

docs.title: _extract_text()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _extract_text(message) -> str:

Description: Concatenates all textual content blocks from the message body into a single output string.

Parameters:

  • message (anthropic.types.Message): The response message.

Returns:

  • str: The assembled response text.

Example:

def _extract_text(message) -> str:
    return "".join(block.text for block in message.content if getattr(block, "type", None) == "text")

The helper filters message.content for blocks with type == "text" and joins their text payloads, isolating generated prose from metadata and reasoning blocks.

docs.title: LLMRefusalError
docs.text:
The module catches safety classifier refusals returned by Anthropic (stop_reason == "refusal"). Rather than triggering transient node retries, call_anthropic() extracts the refusal category from message.stop_details, logs a WARN_ANTHROPIC_REFUSAL event, and raises an LLMRefusalError:

    if message.stop_reason == "refusal":
        count_event("ANTHROPIC", "refusals")
        details = getattr(message, "stop_details", None)
        category = getattr(details, "category", None) if details else None
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_REFUSAL", model=model, category=category or "unknown")
        raise LLMRefusalError(model, category, provider="ANTHROPIC")

This error halts execution for the current prompt branch, preventing repeated submission of rejected prompts.

docs.title: Truncation Handling and TruncatedResponse
docs.text:
When a generation stops due to context or budget exhaustion (max_tokens or model_context_window_exceeded), the module evaluates whether the budget can be expanded:

    if message.stop_reason == "max_tokens" and max_tokens < ceiling:
        # Thinking + reply outgrew the budget: retry once at the largest budget that fits.
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_TRUNCATED_RETRY", max_tokens=f"{max_tokens:,}", cap=f"{ceiling:,}")
        _record_usage(message, raw_tokens, effort, time.time() - start, model=model, observe=False)  # same prompt: observe once
        params, betas = _build_request(prompt, model, effort, ceiling)
        start = time.time()
        message = _send(params, betas)

If the response remains truncated after expanding to ceiling, call_anthropic() wraps the partial output in a TruncatedResponse object. This container indicates to utils/call_llm.py that the text is incomplete and must not be committed to disk cache.

docs.title: SDK Retries and Telemetry Trapping
docs.text:
Network drops, connection resets, and HTTP status codes 408, 409, 429, and 5xx are handled by the Anthropic SDK client configured with max_retries=3. To provide observability, _SdkRetryRecords intercepts SDK debug logs and translates them into structured telemetry events:

    def __call__(self, record):
        message = record.getMessage()
        # ... parse status codes, error causes, and retry counters ...
        elif message.startswith("Retrying request to") and len(record.args or ()) == 2:
            attempt = _SDK_MAX_RETRIES - self.left + 1 if self.left is not None else "?"
            wait = f"{float(record.args[1]):.1f}"
            emit("LLM_HTTP_RETRY", provider="Anthropic", attempt=attempt, attempts=_SDK_MAX_RETRIES + 1, error=brief(self.cause or "?"), wait=wait)
            self.cause, self.left = "", None

This mechanism surfaces transport-level retries and backoff delays to the console without interrupting execution.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
utils/llm_common.py serves as the foundational, provider-neutral utility library for all Large Language Model interactions within the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder architecture. It is intentionally decoupled from external provider SDKs (such as google-genai or anthropic) and third-party dependencies, relying exclusively on Python standard library modules (contextlib, contextvars, hashlib, and logging). By isolating cross-cutting concerns—such as execution response truncation wrappers, refusal exception taxonomies, usage ledger aggregation, and SDK logging bridges—the module prevents circular import chains across concrete provider drivers (llm_anthropic.py, llm_gemini.py, llm_openrouter.py) and top-level orchestrators (call_llm.py).

The module encapsulates three primary operational capabilities:

  1. Response and Error Signaling: It defines TruncatedResponse (a specialized string subclass indicating output token exhaustion) and LLMRefusalError (a structured runtime exception differentiating deterministic prompt declines from retryable output-side policy filters). It backs this taxonomy with a SHA-256 in-memory memoization cache to prevent pipeline retries from burning rate limits on rejected prompts.
  2. Context-Aware Usage Ledger: Utilizing Python's thread-safe and asynchronous-safe contextvars.ContextVar, it tracks token expenditures (input, output, reasoning/thinking, and caching metrics), estimated token allocations, financial costs in USD, and operational failure events across two distinct dimensions: per LLM provider and per logical pipeline step.
  3. SDK Log Interception and Warning De-duplication: It implements _SdkLogBridge, a specialized logging.Handler that captures lower-level client transport events (such as provider HTTP retry notices) without modifying upstream root logging configurations, while warn_once ensures non-fatal warnings are emitted only once per execution run.

docs.title: TruncatedResponse
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: class TruncatedResponse(str):

Description: A specialized string subclass used to wrap model completion text that was prematurely terminated due to token constraints (such as hitting max_tokens limits or reaching context window boundaries). Downstream dispatchers in call_llm.py inspect the boolean attribute truncated to ensure truncated outputs are returned to calling pipeline nodes for handling or retrying, but are never persisted into the persistent LLM disk cache (llm_cache_v2.json).

class TruncatedResponse(str):
    """Response text from a reply that was cut off; call_llm returns it but never caches it."""

    truncated = True

The TruncatedResponse class functions identically to a standard Python str across all text-processing operations, string concatenation, and formatting pipelines. However, downstream parsing utilities (such as YAML deserializers) and dispatch routers identify the truncated = True attribute on the instance to reject incomplete payloads. This mechanism guarantees that partially generated code structures, incomplete JSON schemas, or sliced markdown sections do not corrupt downstream AST validation routines or poison long-term response caches.

docs.title: LLMRefusalError
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: class LLMRefusalError(RuntimeError):

Description: An exception raised when an upstream provider declines to process or complete a prompt due to content filtering, safety moderation, or policy restrictions. The class encapsulates provider metadata, refusal category classification, and a critical retryable boolean flag that distinguishes deterministic prompt declines from sample-dependent output blocks.

class LLMRefusalError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when the provider (and any configured fallback) declines a request.

    retryable=False: the same request is declined again (Claude refusal, blocked prompt,
    prohibited content) — call_llm remembers it and does not re-send it on node retries.
    retryable=True: an output-side block that a new sample can pass (Gemini RECITATION / OTHER /
    SAFETY on the candidate, OpenRouter content_filter) — node retries re-sample normally.
    """

    def __init__(self, model: str, category: str | None, provider: str = "ANTHROPIC", retryable: bool = False):
        self.model = model
        self.category = category
        self.provider = provider
        self.retryable = retryable
        super().__init__(f"{provider} model {model} declined the request (category={category or 'unknown'})")

The LLMRefusalError hierarchy models failure semantics across diverse provider APIs into a uniform interface. When retryable is set to False, the error denotes an input-level policy rejection (such as Anthropic Claude refusing a prompt or Google Gemini blocking input tokens); these rejections are cached via remember_refusal so subsequent pipeline retries fail immediately without wasting API quotas. Conversely, when retryable is set to True, the error signifies a non-deterministic candidate generation block (such as Gemini's RECITATION or SAFETY candidate filters, or OpenRouter output moderation); these allow outer execution loops to resample with alternative temperature or randomness.

docs.title: LLMRefusalError.__init__()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def __init__(self, model: str, category: str | None, provider: str = "ANTHROPIC", retryable: bool = False):

Description: Initializes an LLMRefusalError instance with the model identifier, category of refusal, origin provider name, and retryability classification.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The model identifier that rejected the execution (e.g., "claude-sonnet-5", "gemini-2.5-pro").
  • category (str | None): The provider-specific classification string indicating why the request was declined (e.g., "SAFETY", "RECITATION", "content_filter").
  • provider (str): The backend provider originating the decline. Defaults to "ANTHROPIC".
  • retryable (bool): Flag indicating whether re-submitting the prompt could succeed under different sampling parameters. Defaults to False.

Returns:

  • None: Constructor returns nothing.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_common.py
def __init__(self, model: str, category: str | None, provider: str = "ANTHROPIC", retryable: bool = False):
    self.model = model
    self.category = category
    self.provider = provider
    self.retryable = retryable
    super().__init__(f"{provider} model {model} declined the request (category={category or 'unknown'})")

During initialization, the constructor binds the specific operational context to public instance attributes and compiles a standard formatted message for the parent RuntimeError. The resulting string clearly identifies the provider, model, and category for downstream error logs. This design ensures that callers catching the exception can inspect .retryable or .category programmatically without parsing error message strings.

docs.title: request_key()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def request_key(provider: str, model: str, thinking_level: str | None, prompt: str) -> str:

Description: Computes a deterministic SHA-256 hexadecimal digest that uniquely scopes an LLM inference request by provider, model name, thinking effort level, and prompt content.

Parameters:

  • provider (str): The target provider identifier (e.g., "ANTHROPIC", "GEMINI").
  • model (str): The model name string.
  • thinking_level (str | None): The configured reasoning or thinking tier (e.g., "low", "high", or None).
  • prompt (str): The exact text of the prompt submitted to the model.

Returns:

  • str: A 64-character lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest string.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_common.py
def request_key(provider: str, model: str, thinking_level: str | None, prompt: str) -> str:
    scope = f"{provider}|{model}|{(thinking_level or 'default').lower()}\n"
    return hashlib.sha256((scope + prompt).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

The request_key function normalizes request parameters to guarantee consistent cache addressing. It normalizes absent thinking levels to the literal string "default" in lowercase, combines the parameters with pipe delimiters and a trailing newline separator, and appends the raw prompt string. The resulting byte sequence is hashed using SHA-256 to generate a collision-resistant identifier used as the lookup key in refusal tracking.

docs.title: remember_refusal()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def remember_refusal(key: str, error: LLMRefusalError) -> None:

Description: Stores an LLMRefusalError in the internal process-level refusal memoization ledger _refused under the specified request key.

Parameters:

  • key (str): The 64-character SHA-256 digest produced by request_key.
  • error (LLMRefusalError): The refusal error instance to memoize.

Returns:

  • None: This function mutates internal module state and returns nothing.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_common.py
def remember_refusal(key: str, error: LLMRefusalError) -> None:
    _refused[key] = error

This function acts as a write barrier for refused requests. When an upstream provider encounters an unrecoverable policy refusal, call_llm calls remember_refusal with the request digest. Storing the error prevents repeated invocations across framework-level node retries from re-submitting the identical prompt payload, conserving API quota and eliminating rate-limit burn.

docs.title: previous_refusal()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def previous_refusal(key: str) -> LLMRefusalError | None:

Description: Queries the internal refusal ledger for a prior refusal error associated with the given request digest.

Parameters:

  • key (str): The 64-character SHA-256 request digest to query.

Returns:

  • LLMRefusalError | None: The cached refusal exception if a prior decline was recorded; otherwise None.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_common.py
def previous_refusal(key: str) -> LLMRefusalError | None:
    return _refused.get(key)

The previous_refusal helper provides an O(1) memory lookup. Before dispatching any network request to a remote provider, call_llm evaluates previous_refusal(key). If a non-null LLMRefusalError is returned, the caller can immediately re-raise the exception, short-circuiting network transport and execution latency.

docs.title: usage_step()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def usage_step(step: str | None):

Description: A context manager that scopes all LLM token usage, cost accumulations, and operational event counters within its dynamic block to a designated pipeline step name.

Parameters:

  • step (str | None): The logical pipeline step name (e.g., "extract_facts", "draft_chapters"). If None or empty, defaults to "other".

Returns:

  • Iterator[None]: A context manager yielding control to the enclosed code block.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_common.py
@contextlib.contextmanager
def usage_step(step: str | None):
    """Attribute every record_usage / count_event inside the block to `step`."""
    token = _current_step.set(step or "other")
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        _current_step.reset(token)

This context manager relies on Python's contextvars module to guarantee safe execution contexts across coroutines and nested invocations. Upon entering the block, it assigns the step identifier (defaulting to "other" if falsy) to the context variable _current_step and captures the assignment token. Upon exiting, the finally block invokes _current_step.reset(token), restoring the previous step attribution regardless of whether execution completed normally or raised an exception.

docs.title: current_step()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def current_step() -> str:

Description: Retrieves the currently active pipeline step identifier from the thread/context execution state.

Parameters:

  • None.

Returns:

  • str: The active pipeline step name string, defaulting to "other" if no enclosing usage_step context is active.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_common.py
def current_step() -> str:
    return _current_step.get()

The current_step function reads the current value bound to the private _current_step ContextVar. It is primarily consumed internally by record_usage, count_event, and record_estimate to dynamically route metrics to the correct step accumulator in the _steps ledger without requiring step names to be passed through every intermediary helper function.

docs.title: record_usage()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def record_usage(provider: str, model: str, *, input_tokens: int = 0, output_tokens: int = 0, thinking_tokens: int = 0, cache_read: int = 0, cache_write: int = 0, cost: float | None = None, measured: bool = True) -> None:

Description: Accumulates token counts, cache metrics, and financial costs for a completed API invocation into both the provider-level ledger (_usage) and the active step-level ledger (_steps).

Parameters:

  • provider (str): Target provider name (e.g., "ANTHROPIC", "GEMINI", "OPENROUTER").
  • model (str): Model name or identifier string used during the request.
  • input_tokens (int): Total prompt tokens billed by the provider, inclusive of cached tokens. Defaults to 0.
  • output_tokens (int): Total completion tokens billed, inclusive of reasoning/thinking tokens. Defaults to 0.
  • thinking_tokens (int): Subset of output tokens specifically generated during reasoning/thinking passes. Defaults to 0.
  • cache_read (int): Number of input tokens served via provider-side prompt caching. Defaults to 0.
  • cache_write (int): Number of input tokens written into provider-side prompt caches. Defaults to 0.
  • cost (float | None): Computed monetary cost of the request in USD, or None if the pricing model is unavailable or unknown. Defaults to None.
  • measured (bool): Flag denoting whether the provider returned verified usage figures. If False, flags the request as unmeasured for diagnostic reporting. Defaults to True.

Returns:

  • None: Mutates internal ledger dictionaries and returns nothing.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_common.py
def record_usage(
    provider: str,
    model: str,
    *,
    input_tokens: int = 0,
    output_tokens: int = 0,
    thinking_tokens: int = 0,
    cache_read: int = 0,
    cache_write: int = 0,
    cost: float | None = None,
    measured: bool = True,
) -> None:
    for entry in (_usage.setdefault(provider, _new_entry()), _steps.setdefault(current_step(), _new_entry())):
        if model:
            entry["models"].add(model)
        entry["calls"] += 1
        if not measured:
            entry["unmeasured_calls"] += 1
        entry["input"] += input_tokens or 0
        entry["output"] += output_tokens or 0
        entry["thinking"] += thinking_tokens or 0
        entry["cache_read"] += cache_read or 0
        entry["cache_write"] += cache_write or 0
        if cost is None:
            entry["unpriced_calls"] += 1
        else:
            entry["cost"] += cost

The record_usage function coordinates usage attribution across two dimensions. It resolves or initializes the entry dictionary for both the provider key in _usage and the current step key in _steps using _new_entry(). It registers the model identifier into the entry's models set, increments call counts, and aggregates input, output, thinking, and caching token counts. If cost is None, it increments unpriced_calls, ensuring that downstream summary formatters can flag that financial estimates are incomplete.

docs.title: count_event()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def count_event(provider: str, event: str) -> None:

Description: Increments a specific operational counter (such as "refusals", "fallbacks", or "truncations") for both the specified provider and the current execution step.

Parameters:

  • provider (str): The provider identifier experiencing the event.
  • event (str): The name of the event metric to increment. Supported fields include "refusals", "fallbacks", and "truncations".

Returns:

  • None: Mutates ledger records in place.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_common.py
def count_event(provider: str, event: str) -> None:
    """Increment 'refusals' | 'fallbacks' | 'truncations' for a provider (and the current step)."""
    _usage.setdefault(provider, _new_entry())[event] += 1
    _steps.setdefault(current_step(), _new_entry())[event] += 1

count_event tracks operational anomalies and resilience events that occur outside standard billing loops. When a model returns a truncated response, a provider fails over to a secondary fallback, or a safety refusal is triggered, count_event ensures these incidents are recorded against both the originating provider and the active pipeline step. This data is exposed in the end-of-run execution summaries.

docs.title: record_estimate()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def record_estimate(step: str, estimated_input: int, *, cache_hit: bool = False) -> None:

Description: Records pre-flight token estimates and local cache hit metrics against a specified pipeline step.

Parameters:

  • step (str): The pipeline step name receiving the estimate or cache hit.
  • estimated_input (int): The estimated input token count calculated prior to network dispatch.
  • cache_hit (bool): If True, records that the request was answered directly from the local disk cache (llm_cache_v2.json) without consuming provider API resources. Defaults to False.

Returns:

  • None: Mutates step records directly.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_common.py
def record_estimate(step: str, estimated_input: int, *, cache_hit: bool = False) -> None:
    """Add call_llm's input estimate for a call (billed or served from the LLM cache) to a step."""
    entry = _steps.setdefault(step or "other", _new_entry())
    if cache_hit:
        entry["cache_hits"] += 1
    else:
        entry["estimated_input"] += estimated_input or 0

record_estimate maintains parity between estimated prompt costs and actual provider-billed metrics. When requests are resolved entirely via local caching, cache_hit=True increments the cache_hits tally without updating input token counts. When a live request is dispatched, the estimated input tokens are added to estimated_input, allowing downstream auditing routines to compare tokenizer estimations (e.g., tiktoken approximations) against actual provider billing counters.

docs.title: usage_snapshot()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def usage_snapshot(provider: str) -> dict:

Description: Creates a point-in-time dictionary snapshot of all running numeric counters for a specific provider, omitting non-scalar fields.

Parameters:

  • provider (str): The provider identifier whose totals should be captured.

Returns:

  • dict: A shallow dictionary copy containing all numeric fields from the provider's entry, excluding the models set.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_common.py
def usage_snapshot(provider: str) -> dict:
    """Copy of a provider's running totals (diff two snapshots to get one call's usage)."""
    entry = _usage.get(provider)
    return {k: v for k, v in entry.items() if k != "models"} if entry else {k: v for k, v in _new_entry().items() if k != "models"}

This function enables fine-grained differential tracking across single function calls. By capturing snapshots immediately before and after an individual LLM invocation, callers can pass the returned dictionaries to usage_delta to calculate exact token consumption, cache activity, and monetary cost for that isolated call. If the provider has not yet recorded any usage, an initialized empty schema is returned.

docs.title: usage_delta()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def usage_delta(before: dict, after: dict) -> dict:

Description: Computes the numerical difference between two usage snapshots, producing a delta mapping representing resource usage during the intervening interval.

Parameters:

  • before (dict): The baseline snapshot dictionary obtained from usage_snapshot.
  • after (dict): The subsequent snapshot dictionary obtained after request execution.

Returns:

  • dict: A dictionary containing the arithmetic difference (after[k] - before.get(k, 0)) for every numeric key in after.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_common.py
def usage_delta(before: dict, after: dict) -> dict:
    return {k: after[k] - before.get(k, 0) for k in after}

usage_delta iterates across all keys present in the after snapshot and subtracts the corresponding baseline value from before. This helper powers the per-call console telemetry emitted by call_llm, allowing real-time output of prompt tokens, completion tokens, and dollar expenditures without requiring providers to pass usage objects up the call stack.

docs.title: get_usage_summary()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def get_usage_summary() -> dict:

Description: Compiles a finalized summary dictionary mapping provider names to their sanitized public usage totals for all providers that made at least one call during the process run.

Parameters:

  • None.

Returns:

  • dict: A dictionary of {provider_name: public_entry_dict} mapping each active provider to its public summary.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_common.py
def get_usage_summary() -> dict:
    """{provider: totals} for every provider that made at least one call this run."""
    return {provider: _public(entry) for provider, entry in _usage.items() if entry["calls"]}

get_usage_summary filters out providers that recorded zero live calls (entry["calls"] == 0), transforming internal entry dictionaries into standardized public representations via _public(). This function provides the primary data structure displayed during the final summary emission phase at the conclusion of documentation runs.

docs.title: get_step_summary()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def get_step_summary() -> dict:

Description: Compiles a finalized summary dictionary mapping pipeline step names to their public usage totals, preserving first-use execution order and including steps answered entirely from cache.

Parameters:

  • None.

Returns:

  • dict: A dictionary of {step_name: public_entry_dict} for all recorded steps.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_common.py
def get_step_summary() -> dict:
    """{step: totals} in first-use order, including steps answered only from the LLM cache."""
    return {step: _public(entry) for step, entry in _steps.items() if entry["calls"] or entry["cache_hits"]}

get_step_summary preserves the insertion order of pipeline stages as defined in the global _steps dictionary. It filters for steps that registered at least one live network call or at least one cache hit (entry["calls"] or entry["cache_hits"]). Each matching step entry is formatted via _public(), exposing step-level cost and token attribution for post-run analysis.

docs.title: open_sdk_logger()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def open_sdk_logger(name: str, level: int, on_record) -> None:

Description: Attaches a custom _SdkLogBridge handler to a named Python logger, lowering its log level to intercept internal SDK retry records and routing them to a designated callback.

Parameters:

  • name (str): The logger name string (e.g., "anthropic._base_client", "google_genai").
  • level (int): The integer logging level threshold to set on the target logger (e.g., logging.DEBUG).
  • on_record (Callable[[logging.LogRecord], None]): Callback invoked whenever a new log record is intercepted.

Returns:

  • None: Mutates the target logger configuration.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_common.py
def open_sdk_logger(name: str, level: int, on_record) -> None:
    """Route SDK logger *name* through ``_SdkLogBridge``, opened to *level* (once per process): how the provider
    modules announce the retries their SDK makes and only logs."""
    logger = logging.getLogger(name)
    if any(isinstance(handler, _SdkLogBridge) for handler in logger.handlers):
        return
    passthrough = logger.getEffectiveLevel()
    logger.addHandler(_SdkLogBridge(logger, passthrough, on_record))
    logger.propagate = False
    logger.setLevel(min(level, passthrough))

This function configures vendor SDK logging pipelines idempotently. If an _SdkLogBridge is already attached to the target logger's handlers, the function returns immediately. Otherwise, it captures the logger's current effective level as a passthrough ceiling, installs the bridge handler, disables parent log propagation (propagate = False), and lowers the logger's threshold to min(level, passthrough). This ensures low-level SDK retry events are intercepted and processed without leaking full prompt and response payloads to standard error.

docs.title: warn_once()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def warn_once(key: str, *parts) -> bool:

Description: De-duplicates warning messages across an application run, returning True only the first time a given key-and-parts combination is evaluated.

Parameters:

  • key (str): Primary warning category or identifier string.
  • *parts (Any): Optional variable arguments concatenated with the key to form a composite cache marker.

Returns:

  • bool: True if the marker was seen for the first time during the current process execution; False if it was previously recorded.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_common.py
def warn_once(key: str, *parts) -> bool:
    """True the first time a (key, parts) combination is seen this run."""
    marker = (key, *parts)
    if marker in _warned:
        return False
    _warned.add(marker)
    return True

The warn_once utility provides process-wide deduplication for operational warnings. By recording composite tuples (key, *parts) in the private _warned set, it ensures that high-frequency warnings (such as unsupported sampling parameters, model downgrades, or token budget clamp notices) are displayed to the user only on their initial occurrence, keeping console output clean.

docs.title: _SdkLogBridge
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: class _SdkLogBridge(logging.Handler):

Description: A specialized logging.Handler subclass that routes intercepted log records to an external callback while selectively forwarding records that exceed the original log level threshold to the logger's parent handlers.

class _SdkLogBridge(logging.Handler):
    """Every record of one SDK logger, opened to a lower level, goes to ``on_record`` (the retry notices); on to the
    rest of logging go only the records the logger let through before, exactly as before (``callHandlers`` of its
    parent: the handlers up the tree, else Python's last-resort stderr handler). So opening it changes nothing else
    that is printed: a root handler some library adds never gets the SDK's debug records, which hold whole prompts,
    and the SDK's warnings still reach stderr."""

    def __init__(self, logger: logging.Logger, passthrough: int, on_record):
        super().__init__(logging.NOTSET)
        self.logger, self.passthrough, self.on_record = logger, passthrough, on_record

    def emit(self, record):
        with contextlib.suppress(Exception):  # a notice never breaks a request
            self.on_record(record)
        if record.levelno >= self.passthrough and self.logger.parent is not None:
            self.logger.parent.callHandlers(record)

The _SdkLogBridge class solves a common issue in LLM application telemetry: third-party provider SDKs often emit transient HTTP retry notices only at DEBUG or INFO logging levels. However, opening up those loggers globally can leak prompt text or payload bodies to standard output. By installing _SdkLogBridge, all log records at or above the newly opened level are delivered to on_record, while only records meeting the original passthrough threshold are propagated to parent handlers.

docs.title: _SdkLogBridge.__init__()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private (Public within class scope)

Signature: def __init__(self, logger: logging.Logger, passthrough: int, on_record):

Description: Initializes the _SdkLogBridge handler with its target logger instance, passthrough level ceiling, and record interception callback.

Parameters:

  • logger (logging.Logger): The logger instance being bridged.
  • passthrough (int): The original logging level threshold that records must satisfy to pass to parent handlers.
  • on_record (Callable[[logging.LogRecord], None]): The callback invoked for every record intercepted by this bridge.

Returns:

  • None: Constructor returns nothing.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_common.py
def __init__(self, logger: logging.Logger, passthrough: int, on_record):
    super().__init__(logging.NOTSET)
    self.logger, self.passthrough, self.on_record = logger, passthrough, on_record

The constructor passes logging.NOTSET to the superclass logging.Handler, ensuring that the handler itself performs no level-based filtering and receives all records permitted by the logger's lowered threshold. It then binds logger, passthrough, and on_record to instance attributes for use during record emission.

docs.title: _SdkLogBridge.emit()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private (Public within class scope)

Signature: def emit(self, record):

Description: Handles an intercepted logging.LogRecord by safely invoking the registered callback and conditionally forwarding the record to the logger's parent handlers.

Parameters:

  • record (logging.LogRecord): The log record emitted by the target SDK logger.

Returns:

  • None: Emits the record or swallows internal callback exceptions.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_common.py
def emit(self, record):
    with contextlib.suppress(Exception):  # a notice never breaks a request
        self.on_record(record)
    if record.levelno >= self.passthrough and self.logger.parent is not None:
        self.logger.parent.callHandlers(record)

emit executes a defensive telemetry pattern. It wraps invocation of self.on_record(record) inside a contextlib.suppress(Exception) block to guarantee that any error inside the diagnostic telemetry callback does not abort live inference requests. After running the callback, it evaluates whether the record's level matches or exceeds self.passthrough. If so, and the logger has a parent configured, it invokes self.logger.parent.callHandlers(record) to maintain default warning and error visibility on stderr.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
utils/llm_common.py defines and enforces specific error handling patterns across the inference lifecycle:

  1. Refusal Classification via LLMRefusalError: The module uses LLMRefusalError (subclassing Python's built-in RuntimeError) to trap provider refusals. The error carries a .retryable flag:

    • Non-retryable Refusals (retryable=False): Used for policy blocks, copyright violations, or safety rejections tied deterministically to the input prompt (e.g., Anthropic safety declinations). These are registered in _refused via remember_refusal(). Subsequent attempts to execute the same prompt check previous_refusal() and fail fast without network transmission.
    • Retryable Refusals (retryable=True): Used for output-side sampling rejections (e.g., Gemini RECITATION or candidate safety filters, OpenRouter moderation). These are not cached, allowing caller retry loops to resample with varied temperature or random seeds.

  2. Defensive Callback Isolation: In _SdkLogBridge.emit(), calls to the user-supplied on_record(record) callback are wrapped in contextlib.suppress(Exception). This pattern guarantees that unexpected errors during telemetry parsing or log emission never interrupt ongoing LLM requests.

  3. Fallback Value Initialization: Numeric metric functions (record_usage, record_estimate) defensively normalize falsy or missing parameter values (e.g., input_tokens or 0, cost is None), preventing TypeError exceptions during ledger accumulation.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
Building on the telemetry, token accounting, and refusal-handling mechanisms established in utils/llm_common.py, llm_config.py acts as the single source of truth for Large Language Model configuration, provider routing, context-window management, and credential preflight verification. It was extracted from call_llm.py to decouple the core dispatch engine from tokenizer token-counting utilities (token_utils.py), eliminating what was previously a cyclic dependency. Modules across the pipeline—including main.py, token_utils.py, and provider adapters—rely on this module to determine active endpoints, authentication parameters, thinking budgets, and context window limits.

The module provides deterministic resolution across three supported provider backends: Google Gemini (both Vertex AI enterprise multi-region endpoints and Google AI Studio REST endpoints), Anthropic Claude (supporting direct API keys, auth tokens, Workload Identity Federation, and ant auth login OAuth profiles), and OpenRouter (incorporating an automated dynamic model catalog cache with exponential retry cooldowns). It normalizes disparate vendor naming conventions into unified model families, maps abstract reasoning effort tiers (minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max) into vendor-specific API structures, and enforces output token caps.

Furthermore, llm_config.py executes early, fail-fast credential preflights prior to pipeline execution. Rather than allowing authentication failures to manifest mid-run after extensive crawling and analysis stages have completed, the preflight routines validate SDK installations, verify environment variables or OAuth credential profiles, inspect minimum client library versions, and verify access against provider metadata services.

docs.title: anthropic_output_cap()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def anthropic_output_cap() -> int | None:

Description: Resolves the user-configured maximum output token limit for Anthropic Claude requests by reading the ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS environment variable. If the variable is unset, empty, non-numeric, or less than or equal to zero, it evaluates to None.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • int | None: The parsed positive integer token ceiling, or None if unset or invalid.

Raises:

None.

Example:

# utils/llm_config.py: lines 126-128
def anthropic_output_cap() -> int | None:
    """ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS as an int, or None when unset/invalid."""
    return _env_int("ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS")

The function delegates to the internal _env_int() helper to safely parse ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS. It protects pipeline operations from runtime type crashes caused by whitespace or non-digit input. When configured, this cap takes precedence over default effort-based output ceilings.

docs.title: anthropic_output_budget()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def anthropic_output_budget(thinking_level: str | None) -> int:

Description: Determines the allocated output token budget for adaptive Anthropic Claude models based on the specified reasoning effort level. The value is extracted from ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT and clamped by any active ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS limit.

Parameters:

  • thinking_level (str | None): Desired thinking effort level (e.g., "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max"), or None for default effort.

Returns:

  • int: Allocated token budget for the response payload, including thinking tokens.

Raises:

None.

Example:

# utils/llm_config.py: lines 131-136
def anthropic_output_budget(thinking_level: str | None) -> int:
    """Per-effort table value capped by ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS (adaptive models)."""
    level = thinking_level.lower() if thinking_level else None
    budget = ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT.get(level, ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT[None])
    cap = anthropic_output_cap()
    return min(budget, cap) if cap else budget

This method normalizes the input thinking_level to lowercase and queries ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT. If an unrecognized or None tier is passed, it falls back to the baseline default of 64,000 tokens. When an administrative cap is returned by anthropic_output_cap(), min() ensures that the final budget does not exceed user constraints.

docs.title: anthropic_effort()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def anthropic_effort(model: str, level: str | None) -> str | None:

Description: Translates an abstract thinking level string into a vendor-supported output_config.effort parameter accepted by the Anthropic Claude API. It handles legacy downgrades such as aliasing "minimal" to "low", and clamping "xhigh" to "high" on Claude 4.6 family models that predate the "xhigh" tier.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The target Claude model identifier.
  • level (str | None): Requested reasoning effort level.

Returns:

  • str | None: Validated effort string ("low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", or "max"), or None if the input is unsupported or empty.

Raises:

None.

Example:

# utils/llm_config.py: lines 139-151
def anthropic_effort(model: str, level: str | None) -> str | None:
    """Thinking level → effort the model accepts: minimal → low, xhigh → high on the 4.6 family,
    unknown values → None (model default)."""
    if not level:
        return None
    level = level.lower()
    if level == "minimal":
        level = "low"
    if level not in ANTHROPIC_EFFORT_LEVELS:
        return None
    if level == "xhigh" and (model or "").lower().startswith(ANTHROPIC_NO_XHIGH_PREFIXES):
        return "high"
    return level

The function normalizes input casing before evaluating membership against ANTHROPIC_EFFORT_LEVELS. If the model identifier begins with any prefix in ANTHROPIC_NO_XHIGH_PREFIXES (such as claude-opus-4-6 or claude-sonnet-4-6), requesting "xhigh" is automatically remapped to "high" to prevent HTTP 400 validation failures. Unrecognized levels evaluate to None, directing the downstream caller to rely on the model's server-side default.

docs.title: anthropic_planned_output()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def anthropic_planned_output(model: str, thinking_level: str | None) -> int:

Description: Computes the expected max_tokens reservation for an upcoming Anthropic invocation prior to context-window clamping. It branches between modern adaptive thinking models (which reserve output directly via anthropic_output_budget) and legacy pre-adaptive models such as Haiku 4.5 (which combine explicit budget_tokens with a fixed reply token allowance).

Parameters:

  • model (str): Anthropic model name or identifier string.
  • thinking_level (str | None): Desired thinking effort level.

Returns:

  • int: Total output token count to reserve in request headers and prompt budget calculations.

Raises:

None.

Example:

# utils/llm_config.py: lines 154-163
def anthropic_planned_output(model: str, thinking_level: str | None) -> int:
    """Claude max_tokens the request will plan for (before the model/context ceiling): the per-effort
    table on adaptive models, budget_tokens + 16K on pre-adaptive ones (Haiku 4.5), capped by
    ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS. Shared by llm_anthropic and token_utils.input_token_budget."""
    effort = anthropic_effort(model, thinking_level)
    if (model or "").lower().startswith(ANTHROPIC_ADAPTIVE_PREFIXES):
        return anthropic_output_budget(effort)
    planned = ANTHROPIC_BUDGET_BY_LEVEL.get(effort, 0) + ANTHROPIC_BUDGET_REPLY_TOKENS
    cap = anthropic_output_cap()
    return min(planned, cap) if cap else planned

The routine evaluates whether model begins with any prefix listed in ANTHROPIC_ADAPTIVE_PREFIXES. For adaptive models, it delegates token allocation to anthropic_output_budget(). For pre-adaptive architectures, it looks up the explicit thinking budget in ANTHROPIC_BUDGET_BY_LEVEL (defaulting to 0) and adds ANTHROPIC_BUDGET_REPLY_TOKENS (16,000 tokens), clamping the result to ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS if defined.

docs.title: gemini_thinking_mode()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def gemini_thinking_mode(model: str) -> tuple[str, object]:

Description: Inspects a Gemini model string and returns its supported thinking configuration mode and allowed parameter ranges. It categorizes models into categorical effort levels (gemini-3.x), numeric token budgets (gemini-2.5), or unsupported models (gemini-1.x and non-text variants).

Parameters:

  • model (str): Raw or qualified Gemini model name.

Returns:

  • tuple[str, object]: A two-element tuple consisting of:
    • mode (str): Either "level", "budget", or "none".
    • spec (object): For "level", a tuple of valid strings (e.g., ("low", "medium", "high")); for "budget", a tuple (min_tokens, max_tokens, can_disable); for "none", None.

Raises:

None.

Example:

# utils/llm_config.py: lines 166-180
def gemini_thinking_mode(model: str) -> tuple[str, object]:
    """('level', allowed_levels) for Gemini 3.x, ('budget', (min, max, can_disable)) for 2.5,
    ('none', None) for models without a thinking control the project maps."""
    name = gemini_model_id(model)
    for prefix, low, high, can_disable in GEMINI_BUDGET_RANGES:
        if name.startswith(prefix):
            return "budget", (low, high, can_disable)
    if not name.startswith("gemini-") or name.startswith(("gemini-1", "gemini-2")):
        return "none", None  # 1.x / 2.0, other 2.5 variants (image, live, TTS) and non-Gemini ids
    for prefix, levels in GEMINI_THINKING_LEVELS:
        if name.startswith(prefix):
            return "level", levels
    # Other 3.x ids, '-latest' aliases (gemini-flash-latest, gemini-pro-latest) and newer families:
    # the level set every documented 3.x model accepts (a model that rejects it is handled at runtime).
    return "level", GEMINI_3_DEFAULT_LEVELS

The function extracts the bare model name using gemini_model_id() and iterates over GEMINI_BUDGET_RANGES to identify legacy Gemini 2.5 models requiring ThinkingConfig.thinking_budget. Non-Gemini IDs and older generations (1.x, 2.0) return ("none", None). For modern Gemini 3.x models, it checks GEMINI_THINKING_LEVELS by prefix, defaulting unknown 3.x variants and aliases to GEMINI_3_DEFAULT_LEVELS.
