Signature: def gemini_model_id(model: str) -> str:

Description: Strips Google API resource path prefixes (such as models/ or publishers/google/models/) and normalizes casing to isolate the bare Gemini model slug.

Parameters:

  • model (str): Qualified or unqualified Gemini model identifier.

Returns:

  • str: Stripped, lowercased model identifier.

Raises:

None.

Example:

# utils/llm_config.py: lines 183-185
def gemini_model_id(model: str) -> str:
    """'models/gemini-3.8-flash' / 'publishers/google/models/gemini-3.8-flash' → 'gemini-3.8-flash'."""
    return (model or "").strip().lower().rsplit("/", 1)[-1]

This utility performs defensive string parsing by converting empty or None inputs to empty strings, stripping leading and trailing whitespace, applying .lower(), and extracting the final substring following the last slash separator (/).

docs.title: gemini_vertex_locations()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def gemini_vertex_locations(model: str) -> tuple | None:

Description: Determines the permissible Google Cloud Vertex AI deployment regions that host a specific Gemini model family.

Parameters:

  • model (str): Model identifier to evaluate.

Returns:

  • tuple | None: A tuple of valid region strings (e.g., ("global", "us", "eu")), or None if the model is available across standard regional endpoints.

Raises:

None.

Example:

# utils/llm_config.py: lines 188-194
def gemini_vertex_locations(model: str) -> tuple | None:
    """Vertex AI locations that serve a Gemini 3.x model (None = any, including regional endpoints)."""
    name = gemini_model_id(model)
    for prefix, locations in GEMINI_VERTEX_LOCATIONS:
        if name.startswith(prefix):
            return locations
    return GEMINI_3_VERTEX_LOCATIONS if name.startswith("gemini-3") else None

The function extracts the bare model ID and performs longest-prefix matching against the GEMINI_VERTEX_LOCATIONS table. If a specific prefix matches, its designated location tuple is returned. If no specific entry matches but the model belongs to the Gemini 3 family (gemini-3*), it defaults to GEMINI_3_VERTEX_LOCATIONS (("global", "us", "eu")); otherwise, it returns None.

docs.title: gemini_output_budget()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def gemini_output_budget(thinking_level: str | None, output_limit: int | None = None) -> int:

Description: Calculates the planned max_output_tokens reservation for Gemini generation requests. The budget is derived from the requested thinking effort level, clamped by the model's physical output limit, and capped by GEMINI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS.

Parameters:

  • thinking_level (str | None): Desired thinking effort level.
  • output_limit (int | None, default: None): Hard output ceiling supported by the model. Defaults to GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS[1] (65,536 tokens).

Returns:

  • int: Clamped output token budget.

Raises:

None.

Example:

# utils/llm_config.py: lines 197-204
def gemini_output_budget(thinking_level: str | None, output_limit: int | None = None) -> int:
    """Planned Gemini max_output_tokens: per-level table, capped by the model output limit and
    GEMINI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS. Shared by llm_gemini (request) and token_utils (prompt budget)."""
    level = thinking_level.lower() if thinking_level else None
    budget = GEMINI_OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT.get(level, GEMINI_OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT[None])
    budget = min(budget, output_limit or GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS[1])
    cap = _env_int("GEMINI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS")
    return min(budget, cap) if cap else budget

The method matches the lowercase thinking_level against GEMINI_OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT. It clamps the resulting allocation to the lower of the table value and the model's reported limit (falling back to 65,536). Finally, if GEMINI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS is present in the environment, the budget is bounded by that cap.

docs.title: openrouter_output_budget()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def openrouter_output_budget(model: str, thinking_level: str | None) -> int | None:

Description: Computes the planned output token budget for models served via the OpenRouter gateway. It balances the effort tier allocation against the model's published catalog limits (top_provider.max_completion_tokens) and user overrides.

Parameters:

  • model (str): OpenRouter model slug.
  • thinking_level (str | None): Desired thinking effort tier.

Returns:

  • int | None: Resolved output token ceiling, or None if the model is absent from the OpenRouter catalog (instructing downstream callers to omit explicit limits).

Raises:

None.

Example:

# utils/llm_config.py: lines 207-219
def openrouter_output_budget(model: str, thinking_level: str | None) -> int | None:
    """Planned OpenRouter max_tokens: shared per-effort table, capped by the catalog's
    top_provider.max_completion_tokens and OPENROUTER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS. None when the model is not
    in the catalog (unknown limits, e.g. a non-OpenRouter proxy): max_tokens is then omitted."""
    info = openrouter_model_info(model)
    if info is None:
        return _env_int("OPENROUTER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS")
    level = thinking_level.lower() if thinking_level else None
    budget = OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT.get(level, OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT[None])
    model_cap = (info.get("top_provider") or {}).get("max_completion_tokens")
    budget = min(budget, model_cap) if model_cap else min(budget, 32_000)
    cap = _env_int("OPENROUTER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS")
    return min(budget, cap) if cap else budget

The function checks openrouter_model_info() for metadata. If metadata is unavailable, it returns OPENROUTER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS (which may be None). When catalog metadata is present, it looks up the effort tier in OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT, bounds the budget by top_provider.max_completion_tokens (or 32,000 if omitted), and applies OPENROUTER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS as an upper limit.

docs.title: context_output_reserve()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def context_output_reserve(thinking_level: str | None) -> int | None:

Description: Calculates how many output tokens must be reserved from the overall context window for the active provider.

Parameters:

  • thinking_level (str | None): Desired reasoning effort level.

Returns:

  • int | None: Token count to reserve from context. Returns 0 for Gemini (since input and output token pools are independent), the planned max tokens for Anthropic/OpenRouter, or None for unmanaged providers.

Raises:

None.

Example:

# utils/llm_config.py: lines 222-233
def context_output_reserve(thinking_level: str | None) -> int | None:
    """Output tokens that share the context window with the prompt, for the active provider.
    ANTHROPIC / OPENROUTER: the planned max_tokens (thinking included). GEMINI: 0 — Gemini's input and
    output limits are separate. None: the provider does not size output (5% reserve in token_utils)."""
    provider, model, _, _ = resolve_llm_settings()
    if provider == "ANTHROPIC":
        return anthropic_planned_output(model, thinking_level)
    if provider == "GEMINI":
        return 0
    if provider == "OPENROUTER":
        return openrouter_output_budget(model, thinking_level)
    return None

This method calls resolve_llm_settings() to inspect the runtime provider. For Anthropic and OpenRouter, output generation directly consumes capacity from the shared model context window, requiring explicit deduction via anthropic_planned_output() or openrouter_output_budget(). For Gemini, input and output limits do not share a context budget, so the function returns 0. If the provider is unrecognized, returning None prompts token_utils to apply a generic fallback reserve of 5%.

docs.title: get_llm_provider()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def get_llm_provider() -> str | None:

Description: Resolves the active LLM provider identity from system environment variables. Explicit configuration via LLM_PROVIDER takes absolute priority; otherwise, the presence of Gemini credentials selects GEMINI as a legacy fallback.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • str | None: The uppercase provider key ("GEMINI", "ANTHROPIC", "OPENROUTER", or a custom identifier), or None if unconfigured.

Raises:

None.

Example:

# utils/llm_config.py: lines 236-248
def get_llm_provider() -> str | None:
    """Determine the LLM provider from environment variables.

    Explicit LLM_PROVIDER wins; otherwise Gemini credentials select GEMINI (legacy default).
    ANTHROPIC is never auto-selected: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is often exported globally for other
    tools (e.g. Claude Code), and a silent switch to a paid Claude run would be surprising.
    """
    provider = os.getenv("LLM_PROVIDER")
    if provider:
        return provider.strip().upper()
    if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID") or os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"):
        return "GEMINI"
    return None

The function reads LLM_PROVIDER and strips and uppercases its value. If omitted, it inspects GEMINI_PROJECT_ID or GEMINI_API_KEY. As documented in the code, ANTHROPIC is never auto-selected without an explicit LLM_PROVIDER=ANTHROPIC declaration, preventing accidental billing if developer environments have ambient Claude API keys configured for other tools.

docs.title: resolve_llm_settings()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def resolve_llm_settings() -> tuple[str, str, str, str]:

Description: Serves as the global source of truth for runtime LLM execution settings across the entire codebase. It evaluates environment variables and credentials to produce a normalized configuration tuple containing the provider name, target model, network endpoint, and authentication key.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • tuple[str, str, str, str]: A 4-element tuple structured as (provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key).

Raises:

None.

Example:

# utils/llm_config.py: lines 266-293
def resolve_llm_settings() -> tuple[str, str, str, str]:
    """Return (provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key) for the active provider."""
    provider = get_llm_provider()
    if provider == "GEMINI":
        model = os.getenv("GEMINI_MODEL") or DEFAULT_GEMINI_MODEL
        if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
            location = gemini_location().lower()
            if location == "global":
                host = "aiplatform.googleapis.com"
            elif location in ("us", "eu"):
                host = f"aiplatform.{location}.rep.googleapis.com"  # multi-region endpoints
            else:
                host = f"{location}-aiplatform.googleapis.com"
            return provider, model, host, ""
        return provider, model, "generativelanguage.googleapis.com", os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY", "")
    if provider == "ANTHROPIC":
        endpoint = os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL") or DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_ENDPOINT
        return provider, os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_MODEL") or DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_MODEL, endpoint, os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", "")
    if provider == "OPENROUTER":
        return provider, os.getenv("OPENROUTER_MODEL", "unknown"), openrouter_base_url(), os.getenv("OPENROUTER_API_KEY", "")
    if provider:
        return (
            provider,
            os.getenv(f"{provider}_MODEL", "unknown"),
            os.getenv(f"{provider}_BASE_URL", "unknown"),
            os.getenv(f"{provider}_API_KEY", ""),
        )
    return "UNKNOWN", "unknown", "unknown", ""

This coordinator queries get_llm_provider() to branch logic:

  1. For GEMINI, it selects Vertex AI endpoints if GEMINI_PROJECT_ID is defined (configuring multi-region hostnames like aiplatform.us.rep.googleapis.com or location-specific hostnames like us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com), leaving the API key empty for Google Cloud SDK authentication. If running under AI Studio, it configures generativelanguage.googleapis.com with GEMINI_API_KEY.
  2. For ANTHROPIC, it extracts ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (defaulting to https://api.anthropic.com), ANTHROPIC_MODEL (defaulting to claude-sonnet-5), and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
  3. For OPENROUTER, it supplies OPENROUTER_MODEL, openrouter_base_url(), and OPENROUTER_API_KEY.
  4. For arbitrary custom providers, it dynamically reads {PROVIDER}_MODEL, {PROVIDER}_BASE_URL, and {PROVIDER}_API_KEY. If no provider can be identified, it returns fallback sentinel values ("UNKNOWN", "unknown", "unknown", "").

Signature: def rejects_sampling_params(model_name: str) -> bool:

Description: Identifies reasoning-focused models that reject or ignore traditional temperature, top_p, and top_k sampling parameters. This prevents client HTTP 400 errors from strict APIs such as Claude Opus 4.7+, Claude 5, and Gemini 3.x.

Parameters:

Returns:

# utils/llm_config.py: lines 332-336
def rejects_sampling_params(model_name: str) -> bool:
    """True for models that reject or ignore temperature/top_p/top_k: Claude Opus 4.7+, Opus/Sonnet 5,
    Fable, Mythos (400), and Gemini 3.x (deprecated; ignored or erroring on some endpoints)."""
    name = _catalog_model_id(model_name)
    return _normalize_claude_id(name).startswith(_NO_SAMPLING_PREFIXES) or "gemini-3" in name.lower()

The function first resolves any gateway alias using _catalog_model_id(). It then verifies whether the normalized model string begins with any prefix in _NO_SAMPLING_PREFIXES (e.g., claude-opus-4-7, claude-sonnet-5) or contains "gemini-3". Downstream callers such as call_llm.py and provider adapters inspect this result to strip sampling arguments before serializing HTTP payloads.

docs.title: get_token_ratio()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def get_token_ratio() -> float:

Description: Resolves the static token expansion multiplier mapping standard tiktoken (cl100k) token counts to the active model's native tokenizer.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • float: Multiplier prior used for context budgeting.

Raises:

None.

Example:

# utils/llm_config.py: lines 351-367
def get_token_ratio() -> float:
    """Multiplier from tiktoken (cl100k) counts to the active model's tokenizer.

    tiktoken undercounts Claude tokens (more so on code), so budgets computed with raw counts can
    overflow the real context window. Claude: ANTHROPIC_TOKEN_RATIO, default 1.55 for the tokenizer
    introduced with Opus 4.7 and 1.2 for 4.6 and older. Gemini: GEMINI_TOKEN_RATIO (default 1.0).
    Others: LLM_TOKEN_RATIO (default 1.0). This is the static prior: token_utils.token_ratio() corrects it
    with the ratio observed in provider-reported usage.
    """
    provider, model_name, _, _ = resolve_llm_settings()
    model_name = _catalog_model_id(model_name)
    if is_claude_model(provider, model_name):
        claude_id = _normalize_claude_id(model_name)  # also handles gateway ids on the native provider
        default = CLAUDE_TOKEN_RATIO_NEW_TOKENIZER if claude_id.startswith(_NEW_TOKENIZER_PREFIXES) else CLAUDE_TOKEN_RATIO_OLD_TOKENIZER
        return max(_ratio_from_env("ANTHROPIC_TOKEN_RATIO", default), 1.0)
    if is_gemini_model(provider, model_name):
        return _ratio_from_env("GEMINI_TOKEN_RATIO", 1.0)
    return _ratio_from_env("LLM_TOKEN_RATIO", 1.0)

The function obtains active settings via resolve_llm_settings() and resolves aliases via _catalog_model_id(). For Claude models, it differentiates between modern tokenizers (_NEW_TOKENIZER_PREFIXES, defaulting to 1.55) and legacy tokenizers (defaulting to 1.2), allowing overrides via ANTHROPIC_TOKEN_RATIO (enforcing a minimum floor of 1.0). For Gemini and other architectures, it reads GEMINI_TOKEN_RATIO or LLM_TOKEN_RATIO (defaulting to 1.0). These static priors serve as initial calibration points before token_utils updates ratios based on live usage.

docs.title: openrouter_catalog()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def openrouter_catalog() -> list | None:

Description: Fetches and caches the model list from the OpenRouter /v1/models endpoint. It handles transient network failures using an exponential backoff cooldown and marks permanent client errors (such as 4xx status codes other than 408/429) to avoid redundant requests during a pipeline run.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • list | None: A list of dictionary objects representing model entries, or None if the catalog cannot be retrieved.

Raises:

None. (Internal requests.RequestException and ValueError instances are caught and logged).

Example:

# utils/llm_config.py: lines 396-431
def openrouter_catalog() -> list | None:
    """The model catalog, or None when it could not be fetched (yet). Every failed fetch is announced:
    ``CATALOG_RETRY`` (fetched again when next needed, after the doubling cooldown) or, for a permanent failure,
    ``CATALOG_GAVE_UP``; a fetch that succeeds after failures says so (``CATALOG_LOADED``)."""
    global _openrouter_models_cache, _openrouter_last_failure, _openrouter_failures, _openrouter_gave_up
    if _openrouter_models_cache is not None:
        return _openrouter_models_cache
    if _openrouter_gave_up or (_openrouter_last_failure and time.time() - _openrouter_last_failure < _catalog_cooldown()):
        return None
    url = f"{openrouter_base_url()}/v1/models"
    from utils.output import brief, emit

    try:
        resp = requests.get(url, timeout=20)
        resp.raise_for_status()
        data = resp.json().get("data")
        if not isinstance(data, list):
            raise ValueError("OpenRouter model catalog response has no 'data' list")
        _openrouter_models_cache = data
        if _openrouter_failures:
            emit("CATALOG_LOADED", attempt=_openrouter_failures + 1)
        return data
    except Exception as e:
        from utils.llm_common import warn_once

        _openrouter_last_failure = time.time()
        _openrouter_failures += 1
        if warn_once("openrouter_catalog_unavailable"):  # what the run does without it, once
            emit("WARN_OPENROUTER_CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE", url=url, error=brief(e, 200))
        status = getattr(getattr(e, "response", None), "status_code", None)
        if isinstance(e, ValueError) or (isinstance(status, int) and 400 <= status < 500 and status not in (408, 429)):
            _openrouter_gave_up = True  # the endpoint answers, but not with a catalog: asking again will not help
            emit("CATALOG_GAVE_UP", attempt=_openrouter_failures, error=brief(e, 200))
        else:
            emit("CATALOG_RETRY", attempt=_openrouter_failures, error=brief(e, 200), wait=f"{_catalog_cooldown():.0f}")
        return None

The function returns the cached list stored in _openrouter_models_cache if available. If fetching has permanently failed (_openrouter_gave_up = True) or the exponential retry cooldown (_catalog_cooldown()) has not elapsed, it exits immediately and returns None. Otherwise, it issues an HTTP GET with a 20-second timeout. If the request fails, it updates _openrouter_last_failure, increments _openrouter_failures, emits diagnostic events via utils.output.emit(), and classifies the failure as permanent (setting _openrouter_gave_up = True on malformed responses or non-retryable 4xx status codes) or transient.

docs.title: openrouter_model_info()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def openrouter_model_info(model_id: str) -> dict | None:

Description: Searches the OpenRouter model catalog for a specific model entry. It supports exact ID matches, canonical slugs, routing-suffix stripping (e.g., :nitro, :floor, :thinking), dated canonical slugs, and alias_target redirects.

Parameters:

  • model_id (str): Target OpenRouter model identifier or slug.

Returns:

  • dict | None: The resolved catalog dictionary entry, or None if the model cannot be found or the catalog is unavailable.

Raises:

None.

Example:

# utils/llm_config.py: lines 434-455
def openrouter_model_info(model_id: str) -> dict | None:
    """Catalog entry for a model id: exact id, canonical_slug, routing-suffix variant
    (':nitro', ':floor', ...), dated canonical slug (e.g. 'anthropic/claude-4.6-opus' →
    'anthropic/claude-4.6-opus-20260205'), or a '~...-latest' alias's target."""
    catalog = openrouter_catalog()
    if not catalog or not model_id:
        return None
    wanted = model_id.strip()
    candidates = [wanted, *(wanted[: -len(suffix)] for suffix in _OPENROUTER_ROUTING_SUFFIXES if wanted.endswith(suffix))]
    for name in candidates:
        entry = next((m for m in catalog if m.get("id") == name or m.get("canonical_slug") == name), None)
        if entry is None:
            # Dated canonical slug only ('anthropic/claude-4.6-opus' → '…-20260205'): a looser prefix
            # match would map typos such as 'google/gemini-3.1-pro' onto a different model.
            dated = re.compile(re.escape(name) + r"-\d{8}")
            entry = next((m for m in catalog if dated.fullmatch(str(m.get("canonical_slug", "")))), None)
        if entry is not None:
            target = (entry.get("alias_target") or {}).get("slug")
            if target and target != entry.get("id"):
                return next((m for m in catalog if m.get("id") == target or m.get("canonical_slug") == target), entry)
            return entry
    return None

The method queries openrouter_catalog(). If the catalog is populated, it generates candidate slugs by stripping any routing suffixes defined in _OPENROUTER_ROUTING_SUFFIXES (such as :nitro or :thinking). For each candidate, it searches for exact matches against id or canonical_slug, followed by regex matching against dated snapshots (e.g., -\d{8}). If the matching entry specifies an alias_target slug different from its current ID, the function resolves and returns that target entry.

docs.title: get_model_context_length()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def get_model_context_length(endpoint_url: str, model_name: str, api_key: str = "") -> int:

Description: Resolves the maximum input context window capacity for a given model. It queries native provider SDK limit utilities or inspects cached catalog metadata, falling back to safe offline defaults when remote lookups fail.

Parameters:

  • endpoint_url (str): Target API endpoint or host.
  • model_name (str): Target model name.
  • api_key (str, default: ""): Optional API key.

Returns:

  • int: Maximum supported context length in tokens (defaulting to 100,000 if unresolved).

Raises:

None. (Catches exceptions and emits WARN_CONTEXT_LENGTH_FETCH).

Example:

# utils/llm_config.py: lines 461-499
def get_model_context_length(endpoint_url: str, model_name: str, api_key: str = "") -> int:
    """
    Maximum context length (input tokens) of the active model.
    ANTHROPIC: Anthropic Models API (max_input_tokens), offline fallback table.
    GEMINI: models.get(input_token_limit) on AI Studio, static 1,048,576 (Vertex, or no SDK).
    OPENROUTER: catalog top_provider.context_length, else context_length.
    Other endpoints: 100,000.
    """
    default_limit = 100000
    provider = get_llm_provider()
    try:
        if provider == "ANTHROPIC":
            from utils.llm_anthropic import get_model_limits

            return get_model_limits(model_name)[0]

        if provider == "OPENROUTER" or "openrouter.ai" in (endpoint_url or ""):
            info = openrouter_model_info(model_name)
            if info:
                return (info.get("top_provider") or {}).get("context_length") or info.get("context_length") or default_limit
            return default_limit

        if provider == "GEMINI":
            try:
                from utils.llm_gemini import get_model_limits as gemini_limits
            except ImportError:
                return GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS[0]
            return gemini_limits(model_name)[0]

        if not endpoint_url:
            return default_limit
        if "generativelanguage.googleapis.com" in endpoint_url or "gemini" in model_name.lower():
            return GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS[0]
    except Exception as e:
        from utils.output import emit

        emit("WARN_CONTEXT_LENGTH_FETCH", model=model_name, endpoint=endpoint_url, error=str(e))

    return default_limit

For Anthropic, the function delegates to utils.llm_anthropic.get_model_limits(). For OpenRouter, it reads top_provider.context_length or context_length from the catalog entry returned by openrouter_model_info(). For Gemini, it delegates to utils.llm_gemini.get_model_limits() or falls back to GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS[0] (1,048,576 tokens). For arbitrary or unresolvable endpoints, it defaults to 100,000 tokens.

docs.title: describe_thinking_support()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def describe_thinking_support(provider: str, model: str) -> str:

Description: Formats a localized, human-readable summary string detailing the active model's reasoning capabilities, supported effort tiers, or budget ranges for startup console logging.

Parameters:

  • provider (str): Target provider name.
  • model (str): Target model name.

Returns:

  • str: Localized single-line description of thinking support (e.g., "adaptive thinking + output_config.effort ∈ {low, medium, high, max}").

Raises:

None.

Example:

# utils/llm_config.py: lines 508-545
def describe_thinking_support(provider: str, model: str) -> str:
    """One-line description of how thinking levels are applied for the startup display."""
    if provider == "ANTHROPIC":
        name = (model or "").lower()
        if not name.startswith(ANTHROPIC_ADAPTIVE_PREFIXES):
            return "thinking.budget_tokens (low…max → 2,048…32,000)"
        levels = "low, medium, high, max" if name.startswith(ANTHROPIC_NO_XHIGH_PREFIXES) else "low, medium, high, xhigh, max"
        return f"adaptive thinking + output_config.effort ∈ {{{levels}}}"
    if provider == "GEMINI":
        mode, spec = gemini_thinking_mode(model)
        if mode == "level":
            return f"thinking_level ∈ {{{', '.join(spec)}}}"
        if mode == "budget":
            low, high, can_disable = spec
            return f"thinking_budget {low:,}-{high:,}" + (f" ({_ui('CFG_THINKING_BUDGET_OFF')})" if can_disable else "")
        return "—"
    if provider == "OPENROUTER":
        info = openrouter_model_info(model)
        if info is None:
            return f"reasoning.effort ({_ui('CFG_THINKING_CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE')})" if not openrouter_catalog() else "—"
        reasoning = info.get("reasoning")
        if not isinstance(reasoning, dict):
            return "reasoning.effort" if "reasoning" in (info.get("supported_parameters") or []) else "—"
        efforts = reasoning.get("supported_efforts")
        if "supported_efforts" not in reasoning and reasoning.get("supports_max_tokens"):
            text = "reasoning.max_tokens (minimal…max → 1,024…32,000)"  # llm_openrouter._REASONING_BUDGETS
        elif efforts:
            text = f"reasoning.effort ∈ {{{', '.join(e for e in efforts if e != 'none')}}}"
        else:
            text = "reasoning.effort"
        extras = [_ui("CFG_THINKING_DEFAULT_EFFORT", effort=reasoning["default_effort"])] if reasoning.get("default_effort") else []
        if reasoning.get("mandatory"):
            extras.append(_ui("CFG_THINKING_MANDATORY"))
        return text + (f" · {' · '.join(extras)}" if extras else "")
    return "—"

The method branches on the active provider. For Anthropic, it checks whether the model uses adaptive effort or legacy budget_tokens. For Gemini, it calls gemini_thinking_mode() to report either categorical levels or numeric ranges. For OpenRouter, it parses the catalog dictionary's reasoning block, extracting supported efforts, mandatory reasoning flags, and default effort settings.

docs.title: parse_ant_auth_status()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def parse_ant_auth_status(output: str) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:

Description: Parses the raw stdout and stderr generated by the Anthropic CLI command ant auth status to identify the active OAuth profile and active workspace.

Parameters:

  • output (str): Multi-line CLI output text.

Returns:

  • tuple[str | None, str | None]: A tuple structured as (credential, workspace) containing redacted profile strings, or None for unparsed fields.

Raises:

None.

Example:

# utils/llm_config.py: lines 581-605
def parse_ant_auth_status(output: str) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
    """Return (active credential, active workspace) from `ant auth status` output.

    The command's exit code is not a health signal, so read its `(active)` rows instead:
        Credentials
          (active) * Profile (user_oauth) [via active_config]       sk-ant-oat01-EXA...
        Workspace
          (active) * Workspace                                      wrkspc_01... (Engineering)
    """
    section, credential, workspace = None, None, None
    for line in output.splitlines():
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        if not line[0].isspace():
            header = line.strip().lower()
            section = header if header in ("credentials", "workspace") else None
            continue
        if "(active)" not in line:
            continue
        text = re.sub(r"\s{2,}", " ", _redact(re.sub(r"^\s*\(active\)\s*\*?\s*", "", line))).strip()
        if section == "workspace":
            workspace = workspace or text
        else:
            credential = credential or text
    return credential, workspace

Because the ant CLI tool does not use exit codes as a reliable health indicator, this parser processes its output line by line. It identifies top-level section headers (credentials and workspace) and matches indented lines containing the marker (active). It strips leading whitespace, redacts raw token strings using _redact(), and returns the active credential profile and workspace.

docs.title: check_anthropic_auth()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def check_anthropic_auth() -> bool:

Description: Performs preflight credential verification when using the Anthropic provider. It checks for SDK availability, active API keys, auth tokens, Workload Identity Federation settings, and OAuth credentials managed via the ant CLI.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • bool: True if valid credentials are confirmed or the provider is not Anthropic; False if authentication is missing or unverified.

Raises:

None.

Example:

# utils/llm_config.py: lines 621-686
def check_anthropic_auth() -> bool:
    """Preflight for LLM_PROVIDER=ANTHROPIC. Returns False (after printing instructions) when
    the run cannot authenticate; True otherwise, including for every other provider.

    Order: anthropic package installed → ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN →
    Workload Identity Federation env vars → `ant auth status` (active login profile) →
    stored login files when the `ant` CLI is not installed.
    """
    from utils.output import emit, emit_raw

    if get_llm_provider() != "ANTHROPIC":
        return True
    if not _anthropic_sdk_installed():
        emit("ERROR_ANTHROPIC_SDK_MISSING")
        return False

    if _env_set("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY") and _env_set("ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN"):
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_KEY_AND_TOKEN")
    if _env_set("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"):
        emit("ANTHROPIC_AUTH_OK", source="ANTHROPIC_API_KEY")
        return True
    if _env_set("ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN"):
        emit("ANTHROPIC_AUTH_OK", source="ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN")
        return True
    if all(_env_set(v) for v in _FEDERATION_VARS) and (_env_set("ANTHROPIC_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE") or _env_set("ANTHROPIC_IDENTITY_TOKEN")):
        emit("ANTHROPIC_AUTH_OK", source="Workload Identity Federation")
        return True

    # No key: the SDK falls back to an `ant auth login` profile. Verify one is active.
    ant = shutil.which("ant")
    if not ant:
        stored = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(_anthropic_config_dir(), "credentials", "*.json")))
        if stored:
            emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_ANT_MISSING_LOGIN_FOUND", path=stored[0])
            return True
        emit("ERROR_ANTHROPIC_NO_CREDENTIALS")
        _emit_auth_help(ant_installed=False)
        return False

    # Run with the same environment the SDK will see; empty key variables are dropped so the
    # CLI reports the profile the SDK will actually use (the SDK treats empty as unset).
    env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if not (k in ("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", "ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN") and not v.strip())}
    try:
        result = subprocess.run([ant, "auth", "status"], capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", timeout=30, env=env)
    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as e:
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_AUTH_UNVERIFIED", error=str(e))
        return True

    output = f"{result.stdout}\n{result.stderr}"
    credential, workspace = parse_ant_auth_status(output)
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"ant auth status | exit={result.returncode}\n{_redact(output).strip()}", dest="LOG")
    if not credential:
        emit("ERROR_ANTHROPIC_NOT_LOGGED_IN")
        details = _redact(output).strip()
        if details:
            emit_raw("INFO", "\n".join(f"    {line}" for line in details.splitlines()))
        _emit_auth_help(ant_installed=True)
        return False

    source = _ui("AUTH_SOURCE_ANT_LOGIN", credential=credential)
    if workspace:
        source += f" | {_ui('AUTH_SOURCE_WORKSPACE', workspace=workspace)}"
    emit("ANTHROPIC_AUTH_OK", source=source)
    return True

This preflight routine runs through several authentication checks:

  1. Validates whether the anthropic Python SDK is installed via _anthropic_sdk_installed().
  2. Inspects ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN.
  3. Verifies Workload Identity Federation variables (_FEDERATION_VARS alongside ANTHROPIC_IDENTITY_TOKEN or its file counterpart).
  4. If explicit tokens are missing, it looks for the ant CLI tool on PATH. If missing, it checks for stored JSON profile files in _anthropic_config_dir().
  5. If ant is found, it runs ant auth status in a 30-second subprocess. It parses active credentials via parse_ant_auth_status(), logging redacted diagnostics and printing setup guidance via _emit_auth_help() if authentication is incomplete.

docs.title: check_gemini_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def check_gemini_config() -> bool:

Description: Performs preflight validation for the Google Gemini provider. It verifies that the google-genai SDK is installed and meets version requirements, warns about retired model IDs, and checks for Google Cloud Vertex AI or AI Studio credentials.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • bool: True if the configuration and credentials are valid, False otherwise.

Raises:

None.

Example:

# utils/llm_config.py: lines 709-749
def check_gemini_config() -> bool:
    """Preflight for LLM_PROVIDER=GEMINI (or Gemini credentials without LLM_PROVIDER)."""
    from utils.output import emit

    model = os.getenv("GEMINI_MODEL") or DEFAULT_GEMINI_MODEL
    version = _installed_version("google-genai")
    if version is None:
        emit("ERROR_GEMINI_SDK_MISSING")
        return False
    if version < GEMINI_MIN_SDK:
        emit("ERROR_GEMINI_SDK_OUTDATED", version=".".join(map(str, version)), required=".".join(map(str, GEMINI_MIN_SDK)))
        return False

    retired = GEMINI_RETIRED_MODELS.get(gemini_model_id(model))
    if retired:
        replacement, aliased_on_ai_studio = retired
        if aliased_on_ai_studio and not os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
            emit("WARN_GEMINI_MODEL_RETIRED", model=model, replacement=replacement)
        else:
            emit("ERROR_GEMINI_MODEL_RETIRED", model=model, replacement=replacement)
            return False

    if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
        location = gemini_location()
        allowed = gemini_vertex_locations(model)
        if allowed is not None and location.lower() not in allowed:
            emit("WARN_GEMINI_LOCATION", location=location, model=model, allowed=", ".join(allowed))
        try:
            import google.auth

            google.auth.default()
        except Exception as e:  # DefaultCredentialsError, or google-auth missing
            emit("ERROR_GEMINI_VERTEX_CREDENTIALS", error=str(e).splitlines()[0][:200])
            return False
        emit("LLM_AUTH_OK", provider="Gemini", source=_ui("AUTH_SOURCE_VERTEX", project=os.environ["GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"], location=location))
        return True
    if _env_set("GEMINI_API_KEY"):
        emit("LLM_AUTH_OK", provider="Gemini", source=_ui("AUTH_SOURCE_AI_STUDIO"))
        return True
    emit("ERROR_GEMINI_NO_CREDENTIALS")
    return False

The preflight verifies that google-genai is installed and that its version is at least (1, 56, 0) (the minimum version supporting thinking_level). It flags retired models defined in GEMINI_RETIRED_MODELS. If GEMINI_PROJECT_ID is present, it verifies that gemini_location() matches gemini_vertex_locations(), and invokes google.auth.default() to test Vertex AI credentials. Otherwise, it checks for GEMINI_API_KEY. If neither is configured, it emits ERROR_GEMINI_NO_CREDENTIALS and returns False.

# utils/llm_config.py: lines 752-766

Signature: def check_llm_auth() -> bool:

Description: Dispatches credential and SDK preflight checks for the active provider. It is called by main() during application startup and by self-test routines in utils/call_llm.py.

# utils/llm_config.py: lines 769-778
def check_llm_auth() -> bool:

docs.title: _normalize_claude_id()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _normalize_claude_id(model_name: str) -> str:

Description: Normalizes model identifiers (such as cloud gateway paths, Bedrock ARNs, and dated aliases) into standard family-first Claude slugs (e.g., remapping anthropic/claude-4.7-opus-20260416 to claude-opus-4-7).

Parameters:

  • model_name (str): Raw or qualified model name string.

Returns:

  • str: Normalized Claude model slug.

Raises:

None.

Example:

# utils/llm_config.py: lines 299-310
def _normalize_claude_id(model_name: str) -> str:
    """Gateway/cloud IDs → bare family-first Claude ID: 'anthropic/claude-opus-4.7',
    'bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7-v1:0' and the version-first alias
    'anthropic/claude-4.7-opus-20260416' all → 'claude-opus-4-7...'."""
    name = (model_name or "").lower().replace(".", "-")
    start = name.find("claude-")
    name = name[start:] if start >= 0 else name
    match = _CLAUDE_VERSION_FIRST.match(name)
    if match:
        major, minor, family = match.groups()
        name = f"claude-{family}-{major}" + (f"-{minor}" if minor else "") + name[match.end() :]
    return name

The function converts input strings to lowercase and replaces periods with hyphens to normalize version notation. It strips provider prefixes (such as bedrock/ or anthropic/) by slicing from the first occurrence of claude-. Finally, it uses the _CLAUDE_VERSION_FIRST regular expression to remap version-first patterns (claude-4-7-opus) into family-first slugs (claude-opus-4-7).

docs.title: _ratio_from_env()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _ratio_from_env(name: str, default: float) -> float:

Description: Parses a floating-point token ratio multiplier from an environment variable, clamping the result within TOKEN_RATIO_BOUNDS.

Parameters:

  • name (str): Environment variable name.
  • default (float): Fallback multiplier value.

Returns:

  • float: Clamped token ratio within the range [0.5, 3.0].

Raises:

None.

Example:

# utils/llm_config.py: lines 339-348
def _ratio_from_env(name: str, default: float) -> float:
    """Float env ratio clamped to TOKEN_RATIO_BOUNDS; unparsable / non-finite values use the default."""
    try:
        ratio = float(os.getenv(name, default))
    except ValueError:
        ratio = default
    if not math.isfinite(ratio):
        ratio = default
    low, high = TOKEN_RATIO_BOUNDS
    return min(max(ratio, low), high)

The function wraps float() parsing in a try/except ValueError block. It verifies that the parsed value is finite using math.isfinite(), falling back to default if parsing fails or produces non-finite values (such as NaN or inf). The resulting ratio is clamped to TOKEN_RATIO_BOUNDS (0.5 to 3.0).

  • str: Path to the Anthropic configuration directory.

Raises:

None.

Example:

# utils/llm_config.py: lines 567-573
def _anthropic_config_dir() -> str:
    """Directory where `ant auth login` stores profiles (ANTHROPIC_CONFIG_DIR or the OS default)."""
    if os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_CONFIG_DIR"):
        return os.environ["ANTHROPIC_CONFIG_DIR"]
    if os.name == "nt":
        return os.path.join(os.getenv("APPDATA", os.path.expanduser("~")), "Anthropic")
    return os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), ".config", "anthropic")

The function checks ANTHROPIC_CONFIG_DIR first. Otherwise, it returns %APPDATA%\Anthropic on Windows (os.name == "nt") or ~/.config/anthropic on Unix and macOS.

docs.title: _installed_version()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _installed_version(dist: str) -> tuple[int, ...] | None:

Description: Queries the installed package distribution version and parses it into an integer tuple for version comparisons.

Parameters:

  • dist (str): Package distribution name (e.g., "google-genai").

Returns:

  • tuple[int, ...] | None: A tuple of version integers (e.g., (1, 56, 0)), or None if the package is not installed.

Raises:

None.

Example:

# utils/llm_config.py: lines 695-706
def _installed_version(dist: str) -> tuple[int, ...] | None:
    from importlib import metadata

    try:
        raw = metadata.version(dist)
    except metadata.PackageNotFoundError:
        return None
    parts = []
    for piece in raw.split(".")[:3]:
        digits = re.match(r"\d+", piece)
        parts.append(int(digits.group()) if digits else 0)
    return tuple(parts)

The function imports importlib.metadata and queries the distribution string. If PackageNotFoundError is raised, it returns None. Otherwise, it extracts up to three version components using re.match(r"\d+", piece) and converts them to an integer tuple suitable for comparison.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text: Rather than raising unhandled exceptions during execution, llm_config.py uses defensive validation and preflight checks to emit diagnostic events and return status indicators.

docs.title: Fail-Fast Preflight Verification
docs.text:
check_llm_auth(), check_anthropic_auth(), and check_gemini_config() run before pipeline execution to catch authentication and configuration problems early:

  • Missing SDK packages (e.g., google-genai or anthropic) emit descriptive error events (ERROR_ANTHROPIC_SDK_MISSING, ERROR_GEMINI_SDK_MISSING) and return False.
  • Outdated libraries (such as google-genai versions below (1, 56, 0)) emit ERROR_GEMINI_SDK_OUTDATED and return False, preventing runtime validation errors when configuring thinking levels.
  • Deprecated Gemini preview models trigger WARN_GEMINI_MODEL_RETIRED on AI Studio or hard-fail with ERROR_GEMINI_MODEL_RETIRED on Vertex AI.
  • Missing API keys or invalid CLI login states trigger setup help via _emit_auth_help() and emit notifications like ERROR_ANTHROPIC_NOT_LOGGED_IN or ERROR_GEMINI_NO_CREDENTIALS.

docs.title: OpenRouter Catalog Resiliency and Backoff
docs.text:
The OpenRouter catalog fetcher in openrouter_catalog() handles network and endpoint failures with adaptive retry logic:

  • Transient Network Failures: Connection timeouts, HTTP 408, HTTP 429, or 5xx server errors trigger an exponential cooldown (_catalog_cooldown()) that starts at 60 seconds and doubles up to 900 seconds. Failures emit CATALOG_RETRY, allowing subsequent calls to retry after the cooldown expires.
  • Permanent Endpoint Failures: Non-retryable HTTP 4xx errors (excluding 408/429) or JSON payloads missing the required data list set _openrouter_gave_up = True and emit CATALOG_GAVE_UP. This halts further catalog requests for the remainder of the run.
  • One-Time Warnings: Missing catalog data emits WARN_OPENROUTER_CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE only once per run via warn_once(), avoiding log spam while the system falls back to safe offline defaults.

docs.title: Subprocess and Environment Fault Tolerance
docs.text:
• Anthropic CLI Parsing: check_anthropic_auth() executes ant auth status within a 30-second timeout guard. OSError and subprocess.SubprocessError exceptions are trapped to emit WARN_ANTHROPIC_AUTH_UNVERIFIED, allowing execution to continue if stored credential files exist.
  • Token Redaction: _redact() masks tokens matching _TOKEN_PATTERN (sk-ant-*) before writing command output to debug logs, preventing secret leaks.
  • Numeric Parsing: _env_int() and _ratio_from_env() handle unparsable, non-numeric, or non-finite environment variables by falling back to safe defaults and clamping ratios within TOKEN_RATIO_BOUNDS.

docs.title: llm_gemini.py
docs.text: Source: utils/llm_gemini.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
Building upon the configuration, endpoint routing, and token reserve parameters established in utils/llm_config.py, this module provides the concrete Google Gemini provider implementation using the official google-genai SDK. It encapsulates all vendor-specific communication with Gemini models (Gemini 3.x and 2.5), handling request serialization, streaming transport, thought summary extraction, dynamic thinking parameter negotiation, and fine-grained token cost accounting. By centralizing the google-genai import within this module, the wider architecture avoids hard dependencies on Google's client libraries when other model providers are active.

The module interfaces with either Google AI Studio (authenticated via GEMINI_API_KEY) or Vertex AI (authenticated via GEMINI_PROJECT_ID and GEMINI_LOCATION). All completions are executed over HTTP streaming connections (generate_content_stream), which avoids premature read timeouts on extended reasoning responses that can stretch up to 1,800 seconds. Transport-level transient errors (such as HTTP 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, and 504) are automatically retried by the SDK via HttpRetryOptions and monitored through an intercepted tenacity logger that emits real-time status notices without interrupting execution.

To guarantee downstream cache integrity and prevent retry storms, llm_gemini.py performs rigorous finish reason analysis. Deterministic policy violations, blocklists, and safety filters map directly to utils/llm_common.py's LLMRefusalError, distinguishing between unretryable prompt blocks and retryable candidate stops. When generation limits truncate an output, the module returns a specialized TruncatedResponse instance that prevents partial answers from being committed to persistent disk caches. Additionally, real-time pricing calculations incorporate long-context tiers (>200K tokens), promotional introductory windows, and Vertex AI regional surcharges, directly feeding the system-wide usage ledger.

docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def get_model() -> str:

Description: Resolves the active Gemini model identifier by querying the GEMINI_MODEL environment variable. If the variable is unset or empty, it falls back to DEFAULT_GEMINI_MODEL from utils.llm_config. The resolved name is passed through gemini_model_id() to strip extraneous provider prefixes such as models/ or publishers/google/models/.

Returns:

  • str: The normalized Gemini model identifier (e.g., "gemini-3.7-flash").

Example:

model = get_model()
raw_tokens = count_tokens_raw(prompt)
max_output = _max_output_tokens(model, thinking_level)

The function reads environment configuration once per invocation, stripping resource prefixes dynamically. It ensures that downstream pricing lookups, token limit checks, and client calls receive an identifier that matches Google API conventions.

docs.title: get_model_limits()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def get_model_limits(model: str) -> tuple[int, int]:

Description: Retrieves the context window and output token capacities for a specified Gemini model as an (input_token_limit, output_token_limit) tuple. When running against Google AI Studio (i.e., when GEMINI_PROJECT_ID is not set), the function queries the live API via client.models.get(model=model) to inspect real-time server limits, falling back to static constants in GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS if the remote call fails. For Vertex AI deployments, where the SDK does not populate dynamic token limits, it bypasses the network call and returns static limits directly. Successful lookups are cached in the module-level _model_limits_cache dictionary to prevent redundant network round-trips.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The normalized Gemini model identifier.

Returns:

  • tuple[int, int]: A 2-tuple containing the maximum input tokens and maximum output tokens.

Example:

def get_model_limits(model: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """(input_token_limit, output_token_limit). AI Studio reports them via models.get; Vertex does
    not (the SDK maps no limits there), so the static Gemini 3.x / 2.5 table applies."""
    if model in _model_limits_cache:
        return _model_limits_cache[model]
    global _sdk_retries
    limits = GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS
    if not os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
        try:
            _sdk_retries = 0
            info = _get_client().models.get(model=model)
            limits = (getattr(info, "input_token_limit", None) or limits[0], getattr(info, "output_token_limit", None) or limits[1])
            emit_raw("DEBUG", f"Gemini models.get | model={model} | input={limits[0]:,} | output={limits[1]:,}", dest="LOG")
        except Exception as e:
            emit("WARN_GEMINI_MODEL_LOOKUP", model=model, error=str(e)[:200])
    _model_limits_cache[model] = limits
    return limits

The function implements in-memory memoization through _model_limits_cache. If an unexpected exception occurs while querying AI Studio, the error is truncated to 200 characters and emitted as a warning diagnostic, allowing the fallback tuple to preserve operational continuity.

docs.title: call_gemini()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def call_gemini(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: The primary public entry point for executing completions against Google Gemini models. Orchestrates token pre-estimation, output token reservation, thinking configuration formatting, streaming consumption, error handling, usage accounting, and refusal evaluation.

Parameters:

  • prompt (str): The raw text prompt submitted to the model.
  • thinking_level (str | None, optional): Desired reasoning effort (e.g., "low", "medium", "high"). Defaults to None, which uses the model's native default behavior.

Returns:

  • str: The generated text response, or an instance of TruncatedResponse (a str subclass) if generation hit output limits.

Raises:

  • LLMRefusalError: Raised when the model rejects the request due to policy blocks, safety filters, or terms recitation.
  • google.genai.errors.ClientError: Raised if the API rejects the request with an unhandled 4xx error.
  • ValueError: Raised if neither GEMINI_PROJECT_ID nor GEMINI_API_KEY is present in the environment.

docs.title: Phase 1: Request Configuration and Parameter Budgeting
docs.text:
model = get_model()
    raw_tokens = count_tokens_raw(prompt)
    max_output = _max_output_tokens(model, thinking_level)
    thinking, level_desc = _thinking_config(model, thinking_level)
    # No tools are passed, so automatic function calling is off (google-genai warns on streams otherwise).
    no_afc = types.AutomaticFunctionCallingConfig(disable=True)
    config = types.GenerateContentConfig(max_output_tokens=max_output, thinking_config=thinking, automatic_function_calling=no_afc)
    emit_raw(
        "DEBUG",
        f"Gemini request | model={model} | {level_desc} | max_output_tokens={max_output:,} | location={gemini_location() if os.getenv('GEMINI_PROJECT_ID') else 'ai-studio'}",
        dest="LOG",
    )

The execution begins by resolving the target model and counting raw prompt tokens via count_tokens_raw(). It calculates the maximum permitted output budget via _max_output_tokens() and constructs a types.ThinkingConfig object tailored to the model's architecture. Because no tool definitions are provided, automatic function calling is explicitly disabled to suppress SDK runtime warnings during streaming.

docs.title: Phase 2: Stream Execution with Fallback Recovery
docs.text:
start = time.time()
    try:
        result = _stream(model, prompt, config)
    except genai_errors.ClientError as e:
        # A model that rejects our thinking control (unknown future model, level set changed):
        # warn once and resend without it for the rest of the run.
        if getattr(e, "code", None) == 400 and thinking is not None and "think" in str(e).lower():
            _thinking_rejected.add(model)
            emit("WARN_GEMINI_THINKING_REJECTED", model=model, error=str(e)[:200])
            config = types.GenerateContentConfig(max_output_tokens=max_output, thinking_config=None, automatic_function_calling=no_afc)
            result = _stream(model, prompt, config)
        else:
            raise
    elapsed = time.time() - start

The function executes the streaming completion wrapped inside an exception guard. If Google's API returns an HTTP 400 ClientError indicating that the model rejected the specified ThinkingConfig, the module registers the model into _thinking_rejected. It then strips the thinking configuration from GenerateContentConfig and immediately retries the request once, ensuring continuity on unmapped models.

docs.title: Phase 3: Telemetry, Accounting, and Debug Output
docs.text:
if result["usage"] is not None:
        _record(model, result["usage"], raw_tokens, level_desc, result["finish"], elapsed)
    else:
        record_usage("GEMINI", model, cost=None, measured=False)  # stream carried no usage_metadata
    if is_debug() and result["thoughts"]:
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"THINKING SUMMARY:\n{result['thoughts']}", dest="LOG")

Once the stream is completely consumed, the function evaluates the captured usage_metadata. If usage metrics are available, _record() calculates pricing tiers, records ledger statistics via record_usage(), and updates token calibration ratios. If thought summaries were returned and debug logging is active, the reasoning content is emitted directly to the local diagnostic log file.

docs.title: Phase 4: Candidate Inspection and Refusal/Truncation Handling
docs.text:
if result["block_reason"] or result["finish"] in _BLOCK_FINISH_REASONS:
        category = result["block_reason"] or result["finish"]
        # A blocked prompt repeats for the same input; a stop on the candidate may pass on resampling.
        retryable = not result["block_reason"] and result["finish"] in _RETRYABLE_FINISH_REASONS
        count_event("GEMINI", "refusals")
        emit("WARN_LLM_BLOCKED_RETRYABLE" if retryable else "WARN_LLM_REFUSAL", provider="Gemini", model=model, category=category)
        raise LLMRefusalError(model, category, provider="GEMINI", retryable=retryable)
    if result["finish"] in _TRUNCATION_FINISH_REASONS:
        count_event("GEMINI", "truncations")
        emit("WARN_LLM_TRUNCATED", provider="Gemini", max_tokens=f"{max_output:,}")
        return TruncatedResponse(result["text"])
    if not result["text"]:
        emit("LLM_EMPTY_REPLY", provider="Gemini", reason=result["finish"] or "n/a")
    return result["text"]

The final phase inspects prompt block reasons and candidate finish reasons. If the request was halted by safety or policy filters, it classifies whether the refusal is deterministic (prompt-level violation) or retryable (sampling-dependent candidate stop) and raises LLMRefusalError. If the generation was halted due to MAX_TOKENS, it logs a truncation warning and wraps the text in TruncatedResponse to prevent disk caching before returning the result.

docs.title: _timeout_ms()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _timeout_ms() -> int:

Description: Parses the GEMINI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS environment variable to determine the global per-request deadline in milliseconds. Enforces a lower bound of 30.0 seconds to prevent premature disconnections, defaulting to 1,800 seconds (30 minutes) if the variable is missing or malformed.

Returns:

  • int: Total request timeout in milliseconds for types.HttpOptions.

Example:

def _timeout_ms() -> int:
    """Total per-request deadline (the SDK applies it to the whole streamed response)."""
    try:
        seconds = float(os.getenv("GEMINI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", "1800"))
    except ValueError:
        seconds = 1800.0
    return int(max(seconds, 30.0) * 1000)

Because the google-genai SDK applies timeouts across the entire duration of a streamed response rather than as an idle socket timeout, extended reasoning sequences require generous deadlines. Parsing failures gracefully fall back to the 1,800.0-second default.

docs.title: _sdk_retry_record()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _sdk_retry_record(record) -> None:

Description: Log record interceptor attached to the google_genai._api_client logger via open_sdk_logger. Matches tenacity retry log lines emitted before sleeping, extracts the planned wait time and underlying exception cause, increments the internal _sdk_retries counter, and broadcasts an LLM_HTTP_RETRY telemetry event.

Parameters:

  • record (logging.LogRecord): The standard Python logging record intercepted from the SDK HTTP transport layer.

Example:

def _sdk_retry_record(record) -> None:
    """Reads the SDK's own retry record (tenacity's before-sleep line on ``google_genai._api_client``, through
    ``open_sdk_logger``: ``Retrying … in T seconds as it raised ServerError: 503 …``) into ``LLM_HTTP_RETRY``."""
    global _sdk_retries
    match = _TENACITY_RETRY_RE.match(record.getMessage())
    if match:
        _sdk_retries += 1
        emit(
            "LLM_HTTP_RETRY",
            provider="Gemini",
            attempt=_sdk_retries,
            attempts=_SDK_ATTEMPTS,
            error=brief(match.group("cause")),
            wait=match.group("wait"),
        )

The helper uses regular expression matching via _TENACITY_RETRY_RE to extract structured details from unstructured SDK logs. It transforms obscure transport logs into structured CLI notifications, informing users of transient network backoffs without interrupting node operations.

docs.title: _get_client()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _get_client():

Description: Lazily constructs and returns a singleton instance of google.genai.Client. Configures HttpOptions with the timeout from _timeout_ms() and registers automatic SDK retry attempts for HTTP status codes 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, and 504. Dynamically routes between Vertex AI and AI Studio based on the presence of GEMINI_PROJECT_ID.

Returns:

  • genai.Client: Configured Google GenAI client instance.

Raises:

  • ValueError: Raised if neither GEMINI_PROJECT_ID nor GEMINI_API_KEY is present in the environment.

Example:

def _get_client():
    global _client
    if _client is None:
        http_options = types.HttpOptions(
            timeout=_timeout_ms(),  # milliseconds; with no timeout a stalled connection hangs forever
            # SDK retries for transient errors (announced: _sdk_retry_record); PocketFlow node retries (5 x 20 s) sit on top.
            retry_options=types.HttpRetryOptions(attempts=_SDK_ATTEMPTS, http_status_codes=[408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504]),
        )
        open_sdk_logger("google_genai._api_client", logging.INFO, _sdk_retry_record)
        if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
            _client = genai.Client(vertexai=True, project=os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"), location=gemini_location(), http_options=http_options)
        elif os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"):
            # vertexai=False explicitly: GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=true in the environment would otherwise
            # route the API key to Vertex AI.
            _client = genai.Client(vertexai=False, api_key=os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"), http_options=http_options)
        else:
            raise ValueError("Either GEMINI_PROJECT_ID or GEMINI_API_KEY must be set in the environment")
    return _client

When authenticating via GEMINI_API_KEY, the client explicitly sets vertexai=False. This prevents ambient environment variables like GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=true from misrouting consumer API keys to Google Cloud Vertex endpoints.

docs.title: _thinking_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _thinking_config(model: str, level: str | None):

Description: Translates an abstract thinking level into a concrete types.ThinkingConfig instance and descriptive telemetry string. Respects model-specific reasoning modes ("level" vs "budget" vs "none"), clamps requested levels to allowed boundaries, and requests thought summaries only when debug mode is enabled.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The normalized model identifier.
  • level (str | None): The requested thinking effort level or budget string.

Returns:

  • tuple[types.ThinkingConfig | None, str]: A tuple containing the initialized configuration (or None) and a telemetry description string.

Example:

def _thinking_config(model: str, level: str | None):
    """(ThinkingConfig | None, description). Never mixes thinking_level with thinking_budget."""
    mode, spec = gemini_thinking_mode(model)
    include = True if is_debug() else None  # thought summaries only for the debug log
    if model in _thinking_rejected:
        return None, "default (thinking config rejected by model)"
    if not level:
        # Model default thinking; with --debug still ask for summaries so they can be logged.
        return (types.ThinkingConfig(include_thoughts=True) if include and mode != "none" else None), "default"
    if mode == "level":
        effective = clamp_level(level.lower(), spec) or spec[-1]
        if effective != level.lower() and warn_once("gemini_level", model, level):
            emit("WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_CLAMPED", level=level, effective=effective, model=model)
        return types.ThinkingConfig(thinking_level=effective, include_thoughts=include), f"thinking_level={effective}"
    if mode == "budget":
        low, high, _can_disable = spec
        budget = min(max(GEMINI_THINKING_BUDGETS.get(level.lower(), 4096), low), high)
        return types.ThinkingConfig(thinking_budget=budget, include_thoughts=include), f"thinking_budget={budget}"
    if warn_once("gemini_no_thinking", model):
        emit("WARN_THINKING_NOT_SUPPORTED", model=model)
    return None, "unsupported"

The function guarantees that thinking_level and thinking_budget are never combined in the same configuration, preventing HTTP 400 parameter rejections. If the model was previously flagged in _thinking_rejected, it returns None immediately to suppress reasoning parameters.

docs.title: _max_output_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _max_output_tokens(model: str, level: str | None) -> int:

Description: Computes the output token reservation ceiling for a given model and thinking effort level. Uses get_model_limits() to identify the hard output limit and delegates to gemini_output_budget() to scale the token reserve.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The normalized model identifier.
  • level (str | None): The requested reasoning effort level.

Returns:

  • int: Maximum tokens allowed for generation.

Example:

def _max_output_tokens(model: str, level: str | None) -> int:
    """Per-level budget capped by the model's output limit. Gemini documents separate input and
    output limits, so output is not reduced for large prompts (input_token_budget still reserves it)."""
    _input_limit, output_limit = get_model_limits(model)
    return gemini_output_budget(level, output_limit)

Because Gemini maintains separate, unshared ceilings for input context and output generation, output token reservations are not curtailed for large prompts. This guarantees sufficient token budget for reasoning traces.

docs.title: _name()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _name(value) -> str:

Description: Normalizes API enum objects or string representations into an uppercase name string. Resolves SDK enum objects that may arrive as dynamic structures across library versions.

Parameters:

  • value (Any): An enum instance, string, or object representing a finish or block reason.

Returns:

  • str: The upper-cased string identifier (e.g., "SAFETY", "MAX_TOKENS").

Example:

def _name(value) -> str:
    """Enum → 'NAME' (unknown enum members arrive as dynamic values; compare by name)."""
    return (getattr(value, "name", None) or str(value or "")).split(".")[-1].upper()

The implementation inspects the .name attribute before falling back to string conversion. It splits compound strings by dot notation and extracts the final segment to normalize nested enum types like Candidate.FinishReason.MAX_TOKENS.

docs.title: _price()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _price(model: str, prompt_tokens: int, cached: int, output_tokens: int, today: datetime.date | None = None) -> float | None:

Description: Calculates the estimated cost of an inference call in US dollars based on published per-million-token rate cards. Evaluates prefix matches against _PRICING, applies temporary introductory pricing from _INTRO_PRICING when eligible, switches to tiered long-context pricing (>200K tokens) when applicable, and applies a 10% uplift for regional Vertex AI deployments.

Parameters:

  • model (str): Normalized model name.
  • prompt_tokens (int): Total prompt tokens (including cached tokens).
  • cached (int): Subset of prompt tokens retrieved from context cache.
  • output_tokens (int): Generated tokens (including thought tokens).
  • today (datetime.date | None, optional): Override date for promotional price verification. Defaults to datetime.date.today().

Returns:

  • float | None: Total cost in USD, or None if the model has no pricing entry.

Example:

def _price(model: str, prompt_tokens: int, cached: int, output_tokens: int, today: datetime.date | None = None) -> float | None:
    key = next((k for k in sorted(_PRICING, key=len, reverse=True) if model.lower().startswith(k)), None)
    if key is None:
        return None
    row = _PRICING[key]
    if key in _INTRO_PRICING and (today or datetime.date.today()) <= _INTRO_PRICING_UNTIL:
        row = _INTRO_PRICING[key]
    p_in, p_out, p_cache = row[3:6] if len(row) == 6 and prompt_tokens > _LONG_CONTEXT_THRESHOLD else row[:3]
    uncached = max(prompt_tokens - cached, 0)
    cost = (uncached * p_in + cached * p_cache + output_tokens * p_out) / 1_000_000
    if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID") and gemini_location().lower() != "global":
        cost *= _REGIONAL_UPLIFT
    return cost

The function matches model names by longest prefix to prevent generic identifiers from masking specialized variants (e.g., matching "gemini-3.8-flash-cyber" before "gemini-3.8-flash"). Uncached input tokens are separated from cached tokens so that discounted cache-read rates are applied accurately.

docs.title: _record()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _record(model: str, usage, raw_prompt_tokens: int, level_desc: str, finish: str, elapsed: float) -> None:

Description: Extracts token usage metrics from the SDK's usage_metadata, records metrics in the global ledger via record_usage(), calibrates prompt tokenizer ratios via observe_prompt_tokens(), and emits structured usage logs to console and log sinks.

Parameters:

  • model (str): Model identifier.
  • usage (types.GenerateContentResponseUsageMetadata): Usage metadata object returned by the Gemini API.
  • raw_prompt_tokens (int): Estimated prompt tokens calculated locally before the call.
  • level_desc (str): Human-readable thinking level description.
  • finish (str): Candidate finish reason.
  • elapsed (float): Execution duration in seconds.

Example:

def _record(model: str, usage, raw_prompt_tokens: int, level_desc: str, finish: str, elapsed: float) -> None:
    prompt = getattr(usage, "prompt_token_count", 0) or 0
    candidates = getattr(usage, "candidates_token_count", 0) or 0
    thoughts = getattr(usage, "thoughts_token_count", 0) or 0
    cached = getattr(usage, "cached_content_token_count", 0) or 0
    output = candidates + thoughts  # thinking is billed as output
    cost = _price(model, prompt, cached, output)
    record_usage("GEMINI", model, input_tokens=prompt, output_tokens=output, thinking_tokens=thoughts, cache_read=cached, cost=cost)
    ratio = prompt / raw_prompt_tokens if raw_prompt_tokens else 0.0
    from utils.token_utils import observe_prompt_tokens

    observe_prompt_tokens("GEMINI", model, raw_prompt_tokens, prompt)  # prompt_token_count includes cached tokens
    emit_raw(
        "DEBUG",
        f"GEMINI USAGE | model={model} | {level_desc} | finish={finish or 'n/a'} | in={prompt:,} | out={candidates:,} | thinking={thoughts:,} | "
        f"cached={cached:,} | est_cost={'$' + format(cost, '.4f') if cost is not None else 'n/a'} | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s | observed_token_ratio={ratio:.2f}",
        dest="BOTH",
    )

The helper accounts for thinking tokens under total output, matching Google's billing architecture where generated thoughts are billed at candidate token rates. It lazily imports observe_prompt_tokens() to avoid circular dependencies with utils.token_utils.

docs.title: _stream()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _stream(model: str, prompt: str, config) -> dict:

Description: Consumes the generator returned by client.models.generate_content_stream(). Assembles chunk parts, segregating thought summaries from completion text, and extracts finish reasons, block reasons, and usage metadata.

Parameters:

  • model (str): Model identifier.
  • prompt (str): Prompt string.
  • config (types.GenerateContentConfig): Fully populated generation configuration.

Returns:

  • dict: Stream extraction payload containing aggregated strings, reasons, and metadata.

Example:

def _stream(model: str, prompt: str, config) -> dict:
    """Consume generate_content_stream; returns text, thoughts, finish, block_reason, usage."""
    global _sdk_retries
    text, thoughts = [], []
    finish, block_reason, usage = "", "", None
    _sdk_retries = 0  # _sdk_retry_record counts this request's retries
    for chunk in _get_client().models.generate_content_stream(model=model, contents=[prompt], config=config):
        feedback = getattr(chunk, "prompt_feedback", None)
        if feedback is not None and getattr(feedback, "block_reason", None):
            block_reason = _name(feedback.block_reason)
        if getattr(chunk, "usage_metadata", None) is not None:
            usage = chunk.usage_metadata
        for candidate in getattr(chunk, "candidates", None) or []:
            if getattr(candidate, "finish_reason", None):
                finish = _name(candidate.finish_reason)
            content = getattr(candidate, "content", None)
            for part in (getattr(content, "parts", None) or []) if content is not None else []:
                if getattr(part, "text", None):
                    (thoughts if getattr(part, "thought", False) else text).append(part.text)
            break  # candidate_count is 1
    return {"text": "".join(text), "thoughts": "".join(thoughts), "finish": finish, "block_reason": block_reason, "usage": usage}

The generator iterates through incoming chunks, resetting _sdk_retries at the start of each request. It inspects candidate parts, routing content tagged with part.thought == True to the thoughts buffer and standard text to the output text buffer.

docs.title: Stream Extraction Payload
docs.text:
The dictionary returned by the internal _stream() helper contains the parsed components of the response stream.

Field Type Description text str Complete aggregated completion text generated across all candidates. thoughts str Aggregated reasoning thoughts captured when include_thoughts is enabled. finish str Normalized candidate finish reason (e.g., "STOP", "MAX_TOKENS", "SAFETY"). block_reason str Normalized prompt block reason from prompt_feedback (e.g., "PROHIBITED_CONTENT"). usage types.GenerateContentResponseUsageMetadata \| None Google GenAI SDK token usage object, or None if the stream omitted metadata.

docs.title: Module Constants
docs.text:
The module declares internal lookup tables and sets to govern pricing, retries, and finish reason categorization.

Constant Type Description _RETRYABLE_FINISH_REASONS set[str] Candidate finish reasons ({"SAFETY", "RECITATION", "LANGUAGE", "OTHER"}) that may pass upon resampling. _BLOCK_FINISH_REASONS set[str] Union of retryable finish reasons and deterministic prompt blocks ({"PROHIBITED_CONTENT", "BLOCKLIST", ...}). _TRUNCATION_FINISH_REASONS set[str] Set containing finish reasons indicating output token exhaustion ({"MAX_TOKENS"}). _PRICING dict[str, tuple[float, ...]] Standard rates in USD per million tokens: (input, output, cached [, long_input, long_output, long_cached]). _INTRO_PRICING dict[str, tuple[float, float, float]] Promotional rates for Gemini 3.6-3.8 Flash through December 31, 2026. _INTRO_PRICING_UNTIL datetime.date Expiration date for introductory pricing (datetime.date(2026, 12, 31)). _REGIONAL_UPLIFT float Multiplier (1.10) applied to base pricing for Vertex AI regional deployments. _LONG_CONTEXT_THRESHOLD int Token threshold (200_000) triggering long-context pricing rates. _SDK_ATTEMPTS int Maximum internal retry attempts (2) executed by HttpRetryOptions for transient errors. _TENACITY_RETRY_RE re.Pattern Compiled regex parsing wait durations and exception causes from tenacity retry logs.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text: The module maps error states into structured exceptions and signals to maintain resilience across pipelines:

docs.title: Thinking Parameter Rejection Recovery
docs.text:
Certain experimental or unmapped Gemini models reject explicit reasoning configurations with an HTTP 400 ClientError. The module catches this condition dynamically in call_gemini():

    except genai_errors.ClientError as e:
        # A model that rejects our thinking control (unknown future model, level set changed):
        # warn once and resend without it for the rest of the run.
        if getattr(e, "code", None) == 400 and thinking is not None and "think" in str(e).lower():
            _thinking_rejected.add(model)
            emit("WARN_GEMINI_THINKING_REJECTED", model=model, error=str(e)[:200])
            config = types.GenerateContentConfig(max_output_tokens=max_output, thinking_config=None, automatic_function_calling=no_afc)
            result = _stream(model, prompt, config)
        else:
            raise

When this error occurs, the model identifier is added to _thinking_rejected. The request is re-executed without ThinkingConfig, and subsequent calls for that model skip thinking configurations automatically.

docs.title: Policy Blocks vs. Sample Refusals
docs.text:
Finish reasons and prompt feedback block reasons are evaluated to determine whether an error can be retried:

    if result["block_reason"] or result["finish"] in _BLOCK_FINISH_REASONS:
        category = result["block_reason"] or result["finish"]
        # A blocked prompt repeats for the same input; a stop on the candidate may pass on resampling.
        retryable = not result["block_reason"] and result["finish"] in _RETRYABLE_FINISH_REASONS
        count_event("GEMINI", "refusals")
        emit("WARN_LLM_BLOCKED_RETRYABLE" if retryable else "WARN_LLM_REFUSAL", provider="Gemini", model=model, category=category)
        raise LLMRefusalError(model, category, provider="GEMINI", retryable=retryable)

If block_reason is set, the prompt itself triggered an unretryable block (such as PROHIBITED_CONTENT or BLOCKLIST), setting retryable=False to halt caller retries. If the refusal occurred on the generated candidate (such as SAFETY or RECITATION), retryable is set to True, allowing caller retry loops to resample with a different seed.

docs.title: Truncation Handling
docs.text:
When generation stops due to output token constraints (finish == "MAX_TOKENS"), returning raw strings would risk saving cut-off responses into persistent caches. The module intercepts this condition:

    if result["finish"] in _TRUNCATION_FINISH_REASONS:
        count_event("GEMINI", "truncations")
        emit("WARN_LLM_TRUNCATED", provider="Gemini", max_tokens=f"{max_output:,}")
        return TruncatedResponse(result["text"])

Wrapping the result in TruncatedResponse signals to upstream cache orchestrators (such as utils.call_llm) that the output was truncated and must not be committed to disk.

docs.text:

  • utils/token_utils.py — handles pre-request token estimations (count_tokens_raw) and runtime ratio calibration (observe_prompt_tokens) using observed API counts.

docs.title: llm_openrouter.py
docs.text: Source: utils/llm_openrouter.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
llm_openrouter.py implements the OpenRouter provider adapter for the call_llm dispatch layer in the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder architecture. It exposes an OpenAI-compatible chat completion client driven entirely by dynamic metadata retrieved from OpenRouter's remote model catalog (utils/llm_config.openrouter_model_info). By delegating model capabilities, context windows, parameter limits, and reasoning constraints to catalog inspection, the module natively supports diverse upstream model families (such as Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Qwen, and DeepSeek) without relying on brittle, hardcoded per-model logic within the adapter itself.

The module operates over persistent HTTP streaming connections utilizing Server-Sent Events (SSE) via the requests library. Streaming execution prevents client-side read and gateway timeouts during long generation cycles and deep reasoning runs that may span several minutes. Incoming event streams are decoded line by line as raw bytes rather than standard Unicode string splits to prevent corrupted parsing when multi-byte sequences or raw Unicode line breaks (U+2028, U+0085) appear inside JSON payloads. Keep-alive SSE comment events (: OPENROUTER PROCESSING) are discarded automatically during iteration.

Resilience is built directly into the transport and parsing layers. Network disconnections and transient HTTP response codes (408, 429, 502, 503, 524, 529) trigger bounded exponential backoff retries respecting upstream Retry-After headers. Non-transient status codes and upstream moderation stops are categorized into deterministic refusals or retryable policy filters, raising structured LLMRefusalError exceptions to halt or redirect pipeline nodes. Responses that exhaust output token capacities are encapsulated in TruncatedResponse instances to prevent incomplete generations from entering downstream disk caches, while full token, cache, and cost metrics are recorded to the system ledger.

# Extracted from utils/llm_openrouter.py: call_openrouter()
