docs.title: build_payload()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def build_payload(prompt: str, model: str, level: str | None, prompt_tokens: int) -> tuple[dict, str]:

Description: Assembles the complete OpenAI-compatible JSON dictionary payload for an OpenRouter chat completion request, returning both the payload dictionary and a diagnostic human-readable description of the reasoning configuration.

Parameters:

  • prompt (str): The raw text prompt submitted to the model.
  • model (str): The target model identifier.
  • level (str | None): The requested abstract thinking/reasoning effort level (e.g., "low", "medium", "high"), or None.
  • prompt_tokens (int): Estimated prompt token count used to compute available context headroom.

Returns:

  • tuple[dict, str]: A 2-tuple containing:
    1. dict: The serialized JSON request payload containing model, messages, stream: True, and conditional fields (max_tokens, reasoning, temperature).
    2. str: A short human-readable string summarizing the reasoning parameters (e.g., "effort=medium" or "unsupported").

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_openrouter.py: build_payload() implementation
info = openrouter_model_info(model)
max_tokens = _max_tokens(model, info, level, prompt_tokens)
reasoning, desc = _reasoning(model, info, level, max_tokens)
payload = {
    "model": model,
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
    "stream": True,
}
if max_tokens:
    payload["max_tokens"] = max_tokens
if reasoning is not None:
    payload["reasoning"] = reasoning
if _sends_temperature(model, info, reasoning):
    try:
        payload["temperature"] = float(os.getenv("OPENROUTER_TEMPERATURE", "0.7"))
    except ValueError:
        payload["temperature"] = 0.7

build_payload() serves as the central serialization pipeline for OpenRouter requests. It queries openrouter_model_info(model) to retrieve upstream architectural capabilities, calculates the safe max_tokens reserve via _max_tokens(), constructs reasoning constraints via _reasoning(), and determines temperature inclusion via _sends_temperature(). All requests enforce stream: True to ensure completions are returned through Server-Sent Events.

docs.title: call_openrouter()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def call_openrouter(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Orchestrates the full lifecycle of an OpenRouter model invocation. This includes pre-call token estimation, payload serialization, HTTP dispatch with bounded retries, SSE stream consumption, telemetry recording, and finish reason evaluation.

Parameters:

  • prompt (str): The user or system prompt to send for completion.
  • thinking_level (str | None, optional): Desired reasoning effort level (e.g., "low", "medium", "high"). Defaults to None.

Returns:

  • str: The generated completion text. If the generation was halted due to context length limits, an instance of TruncatedResponse (a str subclass) is returned.

Raises:

  • ValueError: If the OPENROUTER_MODEL environment variable is not set.
  • RuntimeError: If the request fails after all retry attempts, if an SSE stream drops mid-generation without a finish reason, or if the stream yields an upstream error.
  • LLMRefusalError: If the model or OpenRouter content filters reject the prompt.

docs.title: Phase 1: Request Assembly and Validation
docs.text:
model = get_model()
if not model:
    raise ValueError("OPENROUTER_MODEL environment variable is required")
api_key = os.getenv("OPENROUTER_API_KEY", "").strip()
raw_tokens = count_tokens_raw(prompt)  # memoized: the node already counted this prompt
payload, desc = build_payload(prompt, model, thinking_level, int(raw_tokens * token_ratio()))
headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json", **_attribution_headers()}
if api_key:
    headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {api_key}"
max_tokens = payload.get("max_tokens")
emit_raw(
    "DEBUG",
    f"OpenRouter request | model={model} | {desc} | max_tokens={f'{max_tokens:,}' if max_tokens else 'omitted'} | "
    f"temperature={payload.get('temperature', 'omitted')} | catalog={'yes' if openrouter_catalog() else 'no'} | "
    f"attribution={'on' if 'HTTP-Referer' in headers else 'off'}",
    dest="LOG",
)

In the first phase, call_openrouter() validates the presence of OPENROUTER_MODEL and loads credentials from OPENROUTER_API_KEY. Raw prompt tokens are obtained from count_tokens_raw() and scaled by token_ratio() to establish the prompt token baseline. The request dictionary is constructed using build_payload(), optional attribution headers are merged from _attribution_headers(), and debug telemetry is dispatched to log sinks.

docs.title: Phase 2: HTTP Execution and Stream Consumption
docs.text:
start = time.time()
resp = _post(f"{openrouter_base_url()}/v1/chat/completions", headers, payload)
generation_id = resp.headers.get("X-Generation-Id")
try:
    result = _consume(resp)
except Exception:
    # An error chunk mid-stream ("Upstream idle timeout exceeded") still was a request: unmeasured, like a
    # dropped stream, so a failed attempt and its retry both show in the usage ledger
    record_usage("OPENROUTER", model, cost=None, measured=False)
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"OPENROUTER USAGE | model={model} | stream error, no usage reported | generation_id={generation_id or 'n/a'}", dest="BOTH")
    raise
_record(model, result, raw_tokens, desc, time.time() - start, generation_id)
if is_debug() and result["reasoning"]:
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"REASONING:\n{result['reasoning']}", dest="LOG")

The second phase transmits the request via _post() to the completions endpoint resolved by openrouter_base_url(). The resulting streaming response is parsed by _consume(). If an exception occurs mid-stream (such as an idle timeout or dropped connection), the attempt is recorded in the global ledger as an unmeasured request via record_usage() before re-raising the error. Upon successful stream termination, _record() logs the billing and token metrics, and debug thinking traces are emitted if requested.

docs.title: Phase 3: Finish Reason Evaluation and Refusal Classification
docs.text:
finish, native = (result["finish"] or ""), (result["native"] or "")
if finish == "error":
    raise RuntimeError(f"OpenRouter generation ended with an error (native_finish_reason={native or 'n/a'})")
if finish == "content_filter" or result["refusal"] or native.lower() in _REFUSAL_NATIVE_REASONS:
    category = native or finish or "refusal"
    # Filters on sampled output (safety, recitation, content_filter) may pass on another attempt.
    retryable = not result["refusal"] and native.lower() not in _DETERMINISTIC_NATIVE_REASONS
    count_event("OPENROUTER", "refusals")
    emit("WARN_LLM_BLOCKED_RETRYABLE" if retryable else "WARN_LLM_REFUSAL", provider="OpenRouter", model=model, category=category)
    raise LLMRefusalError(model, category, provider="OPENROUTER", retryable=retryable)
if not finish:
    # No data at all, or the connection dropped mid-answer: never return a partial reply.
    raise RuntimeError(
        f"OpenRouter stream ended without a finish_reason after {result['events']} events ({len(result['text']):,} characters received)"
    )
if finish == "length":
    count_event("OPENROUTER", "truncations")
    emit("WARN_LLM_TRUNCATED", provider="OpenRouter", max_tokens=f"{max_tokens:,}" if max_tokens else "default")
    return TruncatedResponse(result["text"])
if not result["text"]:
    emit("LLM_EMPTY_REPLY", provider="OpenRouter", reason=finish or "n/a")
return result["text"]

The final phase examines the stream termination flags (finish and native). If an error is flagged, execution halts. Content filters, native provider refusals, or explicit refusal attributes raise LLMRefusalError, with retryable set to True for output-dependent filters (e.g., recitation or safety) and False for deterministic blocks. A missing finish reason raises a RuntimeError to prevent partial responses from being processed. If the response finished due to context length exhaustion (finish == "length"), the accumulated text is wrapped in a TruncatedResponse to prevent disk caching; otherwise, the raw decoded text is returned.

docs.title: _read_timeout()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _read_timeout() -> float:

Description: Determines the maximum permissible silence duration between Server-Sent Events chunks before timing out.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • float: The read timeout in seconds, bounded to a minimum of 30.0 seconds. Defaults to 300.0 seconds if OPENROUTER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS is unset or invalid.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_openrouter.py: _read_timeout()
try:
    return max(float(os.getenv("OPENROUTER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", "300")), 30.0)
except ValueError:
    return 300.0

_read_timeout() parses the OPENROUTER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS environment variable to configure the socket read timeout for HTTP streaming. Long reasoning models frequently pause for dozens of seconds between emitting thought tokens and final output; enforcing a strict lower floor of 30.0 seconds prevents aggressive socket drops during intense thinking phases.

docs.title: _reasoning()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _reasoning(model: str, info: dict | None, level: str | None, max_tokens: int | None = None) -> tuple[dict | None, str]:

Description: Constructs the OpenRouter-specific reasoning payload dictionary based on the requested thinking level, the catalog specifications for the model, and available output tokens.

Parameters:

  • model (str): Target model identifier.
  • info (dict | None): The catalog entry dictionary returned by openrouter_model_info(), or None if unavailable.
  • level (str | None): Desired reasoning level (e.g., "minimal", "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max").
  • max_tokens (int | None, optional): The allocated completion token budget. Defaults to None.

Returns:

  • tuple[dict | None, str]: A tuple containing:
    1. dict | None: The dictionary payload to send under the "reasoning" key in the API request, or None if reasoning is unsupported or unrequested.
    2. str: A human-readable description for telemetry and logging.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_openrouter.py: _reasoning()
if not level:
    return None, "default"
level = level.lower()
exclude = not is_debug()
if info is None:
    # Catalog unavailable or model unknown: send the level; OpenRouter clamps server-side.
    return {"effort": level, "exclude": exclude}, f"effort={level} (unverified)"
reasoning = info.get("reasoning")
if not isinstance(reasoning, dict) and "reasoning" not in (info.get("supported_parameters") or []):
    if warn_once("openrouter_no_reasoning", model):
        emit("WARN_THINKING_NOT_SUPPORTED", model=model)
    return None, "unsupported"
meta = reasoning if isinstance(reasoning, dict) else {}
if "supported_efforts" not in meta and meta.get("supports_max_tokens"):
    budget = _REASONING_BUDGETS.get(level, _REASONING_BUDGETS["medium"])
    if max_tokens:
        budget = max(min(budget, max_tokens - 1_024), 1_024)
    return {"max_tokens": budget, "exclude": exclude}, f"reasoning.max_tokens={budget}"
efforts = meta.get("supported_efforts")
effort = level
if efforts:
    effort = clamp_level(level, [e for e in efforts if e != "none"]) or level
    if effort != level and warn_once("openrouter_level", model, level):
        emit("WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_CLAMPED", level=level, effective=effort, model=model)
return {"effort": effort, "exclude": exclude}, f"effort={effort}"

_reasoning() inspects the model catalog to negotiate thinking parameters. If a model only accepts explicit token budgets rather than effort strings (indicated by supports_max_tokens), it maps the level to _REASONING_BUDGETS and clamps the budget to remain below max_tokens - 1024. For models supporting effort levels, it utilizes clamp_level() to ensure the effort tier is supported upstream (excluding "none" to prevent HTTP 400 errors on reasoning-mandatory models). In all cases, exclude: True is set unless debugging is enabled, preventing verbose thinking tokens from cluttering the final response payload.

docs.title: _sends_temperature()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _sends_temperature(model: str, info: dict | None, reasoning: dict | None) -> bool:

Description: Evaluates whether an explicit temperature parameter should be included in the API request payload.

Parameters:

  • model (str): Target model identifier.
  • info (dict | None): Catalog metadata for the model.
  • reasoning (dict | None): The constructed reasoning payload, or None.

Returns:

  • bool: True if temperature is supported and safe to send; otherwise False.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_openrouter.py: _sends_temperature()
if reasoning is not None or rejects_sampling_params(model):
    return False
if info is None:
    return True
if "temperature" not in (info.get("supported_parameters") or []):
    return False
meta = info.get("reasoning") if isinstance(info.get("reasoning"), dict) else {}
return not (meta.get("mandatory") or meta.get("default_enabled"))

Modern reasoning models (such as Claude 4.7+, Gemini 3.x, and o1/o3 architectures) reject sampling parameters when reasoning is enabled. _sends_temperature() checks if reasoning is active or if rejects_sampling_params(model) flags the family. If catalog info exists, it validates that "temperature" is listed under supported_parameters and verifies that reasoning is neither mandatory nor default-enabled for the target architecture.

docs.title: _max_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _max_tokens(model: str, info: dict | None, level: str | None, prompt_tokens: int) -> int | None:

Description: Calculates the upper limit of generation tokens allowed for the request, bounded by catalog context limits and prompt token consumption.

Parameters:

  • model (str): Target model identifier.
  • info (dict | None): Catalog metadata dictionary.
  • level (str | None): Requested reasoning effort level.
  • prompt_tokens (int): Count of prompt tokens.

Returns:

  • int | None: The clamped maximum token count, or None if the model is unknown and limits should be deferred to upstream defaults.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_openrouter.py: _max_tokens()
planned = openrouter_output_budget(model, level)
context = ((info or {}).get("top_provider") or {}).get("context_length") or (info or {}).get("context_length")
if planned and context:
    planned = min(planned, max(context - prompt_tokens - CONTEXT_MARGIN, 4_096))
return planned

_max_tokens() coordinates with openrouter_output_budget() to establish a base output ceiling for the model family and effort tier. If the catalog provides the model's total context_length, the planned output is clamped so that planned <= context - prompt_tokens - CONTEXT_MARGIN, while guaranteeing a minimum working window of 4,096 tokens. If the model is absent from the catalog, None is returned to allow OpenRouter and the upstream host to apply default limits.

docs.title: _attribution_headers()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _attribution_headers() -> dict:

Description: Builds optional HTTP headers to attribute API requests on OpenRouter's platform rankings and analytics.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • dict: A dictionary containing HTTP-Referer, X-OpenRouter-Title, and X-Title if OPENROUTER_APP_URL is set; otherwise, an empty dictionary.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_openrouter.py: _attribution_headers()
url = os.getenv("OPENROUTER_APP_URL", "").strip()
if not url:
    return {}
return {"HTTP-Referer": url, "X-OpenRouter-Title": _APP_TITLE, "X-Title": _APP_TITLE}  # X-Title: legacy name

OpenRouter provides public model ranking leaderboards and analytics boards that track consuming client applications. Attribution requires a referer URL; if OPENROUTER_APP_URL is configured, this helper generates both standard and legacy headers setting the application title to "Codebase Knowledge Builder".

docs.title: _retry_after()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _retry_after(resp) -> float | None:

Description: Safely parses the standard HTTP Retry-After header from an incoming response object.

Parameters:

  • resp (requests.Response): The HTTP response to inspect.

Returns:

  • float | None: The retry duration in seconds if present and parseable as a float, or None.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_openrouter.py: _retry_after()
value = resp.headers.get("Retry-After")
try:
    return float(value) if value else None
except ValueError:
    return None

When an endpoint returns rate-limiting status codes (such as HTTP 429), upstream proxies frequently provide explicit wait times in the Retry-After header. _retry_after() extracts this value, returning a numeric float or falling back to None if the header is missing or non-numeric.

docs.title: _error_body()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _error_body(resp) -> dict:

Description: Extracts and standardizes an error payload dictionary from an HTTP response.

Parameters:

  • resp (requests.Response): The response containing an error.

Returns:

  • dict: An error dictionary containing either the parsed JSON error body or a standardized {"message": str(err)} shape.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_openrouter.py: _error_body()
try:
    body = resp.json()
except ValueError:
    return {}
err = body.get("error", body) if isinstance(body, dict) else body
return err if isinstance(err, dict) else {"message": str(err)}

_error_body() unwraps nested JSON error responses returned by OpenRouter or upstream proxy hosts. If the response contains invalid JSON (e.g., HTML gateway error pages), it gracefully returns an empty dictionary. When valid JSON is present, it unwraps top-level "error" keys to normalize error structures across diverse upstream API formats.

docs.title: _error_detail()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _error_detail(resp) -> str:

Description: Generates a detailed, human-readable error string from an HTTP error response, including upstream provider metadata when present.

Parameters:

  • resp (requests.Response): The failed HTTP response.

Returns:

  • str: A formatted error string suitable for logging and exception messages.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_openrouter.py: _error_detail()
err = _error_body(resp)
if not err:
    return resp.text[:300].strip()
meta = err.get("metadata") or {}
raw = meta.get("raw") or meta.get("provider_name") or ""
return f"{err.get('message', err)}" + (f" ({raw})" if raw else "")

_error_detail() inspects the parsed error structure from _error_body(). If JSON parsing failed, it truncates the raw response body to 300 characters to prevent log flooding. When structured error metadata is available, it appends the underlying provider name or raw error text to the primary error message to aid debugging.

docs.title: _refusal_category()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _refusal_category(resp) -> str | None:

Description: Inspects an HTTP 403 response to identify whether it represents a moderation, guardrail, or content refusal.

Parameters:

  • resp (requests.Response): The HTTP response to evaluate.

Returns:

  • str | None: A normalized refusal category string (e.g., "content_policy_violation", "moderation"), or None if the status code is not 403 or the error is unrelated to content moderation.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_openrouter.py: _refusal_category()
if resp.status_code != 403:
    return None
err = _error_body(resp)
meta = err.get("metadata") or {}
kind = str(err.get("type") or err.get("error_type") or meta.get("error_type") or "").lower()
if kind in _REFUSAL_ERROR_TYPES:
    return kind
if meta.get("reasons") or meta.get("flagged_input"):
    reasons = meta.get("reasons") or ["moderation"]
    return ",".join(map(str, reasons)) if isinstance(reasons, list) else str(reasons)
return None

Upstream providers behind OpenRouter frequently intercept sensitive prompts before generation begins, returning HTTP 403 responses containing structured moderation metadata. _refusal_category() inspects the error payload for known refusal types (_REFUSAL_ERROR_TYPES) or metadata indicating flagged inputs, returning a descriptive refusal category that triggers LLMRefusalError rather than generic runtime exceptions.

docs.title: _post()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _post(url: str, headers: dict, payload: dict):

Description: Executes an HTTP POST request with streaming enabled, handling transient failures and rate limits via bounded exponential backoff retries.

Parameters:

  • url (str): The target endpoint URL.
  • headers (dict): HTTP request headers.
  • payload (dict): JSON payload dictionary.

Returns:

  • requests.Response: An open streaming HTTP response ready for SSE consumption.

Raises:

  • LLMRefusalError: If an HTTP 403 response indicates content moderation or policy refusal.
  • RuntimeError: If network connection errors, timeouts, or non-retryable 4xx/5xx responses persist across _MAX_ATTEMPTS.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_openrouter.py: _post()
for attempt in range(1, _MAX_ATTEMPTS + 1):
    try:
        resp = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload, stream=True, timeout=(15, _read_timeout()))
    except (requests.exceptions.ConnectionError, requests.exceptions.Timeout) as e:
        if attempt == _MAX_ATTEMPTS:
            raise RuntimeError(f"OpenRouter request failed after {attempt} attempts: {e}") from e
        emit("LLM_HTTP_RETRY", provider="OpenRouter", attempt=attempt, attempts=_MAX_ATTEMPTS, error=brief(e), wait=2**attempt)
        time.sleep(2**attempt)
        continue
    if resp.status_code in _RETRYABLE_STATUS and attempt < _MAX_ATTEMPTS:
        wait = min(_retry_after(resp) or 2**attempt * 2, 60)
        error = f"HTTP {resp.status_code}: {_error_detail(resp)}"
        emit("LLM_HTTP_RETRY", provider="OpenRouter", attempt=attempt, attempts=_MAX_ATTEMPTS, error=brief(error), wait=f"{wait:.0f}")
        resp.close()
        time.sleep(wait)
        continue
    if resp.status_code >= 400:
        detail, category = _error_detail(resp), _refusal_category(resp)
        resp.close()
        if category:
            model = payload.get("model", "")
            count_event("OPENROUTER", "refusals")
            emit("WARN_LLM_REFUSAL", provider="OpenRouter", model=model, category=category)
            emit_raw("WARNING", f"OpenRouter HTTP 403 refusal: {detail}", dest="LOG")
            raise LLMRefusalError(model, category, provider="OPENROUTER")
        raise RuntimeError(f"OpenRouter HTTP {resp.status_code}: {detail}")
    return resp
raise RuntimeError("OpenRouter request failed")  # unreachable

_post() wraps HTTP transport in an attempt loop bounded by _MAX_ATTEMPTS (3). Sockets enforce a connection timeout of 15 seconds and a read timeout determined by _read_timeout(). Network disconnections and retryable status codes (_RETRYABLE_STATUS) calculate wait times using exponential backoff or _retry_after(), capped at 60 seconds. Fatal HTTP errors are parsed for refusal classifications; if identified as a moderation rejection, an LLMRefusalError is raised immediately to halt redundant retries.

docs.title: _consume()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _consume(resp) -> dict:

Description: Parses the incoming HTTP response body into accumulated text, reasoning traces, finish reasons, and usage statistics, supporting both streaming SSE lines and single-chunk JSON responses.

Parameters:

  • resp (requests.Response): The open streaming HTTP response.

Returns:

  • dict: An accumulated result dictionary matching the Stream Aggregation Payload schema.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_openrouter.py: _consume()
out = {"text": [], "reasoning": [], "finish": None, "native": None, "refusal": None, "usage": None, "events": 0}
try:
    if "application/json" in (resp.headers.get("Content-Type") or "").lower():
        # An OpenAI-compatible proxy that ignores stream=true answers with one JSON body.
        _apply_chunk(out, resp.json())
    else:
        for raw_line in resp.iter_lines():
            line = raw_line.decode("utf-8", errors="replace") if isinstance(raw_line, bytes) else raw_line
            if not line or line.startswith(":") or not line.startswith("data:"):
                continue  # blank separators and ': OPENROUTER PROCESSING' keep-alives
            data = line[5:].strip()
            if data == "[DONE]":
                break
            try:
                chunk = json.loads(data)
            except ValueError:
                continue
            _apply_chunk(out, chunk)
finally:
    resp.close()
out["text"] = "".join(out["text"])
out["reasoning"] = "".join(out["reasoning"])
return out

_consume() handles the transport deserialization of streaming responses. Because certain proxies ignore stream=true and return single JSON bodies, it branches based on Content-Type. For SSE streams, it iterates over raw byte lines via iter_lines() to prevent Python's str.splitlines() from splitting on raw Unicode control characters (U+2028, U+0085). Comment lines prefixed with : (such as OpenRouter keep-alive pings) and empty delimiter lines are skipped, and JSON payload chunks are delegated to _apply_chunk().

docs.title: _apply_chunk()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _apply_chunk(out: dict, chunk: dict) -> None:

Description: Folds an individual SSE JSON chunk (or non-streamed completion response) into the in-progress stream accumulator dictionary.

Parameters:

  • out (dict): The accumulator dictionary created by _consume().
  • chunk (dict): A deserialized JSON chunk from the API response.

Returns:

  • None

Raises:

  • RuntimeError: If the chunk contains an top-level or choice-level error message.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_openrouter.py: _apply_chunk()
out["events"] += 1
if chunk.get("error"):
    err = chunk["error"]
    raise RuntimeError(f"OpenRouter stream error: {err.get('message', err) if isinstance(err, dict) else err}")
if chunk.get("usage"):
    out["usage"] = chunk["usage"]
for choice in chunk.get("choices") or []:
    delta = choice.get("delta") or choice.get("message") or {}
    if delta.get("content"):
        out["text"].append(delta["content"])
    if delta.get("reasoning"):
        out["reasoning"].append(delta["reasoning"])
    if delta.get("refusal"):
        out["refusal"] = delta["refusal"]
    if choice.get("finish_reason"):
        out["finish"] = choice["finish_reason"]
    if choice.get("native_finish_reason"):
        out["native"] = choice["native_finish_reason"]
    if choice.get("error"):
        err = choice["error"]
        raise RuntimeError(f"OpenRouter upstream error: {err.get('message', err) if isinstance(err, dict) else err}")

_apply_chunk() increments the event counter and checks for mid-stream error envelopes emitted by upstream providers or proxies. It extracts text deltas, reasoning strings, and refusal messages from choice.delta or choice.message. It also captures termination signals (finish_reason and native_finish_reason) and records the terminal usage dictionary emitted in the final chunk of the stream.

docs.title: _record()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _record(model: str, result: dict, raw_prompt_tokens: int, desc: str, elapsed: float, generation_id: str | None) -> None:

Description: Parses token accounting data from the consumed stream, computes financial costs (including Bring-Your-Own-Key upstream billing), updates the global usage ledger, and calibrates token estimation ratios.

Parameters:

  • model (str): Target model identifier.
  • result (dict): Accumulated result dictionary from _consume().
  • raw_prompt_tokens (int): Baseline prompt token count.
  • desc (str): Human-readable reasoning description.
  • elapsed (float): Total wall-clock execution time in seconds.
  • generation_id (str | None): The OpenRouter generation identifier (X-Generation-Id header).

Returns:

  • None

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_openrouter.py: _record()
if not result["usage"]:
    record_usage("OPENROUTER", model, cost=None, measured=False)
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"OPENROUTER USAGE | model={model} | no usage reported | generation_id={generation_id or 'n/a'}", dest="BOTH")
    return
usage = result["usage"]
prompt = usage.get("prompt_tokens") or 0
completion = usage.get("completion_tokens") or 0  # includes reasoning tokens
reasoning_tokens = (usage.get("completion_tokens_details") or {}).get("reasoning_tokens") or 0
details = usage.get("prompt_tokens_details") or {}
cached = details.get("cached_tokens") or 0
cache_write = details.get("cache_write_tokens") or 0
cost = usage.get("cost")
upstream = (usage.get("cost_details") or {}).get("upstream_inference_cost")
if usage.get("is_byok") and isinstance(upstream, int | float):
    # BYOK: `cost` is only OpenRouter's fee; the provider bills upstream_inference_cost to your key.
    cost = (cost if isinstance(cost, int | float) else 0.0) + upstream
record_usage(
    "OPENROUTER",
    model,
    input_tokens=prompt,
    output_tokens=completion,
    thinking_tokens=reasoning_tokens,
    cache_read=cached,
    cache_write=cache_write,
    cost=float(cost) if isinstance(cost, int | float) else None,
)
ratio = prompt / raw_prompt_tokens if raw_prompt_tokens else 0.0
from utils.token_utils import observe_prompt_tokens

observe_prompt_tokens("OPENROUTER", model, raw_prompt_tokens, prompt)

_record() handles the accounting lifecycle for OpenRouter completions. If an API proxy omits usage metadata, it records an unmeasured entry via record_usage(). When usage is available, it isolates standard completion tokens, reasoning tokens, prompt cache read/write tokens, and financial costs. For Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) configurations, it adds upstream_inference_cost to OpenRouter's routing fee to reflect the true financial cost. Finally, it passes the observed prompt token counts into observe_prompt_tokens() to dynamically calibrate the application's heuristic tokenizer ratio.

docs.title: Module Constants
docs.text:
The module defines constants governing network retries, refusal classification, thinking budgets, and tool identity.

Constant Name Type Value Description _RETRYABLE_STATUS set[int] {408, 429, 502, 503, 524, 529} HTTP response status codes that trigger automatic retry attempts. _MAX_ATTEMPTS int 3 Maximum number of HTTP request attempts per call. _REFUSAL_NATIVE_REASONS set[str] {"refusal", "safety", "prohibited_content", "recitation", "blocklist", "spii", "content_filter"} Upstream native stop reasons classified as content refusals. _DETERMINISTIC_NATIVE_REASONS set[str] {"refusal", "prohibited_content", "blocklist", "spii"} Native stop reasons that deterministically repeat for identical input. _REFUSAL_ERROR_TYPES set[str] {"refusal", "content_policy_violation", "moderation"} HTTP 403 error types that indicate guardrail or moderation stops. _REASONING_BUDGETS dict[str, int] See table below Token budgets for models supporting reasoning.max_tokens but no effort levels. _APP_TITLE str "Codebase Knowledge Builder" Application title header sent for attribution when OPENROUTER_APP_URL is set.

The _REASONING_BUDGETS dictionary maps abstract thinking levels to explicit token budgets:

Level Key Token Budget Description "minimal" 1,024 Minimal budget for fast sanity checks. "low" 2,048 Budget for light conceptual analysis. "medium" 8,192 Default working budget for reasoning passes. "high" 16,384 Deep reasoning budget for architecture analysis. "xhigh" 24,576 Extended reasoning budget for complex chapters. "max" 32,000 Absolute ceiling budget for exhaustive verification.

docs.title: OpenRouter Completion Request Payload
docs.text:
The dictionary shape produced by build_payload() and transmitted by _post() to /v1/chat/completions.

Field Type Description model str Target model identifier (e.g., "anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet"). messages list[dict[str, str]] List containing the single turn user message [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}]. stream bool Always set to True to enforce SSE streaming transport. max_tokens int (optional) Generation ceiling clamped to the model's remaining context window. reasoning dict (optional) Nested reasoning configuration ({"effort": str} or {"max_tokens": int}). temperature float (optional) Sampling temperature (defaults to 0.7); omitted when reasoning is active.

docs.title: Stream Aggregation Payload
docs.text:
The accumulator dictionary maintained by _consume() and updated by _apply_chunk().

Field Type Description text list[str] / str List of delta strings accumulated during streaming, joined into a final str. reasoning list[str] / str List of thinking delta strings accumulated during streaming, joined into a final str. finish str | None The standard finish reason reported by the top provider (e.g., "stop", "length"). native str | None The upstream vendor's raw native stop reason (e.g., "end_turn", "safety"). refusal str | None Model refusal string if explicitly emitted in the chunk deltas. usage dict | None Token usage metadata chunk, or None if unmeasured. events int Total count of SSE chunk events processed.

docs.title: Error Payload Schema
docs.text:
The normalized dictionary extracted by _error_body() from non-200 HTTP responses.

Field Type Description message str Human-readable error description returned by OpenRouter or the provider. type / error_type str (optional) Error classification type (e.g., "content_policy_violation"). metadata dict (optional) Extended metadata dictionary containing raw, provider_name, or reasons.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module provides defensive error classification and recovery routines across transport, parsing, and upstream provider boundaries:

  • HTTP Transport Retries: Network drops (ConnectionError), socket timeouts (Timeout), and transient HTTP status codes (408, 429, 502, 503, 524, 529) are caught within _post(). It performs up to 3 attempts with exponential backoff (2**attempt seconds). When an HTTP 429 response includes a valid Retry-After header, _retry_after() honors the server's requested delay up to a 60-second ceiling.
  • HTTP 403 Moderation Rejections: Upstream guardrails that reject prompts before generation begins are detected by _refusal_category(). Instead of raising a retryable network error, the response is categorized into an LLMRefusalError(retryable=False), logging the refusal event and aborting node retries immediately.
  • Stream Corruption and Disconnections: If an SSE connection drops mid-stream, _consume() exits its loop. In call_openrouter(), if finish is empty or missing, a RuntimeError is raised stating the number of events and characters received. Partial or fragmented responses are never returned.
  • Mid-Stream Provider Errors: When upstream providers fail during generation (e.g., idle timeouts), OpenRouter emits an SSE chunk with an error dictionary. _apply_chunk() detects this structure and raises a RuntimeError, causing the mid-stream attempt to be logged as unmeasured in record_usage() before escalating to the node retry runner.
  • Token Length Truncations: When generations terminate with finish == "length", the output is wrapped in a TruncatedResponse instance. This informs call_llm and downstream orchestrators that the completion was truncated, preventing the incomplete response from being written to the disk cache (llm_cache_v2.json).
  • Content Filter and Safety Stops: Terminations flagged with finish == "content_filter", an explicit refusal message, or native reasons matching _REFUSAL_NATIVE_REASONS raise LLMRefusalError. If the stop was caused by non-deterministic sampling filters (e.g., safety or recitation), retryable is set to True, permitting the caller to resubmit the prompt with alternative sampling seeds or lower temperatures.

docs.title: mkdocs.py
docs.text: Source: utils/mkdocs.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The mkdocs.py module serves as the centralized static documentation generation and artifact serialization engine for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder architecture. It consolidates site configuration generation, navigation assembly, architecture overview diagramming, cross-chapter link normalization, and output writing. Positioned at the culmination of the documentation pipeline, this module transforms synthesized chapter payloads, extracted code facts, and LLM-derived abstractions into production-ready MkDocs Material static documentation sites or self-contained standalone Markdown bundles.

The module operates across two distinct generation modes: --mkdocs site compilation and standalone Markdown assembly. For MkDocs generation, it crafts a full mkdocs.yml configuration configured with the Material theme, dark/light palette toggles, code copy buttons, search, and a pan-zoom extension tailored for interactive Mermaid diagrams. In api-reference mode, the module employs an LLM-assisted grouping workflow with deterministic fallbacks to cluster modules into logical reading-order tiers (types, setup, core, support, operational). It cross-references source-verified AST edges from facts.json to generate top-level architecture overview maps, complete module dependency graphs, and dedicated fan-in diagrams for shared architectural hubs.

To guarantee rendering fidelity and factual integrity across varied CommonMark parsers, mkdocs.py incorporates an automated, render-verified markup repair pipeline. This subsystem detects and repairs malformed Markdown constructs—such as tables or lists rendered as raw prose text due to missing boundary blank lines, or un-indented nested sub-lists—by running candidate transformations through an isolated Markdown rendering engine to ensure that visible text and code blocks remain invariant. Finally, the module performs case-safe stale file pruning via filesystem device and inode tracking, normalizes all internal cross-chapter hyperlinks relative to nested directory structures, and invokes deterministic quality-assurance auditing through chapter_check.py.

docs.title: yaml_str()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def yaml_str(value) -> str:

Description: Serializes any scalar value into a valid YAML string literal by leveraging json.dumps with ensure_ascii=False. Because JSON string literals represent valid YAML double-quoted scalars, this prevents structural corruption in generated YAML files (mkdocs.yml, nav_snippet.yml) when titles, labels, or paths contain special metacharacters such as colons, apostrophes, square brackets, quotes, or leading @ symbols.

Parameters:

  • value (Any): The scalar value to serialize as a YAML string.

Returns:

  • str: A double-quoted string literal safe for inclusion in YAML configurations.

Example:

# Quoting a navigation section title containing colons and brackets
label = yaml_str("Core [Service]: Accounting & Billing")
# Output: '"Core [Service]: Accounting & Billing"'

docs.title: build_mkdocs_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def build_mkdocs_config(site_name: str, nav_yaml: str, include_home: bool = True, lang_code: str = "") -> str:

Description: Programmatically constructs the complete mkdocs.yml configuration file for the static documentation build. Configures the Material theme, syntax highlighting through pymdownx.highlight, inline code highlighting (pymdownx.inlinehilite), and custom Mermaid diagram fences (pymdownx.superfences) emitting <div class="mermaid-raw"> to isolate diagrams from Material's CSS palette overrides. It sets up the panzoom plugin for interactive diagram zooming, registers dark and light theme toggles, injects localized UI settings, and integrates the compiled navigation hierarchy.

Parameters:

  • site_name (str): The display title of the static documentation site.
  • nav_yaml (str): Pre-formatted YAML lines containing the site navigation tree.
  • include_home (bool, optional): Whether to inject a Home entry pointing to index.md. Defaults to True.
  • lang_code (str, optional): Two-letter ISO language code for UI localization (e.g., "fr", "vi"). Defaults to "".

Returns:

  • str: The complete text content of mkdocs.yml.

Example:

config = build_mkdocs_config(
    site_name="My Project — API Reference",
    nav_yaml="nav:\n  - API:\n    - api/index.md\n",
    include_home=True,
    lang_code="vi"
)

docs.title: build_mermaid_init_js()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def build_mermaid_init_js() -> str:

Description: Returns the client-side JavaScript snippet responsible for initializing Mermaid diagrams inside the browser. Diagram containers are targeted via the custom .mermaid-raw selector to avoid conflicts with MkDocs Material's built-in styles. The script dynamically injects CSS to provide a light background card for diagrams when the slate (dark) color scheme is active, sets the initialization mode to startOnLoad: false, applies strict security isolation, and executes mermaid.run().

Returns:

  • str: The JavaScript code snippet stored in MERMAID_INIT_JS.

Example:

js_code = build_mermaid_init_js()
with open("docs/javascripts/mermaid-init.js", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write(js_code)

docs.title: site_renderer()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def site_renderer():

Description: Constructs an isolated, in-memory Markdown converter configured with the exact extensions and options specified in build_mkdocs_config(). It dynamically parses the local mkdocs.yml specification using PyYAML, resolving extensions such as toc, tables, fenced_code, and pymdownx.superfences (resolving the Python function pointer pymdownx.superfences.fence_div_format). Returns a closure render(text: str) -> str used during quality assurance and markup repair passes to ensure the verification engine reads and renders Markdown pages identically to the MkDocs build process.

Returns:

  • Callable[[str], str] | None: A single-argument callable converting Markdown strings to rendered HTML, or None if markdown or its extensions are not installed in the environment.

Example:

render = site_renderer()
if render:
    html = render("# Heading

| Col 1 | Col 2 |
|---|---|
| A | B |")

docs.title: build_chapter_filenames()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def build_chapter_filenames(chapter_order: list, abstractions: list, is_mkdocs: bool) -> dict:

Description: Computes deterministic filenames for all generated documentation chapters. For MkDocs builds where abstractions provide an original_path (such as in api-reference mode), the source path is mirrored with an appended .md extension; otherwise, sanitized lowercase names are used. For standalone output modes, chapters receive a zero-padded index prefix (01_name.md). To prevent accidental page collisions on case-insensitive filesystems or overwriting generated index pages, filenames are evaluated through case-folded keys, mapping directory-level readme.md files to index.md, and appending incrementing numeric suffixes (_2.md, _3.md) when collisions occur.

Parameters:

  • chapter_order (list): Ordered abstraction indices representing the sequence of chapters.
  • abstractions (list): List of abstraction metadata dictionaries containing name and path specifications.
  • is_mkdocs (bool): Flag indicating whether output targets an MkDocs site structure.

Returns:

  • dict[int, str]: Mapping of chapter position index to the resolved relative output filename.

Example:

filenames = build_chapter_filenames(
    chapter_order=[0, 1],
    abstractions=[
        {"name": "App Flow", "original_path": "flow.py"},
        {"name": "Nodes", "original_path": "nodes.py"}
    ],
    is_mkdocs=True
)
# Result: {0: 'flow.py.md', 1: 'nodes.py.md'}

docs.title: split_frontmatter()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def split_frontmatter(text: str) -> tuple[str, bool]:

Description: Inspects the start of a Markdown text document for a YAML frontmatter block enclosed between --- boundaries, matching the parsing logic employed by MkDocs. It verifies that the enclosed content safely deserializes into a YAML dictionary (mapping). If valid frontmatter is found, it strips the frontmatter block and returns the remaining body text; otherwise, the original text is preserved intact (protecting documents that open with horizontal markdown rules).

Parameters:

  • text (str): Raw Markdown file content.

Returns:

  • tuple[str, bool]: A 2-tuple (body, found), where body is the stripped text and found indicates whether valid frontmatter was detected and excised.

Example:

body, has_fm = split_frontmatter("---
title: Overview
---
# Content")
# Result: ("# Content", True)

docs.title: strip_summary_header()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def strip_summary_header(summary: str) -> str:

Description: Removes the standardized chapter heading line generated by upstream LLM synthesis passes (such as Chapter 1 — Core Routing: or <Chapter> 2 — Storage:) from the beginning of chapter summary text blocks.

Parameters:

  • summary (str): The raw chapter summary text.

Returns:

  • str: The summary text stripped of the leading header line.

Example:

cleaned = strip_summary_header("Chapter 1 — Ingestion:\nThis module ingests files.")
# Result: "This module ingests files."

docs.title: clip_sentences()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def clip_sentences(text: str, limit: int) -> str:

Description: Collapses internal whitespace and truncates prose text to a maximum character threshold while strictly preserving sentence boundaries. It iterates through extracted sentences, appending complete sentences until the limit is reached. If even the first sentence exceeds the specified character limit, the text is sliced cleanly at a preceding word boundary, trailing punctuation is stripped, unclosed code spans (backticks) are balanced, and an ellipsis (…) is appended.

Parameters:

  • text (str): Input text to truncate.
  • limit (int): Maximum allowable character count.

Returns:

  • str: Formatted, sentence-bounded text constrained within the specified character ceiling.

Example:

snippet = clip_sentences("First sentence. Second sentence goes here.", 20)
# Result: "First sentence."

docs.title: table_cell_text()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def table_cell_text(text: str) -> str:

Description: Sanitizes text strings for safe embedding inside Markdown table cells by escaping pipe characters (| to \|). The function parses the input for inline backtick code spans (_CODE_SPAN_RE), preserving pipes within code spans untouched (e.g., keeping type unions like str | None intact) while escaping pipes in regular prose.

Parameters:

  • text (str): Raw string intended for display inside a table cell.

Returns:

  • str: Pipe-escaped Markdown string.

Example:

cell = table_cell_text("Returns value | type `str | None`")
# Result: "Returns value \| type `str | None`"

docs.title: summary_description()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def summary_description(summary: str, limit: int = 300) -> str:

Description: Generates a clean, single-paragraph table cell description from a 4-point chapter summary brief. It strips introductory preambles and targets point (1) (typically "Component Scope & Responsibility"). It removes point markers (### (1), **1.**) and inline category labels, extracts the substantive text, enforces sentence clipping via clip_sentences(), and escapes pipes using table_cell_text().

Parameters:

  • summary (str): The multi-point chapter summary block.
  • limit (int, optional): Maximum character length. Defaults to 300.

Returns:

  • str: Sanitized table cell text derived from the summary's first core point.

Example:

desc = summary_description("### (1) Scope:\nHandles caching and network retries.")
# Result: "Handles caching and network retries."

docs.title: md_link_text()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def md_link_text(text: str) -> str:

Description: Escapes Markdown metacharacters (\, `, *, _, [, ], |) with backslashes so that raw source filenames or identifier names (such as __init__.py or [core]) render literally rather than triggering Markdown emphasis or link formatting.

Parameters:

  • text (str): The raw text to escape.

Returns:

  • str: Escaped Markdown string safe for hyperlink text labels.

Example:

safe_label = md_link_text("__init__.py")
# Result: "\_\_init\_\_.py"

docs.title: md_heading_text()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def md_heading_text(text: str) -> str:

Description: Prepares raw text for safe inclusion in Markdown headings. Applies md_link_text() and additionally escapes hash characters (# to \#), preventing trailing hash characters from being interpreted as closed CommonMark heading indicators when section names reflect directory paths (such as Samples/C#).

Parameters:

  • text (str): Raw heading title.

Returns:

  • str: Markdown-escaped heading string.

Example:

heading = md_heading_text("Framework/C#")
# Result: "Framework/C\\#"

docs.title: module_name_lookup()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def module_name_lookup(chapter_files: list) -> dict:

Description: Builds an exhaustive alias lookup dictionary that maps various naming conventions an LLM might emit for a module back to its canonical module_name. Maps the canonical name, the original_path, and the bare filename basename (provided that the basename is unique across the entire project).

Parameters:

  • chapter_files (list): List of chapter file dictionaries.

Returns:

  • dict[str, str]: Mapping of alternative names and path aliases to canonical module names.

Example:

lookup = module_name_lookup([
    {"module_name": "utils.call_llm", "original_path": "utils/call_llm.py"}
])
# Result: {"utils.call_llm": "utils.call_llm", "utils/call_llm.py": "utils.call_llm", "call_llm.py": "utils.call_llm"}

docs.title: grouping_extras()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def grouping_extras(parsed, chapter_files: list) -> tuple[dict, dict]:

Description: Extracts, validates, and normalizes optional descriptions and dependencies payloads returned by the group_modules.md LLM prompt. Resolves module aliases using module_name_lookup(), removes self-dependencies, eliminates duplicated edges, discards unknown modules, and cleanses description strings for table cells by clipping them to 400 characters.

Parameters:

  • parsed (Any): Deserialized JSON or dictionary payload returned by the grouping prompt.
  • chapter_files (list): List of active chapter file dictionaries.

Returns:

  • tuple[dict, dict]: A 2-tuple containing:
    1. descriptions (dict[str, str]): Cleaned one-line descriptions keyed by canonical module name.
    2. dependencies (dict[str, list[str]]): Dependency edges mapping source modules to target module lists.

Example:

descriptions, deps = grouping_extras(
    {"descriptions": {"call_llm.py": "Dispatches LLMs."}, "dependencies": {"call_llm.py": ["token_utils.py"]}},
    chapter_files
)

docs.title: modules_with_facts()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def modules_with_facts(module_facts: dict, chapter_files: list) -> set:

Description: Identifies all modules in the project for which fact extraction succeeded during upstream analysis passes (ExtractFacts). Returns a set of canonical module names whose fact records contain non-null claim sets, indicating that their dependency edges are verified by source code AST inspection.

Parameters:

  • module_facts (dict): Dictionary mapping file paths to extracted code fact records.
  • chapter_files (list): List of active chapter file dictionaries.

Returns:

  • set[str]: Set of module names with verified code facts.

Example:

verified_set = modules_with_facts(module_facts, chapter_files)

docs.title: verified_dependencies()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def verified_dependencies(module_facts: dict, chapter_files: list) -> dict:

Description: Extracts deterministic dependency edges directly from source-verified facts. It inspects the depends_on lists within module_facts, resolves target paths to canonical module names, filters out references outside the current chapter set, and removes self-references.

Parameters:

  • module_facts (dict): Fact database mapping file paths to extracted metadata.
  • chapter_files (list): List of active chapter file dictionaries.

Returns:

  • dict[str, list[str]]: Mapping from canonical source module names to lists of unique target module names.

Example:

deps = verified_dependencies(prep_res["module_facts"], chapter_files)

docs.title: build_section_map()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def build_section_map(sections: list, dependencies: dict, max_listed: int = 8) -> tuple[str, bool, bool]:

Description: Generates top-down (flowchart TD) Mermaid diagram source code representing the high-level architecture overview for api/index.md. Each top-level section is rendered as a single node enumerating its constituent modules (up to max_listed). Inter-section edges are drawn when any module in Section A depends on a module in Section B. Sections targeted by two or more incoming inter-section edges are designated as architectural hubs and assigned the entryNode CSS class.

Parameters:

  • sections (list): Hierarchical section tree dictionaries.
  • dependencies (dict): Dependency graph mapping source modules to target module lists.
  • max_listed (int, optional): Maximum module names displayed per section node before summarizing with an overflow count. Defaults to 8.

Returns:

  • tuple[str, bool, bool]: A 3-tuple (source, has_arrows, has_hubs):
    • source: The generated Mermaid diagram syntax (empty if fewer than 2 sections exist).
    • has_arrows: Boolean indicating whether cross-section dependencies exist.
    • has_hubs: Boolean indicating whether any section met the hub threshold.

Example:

mermaid_src, has_edges, has_hubs = build_section_map(sections, dependencies)

docs.title: build_module_graph()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def build_module_graph(sections: list, dependencies: dict, chapter_files: list) -> tuple[str, int]:

Description: Constructs a detailed left-to-right (flowchart LR) Mermaid diagram mapping individual module dependencies grouped inside subgraphs corresponding to top-level sections. To prevent visual chaos from high fan-in components (e.g., shared utilities or logging modules), modules with incoming dependencies exceeding a calculated threshold (max(5, total_modules // 4)) are designated as hub nodes. Hub nodes receive the entryNode styling class, display an annotated used by N modules badge, and have their incoming dependency arrows omitted from the main diagram to preserve layout readability.

Parameters:

  • sections (list): Hierarchical section tree dictionaries.
  • dependencies (dict): Dependency dictionary mapping source modules to target module lists.
  • chapter_files (list): List of active chapter file dictionaries.

Returns:

  • tuple[str, int]: A 2-tuple (source, hub_threshold):
    • source: Mermaid flowchart string (empty if dependencies are absent or module count exceeds 80).
    • hub_threshold: The integer threshold used to classify hub nodes (0 if no hubs were found).

Example:

graph_src, threshold = build_module_graph(sections, dependencies, chapter_files)

docs.title: build_hub_fan_ins()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def build_hub_fan_ins(sections: list, dependencies: dict, chapter_files: list, threshold: int) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:

Description: Generates dedicated, isolated left-to-right (flowchart LR) Mermaid diagrams for each hub module identified by build_module_graph(). For each hub, callers are aggregated by their parent navigation section. The resulting diagram displays one node per calling section containing a list of referencing modules, connected to the central hub node by an edge annotated with the caller count.

Parameters:

  • sections (list): Hierarchical section tree dictionaries.
  • dependencies (dict): Mapping of source module dependencies.
  • chapter_files (list): Active chapter file records.
  • threshold (int): Minimum incoming caller count that classified the module as a hub.

Returns:

  • list[tuple[str, str]]: List of (hub_module_name, mermaid_source) pairs sorted in descending order of caller volume.

Example:

fan_in_diagrams = build_hub_fan_ins(sections, dependencies, chapter_files, threshold=5)
for hub_name, diagram_source in fan_in_diagrams:
    print(f"Hub diagram for {hub_name}")

docs.title: build_grouped_nav()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def build_grouped_nav(sections: list, chapter_files: list, indent: int = 4) -> list[str]:

Description: Recursively constructs MkDocs navigation YAML lines from a structured section tree. It preserves hierarchical section nesting using the children key. Within each section, modules are automatically grouped into directory sub-layers based on their original_path directory while root-level files remain flat. File targets are formatted relative to the api/ directory.

Parameters:

  • sections (list): List of section dictionary definitions.
  • chapter_files (list): Active chapter file dictionaries.
  • indent (int, optional): Indentation space count for current nesting depth. Defaults to 4.

Returns:

  • list[str]: Formatted YAML lines representing the navigation hierarchy.

Example:

nav_lines = build_grouped_nav(sections, chapter_files, indent=4)

docs.title: collect_all_modules()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def collect_all_modules(sections: list) -> set:

Description: Recursively traverses a section hierarchy to collect every referenced canonical module name into a flat set.

Parameters:

  • sections (list): Hierarchical section tree.

Returns:

  • set[str]: A set containing all module names declared across all sections and sub-sections.

Example:

all_grouped = collect_all_modules(sections)

docs.title: prune_sections()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def prune_sections(sections: list, chapter_files: list) -> list:

Description: Cleanses raw section structures parsed from LLM grouping responses. Resolves module aliases via module_name_lookup(), removes unresolvable module names, recursively prunes child sections, and deletes empty sections or sections lacking a valid string name. This prevents mkdocs build from failing due to null navigation items (- "Name":).

Parameters:

  • sections (list): Raw list of section dictionaries from the LLM.
  • chapter_files (list): List of active chapter file dictionaries.

Returns:

  • list[dict]: Cleaned, validated section dictionaries.

Example:

clean_sections = prune_sections(raw_sections, chapter_files)

docs.title: tree_order_key()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def tree_order_key(chapter_file: dict) -> tuple:

Description: Provides a sort key tuple (dirname, basename) based on a chapter file's original_path. Used to arrange chapters in directory-tree order (root-level files first, followed by directories in alphabetical order).

Parameters:

  • chapter_file (dict): Chapter file dictionary containing an original_path entry.

Returns:

docs.title: GROUPING_WAIT
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: GROUPING_WAIT = 20

Description: Constant defining the wait interval in seconds between successive retry attempts when requesting module grouping.

docs.title: request_grouping()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def request_grouping(prompt: str, prep_res: dict, chapter_files: list) -> tuple[dict, list]:

Description: Dispatches the module grouping prompt to the LLM via call_llm(), executing an automated retry loop up to GROUPING_ATTEMPTS times with a GROUPING_WAIT sleep interval between attempts. The response cache is consulted exclusively on the first attempt. Responses are deserialized via parse_grouping_response() and sanitized with prune_sections(). Non-retryable safety refusals (LLMRefusalError with retryable=False) immediately abort the retry loop and re-raise the exception.

def request_grouping(prompt: str, prep_res: dict, chapter_files: list) -> tuple[dict, list]:
    use_cache = prep_res.get("use_cache", True)
    attempt = 1
    while True:
        try:
            response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=use_cache and attempt == 1, thinking_level=prep_res.get("thinking_level"), step="group_modules")
            parsed = parse_grouping_response(response)
            sections = parsed.get("sections", parsed) if isinstance(parsed, dict) else None
            # Drop unknown module names and the sections they leave empty (null nav entries break mkdocs build)
            sections = prune_sections(sections, chapter_files) if isinstance(sections, list) else []
            if not sections:
                raise ValueError(get("GROUP_NO_SECTIONS"))
            return (parsed if isinstance(parsed, dict) else {}), sections
        except LLMRefusalError as e:
            if not e.retryable:
                raise
            error = e
        except Exception as e:
            error = e
        if attempt == GROUPING_ATTEMPTS:
            raise error
        emit("GROUP_RETRY", attempt=attempt, attempts=GROUPING_ATTEMPTS, error=error, wait=GROUPING_WAIT)
        time.sleep(GROUPING_WAIT)
        attempt += 1

The function coordinates communication between the high-level MkDocs generation pipeline and the LLM inference provider. If the model fails to return valid sections or references unknown modules that get pruned entirely, it raises a ValueError with localized diagnostic text. Transient exceptions trigger diagnostic telemetry emission via emit("GROUP_RETRY") before sleeping. If all three attempts fail, the final recorded exception is re-raised to allow graceful fallback to directory-based sections.

Parameters:

  • prompt (str): Fully formatted prompt template populated with project metadata.
  • prep_res (dict): Pipeline preparation results containing cached configurations and thinking budgets.
  • chapter_files (list): Active chapter file dictionaries.

Returns:

  • tuple[dict, list]: A 2-tuple (parsed_payload, pruned_sections).

Raises:

  • LLMRefusalError: When the provider refuses the prompt with a non-retryable violation.
  • ValueError: When the LLM reply parses into empty or unresolvable sections.
  • Exception: Any network or provider-level exception that persists past maximum retries.

Example:

parsed, sections = request_grouping(group_prompt, prep_res, chapter_files)

docs.title: normalize_chapter_links()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def normalize_chapter_links(chapter_files):

Description: Deterministically post-processes and rewrites cross-chapter Markdown links ([text](target.md)) throughout all chapter contents. It compiles an authoritative filename lookup table, including unique basename aliases. For each link, it computes the exact relative path from the linking chapter's directory to the target chapter's directory, pinning targets with ./ when a relative path could collide with a root-level page.

def normalize_chapter_links(chapter_files):
    filenames = [cf["filename"] for cf in chapter_files]
    filename_lookup = {fname: fname for fname in filenames}
    basename_counts = Counter(fname.rsplit("/", 1)[-1] for fname in filenames)
    for fname in filenames:
        basename = fname.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
        if basename_counts[basename] == 1 and basename not in filename_lookup:
            filename_lookup[basename] = fname

    link_pattern = re.compile(r"\[([^\]]*)\]\(([^)#]+\.md)(#[^)]*)?\)")
    fixed_count = 0

    for cf in chapter_files:
        current_dir = os.path.dirname(cf["filename"])  # e.g. "CoreService"

        def fix_link(match, _dir=current_dir):
            nonlocal fixed_count
            text, target, anchor = match.group(1), match.group(2), match.group(3) or ""
            if target.startswith(("http://", "https://")):
                return match.group(0)
            canonical = filename_lookup.get(target)
            if not canonical:
                resolved = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(_dir, target)).replace("\\", "/")
                canonical = filename_lookup.get(resolved)
            if canonical:
                correct_rel = os.path.relpath(canonical, _dir).replace("\\", "/") if _dir else canonical
                if _dir and filename_lookup.get(correct_rel, canonical) != canonical:
                    correct_rel = f"./{correct_rel}"
                if correct_rel != target:
                    fixed_count += 1
                return f"[{text}]({correct_rel}{anchor})"
            return match.group(0)

        cf["content"] = link_pattern.sub(fix_link, cf["content"])

    if fixed_count:
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"LINK NORMALIZATION | fixed {fixed_count} cross-chapter links", dest="LOG")

The algorithm operates independently of chapter iteration order by indexing all known full paths before creating single-occurrence basename aliases. External URLs (http://, https://) and unresolvable targets are left unmodified. Fixed links that were altered are counted and reported to the debug logging sink via emit_raw().

Parameters:

  • chapter_files (list[dict]): List of chapter records whose "content" strings are mutated in-place.

Returns:

  • None: Modifies chapter dictionaries in-place.

Example:

normalize_chapter_links(chapter_files)

docs.title: repair_markup()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def repair_markup(markdown: str, render) -> tuple[str, Counter]:

Description: Evaluates and repairs CommonMark syntax defects that cause documentation sites to render structured blocks as plain text. It addresses tables and lists rendered as raw prose due to missing leading blank lines, and nested sub-lists whose indentation was flattened. The repair process is strictly guarded by the provided render closure: repairs are accepted only if the document's visible text characters and fenced code blocks remain completely invariant, and the HTML AST confirms that defect markers were resolved without modifying other valid markup structures.

docs.title: Phase 1: Diagnostic Scanning and Baseline Assessment
docs.text:
current = markdown
    for _round in range(5):  # re-indenting a nested list can show the level below it flattened
        if renders >= _REPAIR_RENDERS:
            break
        found = markup_problems(current, parse_page(current), render)
        pending = [(kind, finding) for kind in _REPAIRED_KINDS for finding in found[kind]]
        if not pending:
            break
        before = verdicts(current)
        renders += 1  # markup_problems above

The function initiates an iterative repair loop capped at 5 rounds and bounded by a maximum render ceiling (_REPAIR_RENDERS = 40). In each iteration, markup_problems() identifies defective line positions across three target classes: lists_as_text, tables_as_text, and lists_flattened. It records an initial baseline verdict using markup_verdicts() to establish structural parity constraints.

docs.title: Phase 2: Batch Speculative Repair
docs.text:
runs, kept = [], []
        lines = current.split("\n")
        for kind, finding in sorted(pending, key=lambda item: item[1]["line"]):
            index = finding["line"] - 1
            if kind == "lists_flattened":
                if any(start <= index < end for start, end in runs):
                    continue
                runs.append((index, _flattened_run(lines, index)))
            kept.append((kind, finding))
        kept.reverse()  # bottom-up, so the line numbers above stay valid while lines are inserted
        batch = lines
        for kind, finding in kept:
            batch = _repair(batch, kind, finding)
        after = improved("\n".join(batch), before)
        if after is not None:
            current = "\n".join(batch)
            continue

Findings are sorted and de-duplicated so that nested list items within an active run are not processed twice. The algorithm applies candidate line modifications from the bottom of the document upward, ensuring that line index insertions do not invalidate earlier offsets. It first attempts a speculative batch repair of all findings at once. The improved() closure evaluates the rendered output; if batch repair satisfies all invariance constraints, the modified text is accepted immediately.

docs.title: Phase 3: Incremental Repair and Counter Aggregation
docs.text:
progress = False
        for kind, finding in kept:
            if renders >= _REPAIR_RENDERS:
                break
            candidate = "\n".join(_repair(current.split("\n"), kind, finding))
            after = improved(candidate, before)
            if after is not None:
                current, before, progress = candidate, after, True
        if not progress:
            break
    if current == markdown:
        return markdown, Counter()
    start = markup_problems(markdown, parse_page(markdown), render)
    end = markup_problems(current, parse_page(current), render)
    return current, +Counter({kind: len(start[kind]) - len(end[kind]) for kind in _REPAIRED_KINDS})

If the batch repair fails invariant verification, the function falls back to testing candidate transformations individually. If a single change demonstrates verified progress without violating code or text invariance, it is committed to current. Once iterations terminate, the net reduction in detected markup defects is compiled into a Counter object and returned alongside the repaired Markdown text.

Parameters:

  • markdown (str): Raw Markdown content of a chapter.
  • render (Callable[[str], str]): The site renderer closure produced by site_renderer().

Returns:

  • tuple[str, Counter]: A 2-tuple containing the repaired Markdown string and a Counter reflecting fixed defect counts per category.

Example:

renderer = site_renderer()
if renderer:
    clean_md, stats = repair_markup(raw_content, renderer)

docs.title: Phase 1: Setup and Chapter Summary Preparation
docs.text:
project_name = prep_res["project_name"]

docs.text:

            if has_facts:
                dependencies = {source: targets for source, targets in replied.items() if source not in with_facts} | verified
                inferred_sources = sorted(source for source in dependencies if source not in with_facts)
            else:
                dependencies = replied

In api-reference mode with more than 5 modules, the function invokes the group_modules.md LLM prompt via request_grouping(). Extracted dependencies from verified facts override LLM inferences for verified modules. Sections are re-ordered into semantic roles via order_sections(), ungrouped modules are appended under an Other category, and navigation lines are compiled. If the grouping LLM call fails or times out, it logs an error and gracefully falls back to directory-based sections via directory_sections().

docs.title: Phase 6: Iterative Render-Verified Markup Repair
docs.text:
# --- Lists and tables the site would show as text, flattened nested lists: repaired, render-verified ---

        repaired = Counter()
        for chapter_info in chapter_files:

The site renderer closure is initialized via site_renderer(). If available, each chapter's Markdown content is processed through repair_markup(). Detected syntax anomalies (such as missing blank lines preceding lists or tables) are repaired, verified against the Markdown HTML renderer, and logged to telemetry sinks.

docs.text:
# --- Write chapter files ---

Finally, run_chapter_check() performs a non-LLM structural and factual validation pass over the written site files.

docs.title: _sentences()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _sentences(text: str):

Description: Generator yielding consecutive sentence substrings extracted from text. Leverages _SENTENCE_END_RE while bypassing terminal periods associated with known abbreviations via _ends_with_abbreviation().

def _sentences(text: str):
    start = 0
    for match in _SENTENCE_END_RE.finditer(text):
        piece = text[start : match.start()]
        if not piece or _ends_with_abbreviation(piece):
            continue
        yield piece
        start = match.end()
    if text[start:]:
        yield text[start:]

The generator iterates through sentence boundaries, checking whether the preceding substring terminates with a recognized abbreviation before yielding. Any trailing content following the last boundary match is yielded as the final sentence segment.

Parameters:

  • text (str): Raw input prose text.

Yields:

  • str: Individual sentence strings.

docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _flattened_run(lines: list[str], index: int) -> int:

Description: Scans forward through document lines starting at index to find the terminating boundary of a flattened nested list block. Returns the line index immediately following all items and indented paragraphs belonging to the run.

docs.title: _repair()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _repair(lines: list[str], kind: str, finding: dict) -> list[str]:

Description: Applies a specific formatting repair transformation to a list of lines. For lists_as_text or tables_as_text, it inserts a blank line (or blockquote marker >) preceding the element. For lists_flattened, it shifts the nested list block rightward by 4 spaces past its parent item, shifting enclosed fenced code blocks as intact units while leaving lines containing literal tabs untouched.

def _repair(lines: list[str], kind: str, finding: dict) -> list[str]:
    index = finding["line"] - 1
    if kind in ("lists_as_text", "tables_as_text"):
        if index == 0 or not lines[index - 1].strip():
            return lines
        quote = re.match(r"^(?: {0,3}> ?)+", lines[index])
        return [*lines[:index], quote.group(0).rstrip() if quote else "", *lines[index:]]
    indent = _indent_of(lines[index])
    parent = next((line for line in reversed(lines[:index]) if line.strip() and _indent_of(line) < indent), None)
    if parent is None or _indent_of(parent) + 4 <= indent:
        return lines
    end = _flattened_run(lines, index)
    if any("\t" in line[: len(line) - len(line.lstrip())] for line in lines[index:end]):
        return lines
    repaired = list(lines)
    levels = []
    fence = None
    for position in range(index, end):
        line = lines[position]
        if fence:
            if line.strip():
                repaired[position] = " " * fence[1] + line
            if fence[0].match(line):
                fence = None
            continue
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        old = _indent_of(line)
        item = _ITEM_START_RE.match(line.expandtabs(4))
        if item:
            while levels and old <= levels[-1][0]:
                levels.pop()
            new = levels[-1][1] + 4 if levels else _indent_of(parent) + 4
            spaces = len(item.group(3))
            levels.append((old, new, item.end(2) + (spaces if 1 <= spaces <= 4 else 1)))
            shift = new - old
        else:
            while levels and old < levels[-1][2]:
                levels.pop()
            shift = levels[-1][1] + 4 - levels[-1][2] if levels else 0
            opener = _FENCE_LINE_RE.match(line)
            if opener:
                fence = (re.compile(rf"^\s*{re.escape(opener.group(1)[0])}{{{len(opener.group(1))},}}\s*$"), max(shift, 0))
        if shift > 0:
            repaired[position] = " " * shift + line
    return repaired

This helper implements the core line-rewriting logic used by repair_markup(). When inserting blank lines before un-separated tables or lists, it preserves blockquote nesting depth by copying any leading quote markers (>). When re-indenting flattened lists, it maintains a tracking stack (levels) of active parent indentations, ensuring that multi-line list paragraphs and enclosed code fences receive matching visual indent shifts.

Parameters:

  • lines (list[str]): Target document split into lines.
  • kind (str): Defect classification string ("lists_as_text", "tables_as_text", or "lists_flattened").
  • finding (dict): Defect descriptor dictionary containing a 1-based "line" key.

Returns:

  • list[str]: A new list of lines with the repair applied.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
• LLM Refusal Interception: In request_grouping(), errors from call_llm() are inspected for LLMRefusalError. If an error is flagged as non-retryable (e.retryable is False), the retry loop is bypassed and the error re-raised immediately to prevent wasting API tokens on deterministic safety rejections.
  • Bounded Grouping Retries: The LLM grouping pipeline retries transient failures (such as network drops or unparsable model outputs) up to GROUPING_ATTEMPTS (3) times with a GROUPING_WAIT (20s) delay. If all attempts are exhausted or the returned sections contain no resolvable modules, request_grouping() raises a ValueError, prompting write_mkdocs_output() to log the traceback and fall back to directory-based sections.
  • Markup Repair Safety Invariants: The repair_markup() function guards all text transformations against corruption. A repair candidate is discarded if visible non-whitespace characters change (_visible()), if dedented code blocks change (_code_blocks()), if CommonMark token readings diverge, or if previously valid markup elements regress.
  • Case-Safe Pruning: Stale file pruning in prune_stale_pages() uses filesystem device and inode numbers (os.stat(path).st_dev, st_ino) rather than filename strings. This ensures that case-only file renames on case-insensitive filesystems (such as macOS or Windows) do not delete active files.
  • Defensive Frontmatter Parsing: split_frontmatter() wraps PyYAML execution in a general exception trap. Documents containing invalid YAML syntax or invalid dates (e.g., 2024-02-30) fall back gracefully to preserving the original text rather than raising runtime errors.
  • Missing Renderer Degradation: If markdown or its third-party extensions are missing, site_renderer() emits a CHAPTER_CHECK_NO_RENDERER telemetry event and returns None. Downstream processes check for None and skip markup repairs and rendered audits without crashing.
